quote: We find that sharing parameters among layers not only improves the parameter efficiency, but also acts as a form of regularization that stabilizes the training.

title: Deep Reinforcement Learning with Transformers for Text Adventure Games
claim: The weight-shared lightweight transformer encoder solves single games with fewer interactions and generalizes better to unseen games (sharing not isolated).
quote: The experimental results show that our proposed model not only solves single games with much fewer interactions, but also achieves better generalization on a set of unseen games.

title: DistilALHuBERT: A Distilled Parameter Sharing Audio Representation Model
claim: At the same parameter count, the recursive (shared-layer) student beats the unshared DistilHuBERT.
quote: Evaluation results on the S3PRL benchmark show that DistilALHuBERT can significantly outperform the DistilHuBERT model with the same number of parameters.

title: Implementasi Konsep Tiny Recursion Model Pada Kasus Klasifikasi
claim: A TRM with only thousands of parameters reaches competitive accuracy on small tabular datasets (no matched baseline stated).
quote: Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa TRM yang sangat efisien, dengan hanya ribuan parameter, berhasil mencapai akurasi pengujian yang kompetitif (hingga 97% untuk Iris, 94% untuk Breast Cancer, dan 78% untuk Diabetes).

title: Leveraging Adapter for Parameter-Efficient ASR Encoder
claim: Shared parameters plus adapters remove about half the parameters and 20% of compute without degrading recognition.
quote: Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed architecture reduces approximately 50% of parameters and 20% of computations without compromising speech recognition performance.

title: Recurrent Fine-Grained Self-Attention Network for Video Crowd Counting
claim: Recurrently feeding features through the same decoder reduces parameters and improves density-map quality.
quote: Moreover, the RFSNet recurrently feeds the features into the decoder to enhance the spatio-temporal representations. This strategy not only simplifies the model structure and reduces the number of parameters

title: ShareDAB-DETR: Memory-Efficient Object Detection through CentralBank Parameter Sharing
claim: Weight-table sharing retains 99% of DAB-DETR accuracy with up to 84% fewer transformer parameters.
quote: Applied to DAB-DETR, our approach achieves up to 84% reduction in trans-former parameters (19.67M to 3.21M) and 67% reduction in training memory while retaining 99% of baseline accuracy (41.8 vs 42.2 AP on COCO).

title: SkipFold: Test-Time Dynamic Depth for Scalable Biomolecular Inference
claim: Skipping early PairFormer blocks in later recycling iterations cuts block evaluations by 56% while keeping high agreement for medium and long proteins; short proteins lose more.
quote: the schedule (0,40,40,40) cuts PairFormer block evaluations from 212 to 92 (56%; a ~35% PairFormer-region wall-clock reduction over a torch.compile baseline, ~12% end-to-end on medium and long targets)

title: UT-ATD: Universal Transformer for Anomalous Trajectory Detection by Embedding Trajectory Information
claim: UT-based detector trains faster with relatively few parameters and achieves state-of-the-art performance in most aspects.
quote: UT-ATD has a faster training speed, relatively few model parameters, and sufﬁcient portability, which are ideal for the realistic scene requirements.

title: Depth as Time in One-Step Generative Models
claim: A single interval-conditioned shared block, applied as many times as the teacher has layers, recovers most of a MeanFlow teacher's quality at 8.2x / 16.6x fewer parameters.
quote: The compressed models reach FID-50k 15.6 and 11.7, which improve to 8.2 and 4.9 with FD-loss post-training (Yang et al., 2026), compared with 6.2 and 4.0 for the original models.

title: Depth as Time in One-Step Generative Models
claim: Time (interval) conditioning of the shared block is essential; removing it more than doubles FID on CIFAR-10.
quote: We ablate the effect of conditioning on the interval (τi , τi+1 ) in Appendix C.4 and show that on CIFAR-10, removing it from an otherwise identical weight-shared block more than doubles FID-50k.

title: Depth as Time in One-Step Generative Models
claim: Compressibility into a looped block depends on the training task: drifting models (no time-indexed transport) compress poorly.
quote: the drifting B/2 student reaches only FID-50k 47.09, about three times worse than the MeanFlow SiT-B/2 student (15.61) at a similar compression ratio, despite distilling from a stronger teacher (FID 1.75).

title: Iterate or Widen? When Test-Time Refinement Helps LiDAR Scene Completion: A Controlled Study of Evidence Geometry
claim: Iteration beats a parameter-matched wider model only for coherent missing regions; for independent thinning, augmentation helps far more than iteration.
quote: Under independent 75% thinning, iteration adds only 0.300 points [0.166, 0.436], whereas observation-family augmentation adds 5.975 points [5.662, 6.140]. Neither intervention repairs additive clutter.

title: Looped Diffusion Language Models
claim: At matched parameters and matched total training FLOPs, LoopMDM reaches the baseline's final test NLL with 3.34x, 2.95x and 2.34x fewer training FLOPs on LM1B, OWT and FineWeb-Edu.
quote: For S ≥ 6, LoopMDM consistently outperforms the MDM baseline across all three corpora, reaching the same final NLL with 3.34×, 2.95×, and 2.34× fewer training FLOPs, respectively.

title: Looped Diffusion Language Models
claim: Looping beats a deeper non-looped 21-layer MDM whose per-step training FLOPs match LoopMDM's on GSM8K, so gains are not explained by depth alone (note: at S=8/16 LoopMDM's inference depth exceeds 21 layers).
quote: More importantly, it outperforms a 21-layer baseline with comparable per-step FLOPs, achieving gains of +2.7 at S = 8 and +3.4 points at S = 16.

title: Looped Diffusion Language Models
claim: Where to loop matters: looping more than six layers underperforms the non-looped baseline at matched FLOPs; early-middle positions are best.
quote: In particular, looping more than six layers underperforms the baseline, indicating that simply applying looping to more layers does not lead to more effective use of training FLOPs.

title: Looped Diffusion Language Models
claim: Loop extrapolation: inference with S=24 (> Smax=12) keeps improving NLL; S=1 underperforms the baseline.
quote: At S = 24, beyond the training maximum Smax = 12, performance continues to improve, indicating that the learned operator generalizes beyond the training regime.

title: Looped Diffusion Language Models
claim: A hidden-state-change stopping rule reduces average loops from 12 to about 5 while preserving most gains.
quote: adaptive looping reduces the average loop count from S = 12 to roughly five iterations while preserving most of the performance gains across all evaluation settings.

title: bioMoR: Biology-Guided Mixture-of-Recursions for Effective Genomic Learning
claim: With effective depth aligned to the vanilla Transformer (K=4), bioMoR improves average macro-F1 by 8.2 points and balanced accuracy by 7.1 points over the best non-bioMoR baseline with 75% fewer parameters.
quote: To align effective depth with the base Transformer, denoted Vanilla, all recursive models in Table 1 use K=4. Both bioMoR routing variants outperform these baselines on average for both metrics.

title: bioMoR: Biology-Guided Mixture-of-Recursions for Effective Genomic Learning
claim: bioMoR keeps about 69-70% macro-F1 across recursion depths K=2..4 with fewer FLOPs than vanilla; at K=2 it uses 58% fewer FLOPs.
quote: bioMoR consistently maintains approximately 69– 70% macro-F1 across all recursion depths while requiring fewer FLOPs than Vanilla. At K=2, bioMoR uses 58% fewer FLOPs than Vanilla.

title: The Thinking Pixel: Recursive Sparse Reasoning in Multimodal Diffusion Latents
claim: On GenEval, recursion with modulation over multiple SD3 layers gives the best overall score (71.18) vs SD3-medium (67.93) and same-data LoRA SFT (69.55); both recursion and modulation contribute.
quote: The results show that both recursion and modulation contribute to the improvement of model performance. Targeting multiple layers of SD3 further enhances its benefits and achieves the best overall scores on the benchmark.

title: The Thinking Pixel: Recursive Sparse Reasoning in Multimodal Diffusion Latents
claim: On ImageNet 256 the method is competitive with DiT-XL/2 at the same reported size (FID 2.27 vs 2.34).
quote: framework achieves competitive performance with the baseline DiT-XL/2 model. DiffuSSM-XL achieved better sFID and precision scores.

title: LoopICL: Looping a single transformer block to solve tabular tasks
claim: Versus 6 stacked blocks matching the mean pretraining loop count, the looped model has higher in-distribution loss on synthetic priors but lower loss on real development tasks (better generalization).
quote: In contrast, the recurrent variants achieve lower loss on the development set tasks, indicating better generalization to unseen tasks.

title: LoopICL: Looping a single transformer block to solve tabular tasks
claim: Recurrence makes optimization harder (larger gradient norms); distributional conditioning stabilizes it.
quote: we observe that recurrent models are more challenging to train, exhibiting generally larger gradient norms.

title: LoopICL: Looping a single transformer block to solve tabular tasks
claim: At 12 loops LoopICL is competitive with TabICLv2 whose 12 blocks give the same dominant FLOPs, with 88.2% fewer parameters.
quote: TabICLv2 uses 12 ICL blocks and hidden dimensions of the same size as LoopICL, thus, the dominant FLOPs cost is the same

title: LoopICL: Looping a single transformer block to solve tabular tasks
claim: Loop extrapolation depends on residual scaling: alpha=1 degrades at high loop counts, while 1/L-type scaling extrapolates beyond the pretraining limit; the deployed model works at about twice the mean training loops.
quote: these results demonstrate that our model robustly extrapolates beyond its pretraining limit on real-world tasks and operates effectively at roughly twice the average number of loop steps observed during pretraining.

title: Thinking in Depth, Speaking Directly: Recurrent Latent Reasoning for Paralinguistically Grounded Spoken Dialogue
claim: Against CoT-SFT on the same base and data, LoopSLM gains over 20 points in reasoning accuracy with 64.5% fewer generated tokens.
quote: Relative to the matched Qwen2.5 CoT-SFT baseline, it gains over 20 percentage points in reasoning accuracy with 64.5% fewer generated tokens.

title: Thinking in Depth, Speaking Directly: Recurrent Latent Reasoning for Paralinguistically Grounded Spoken Dialogue
claim: At fixed executed depth, replacing passes with stock (untrained) blocks gives little benefit, while trained recurrent passes give progressively larger gains, so the benefit comes from the learned recurrent transform rather than extra layer evaluations.
quote: These results show that the benefit comes from the learned recurrent transformation rather than additional layer evaluations alone.

title: Thinking in Depth, Speaking Directly: Recurrent Latent Reasoning for Paralinguistically Grounded Spoken Dialogue
claim: More trained loops are not monotonically better: R=4 best; R=6 hurts reasoning and format adherence.
quote: Models trained at different recurrence depths show that the benefit is not monotonic (Table 2, bottom). R4 gives the strongest overall reasoning.

title: Thinking in Depth, Speaking Directly: Recurrent Latent Reasoning for Paralinguistically Grounded Spoken Dialogue
claim: Loop placement matters: looping L9-11 beats L15-17 on understanding and reasoning; L3-5 harms transcription.
quote: Looping L9–11 rather than L15–17 improves understanding and reasoning on EchoMind by 6.29 and 3.57 points, respectively, whereas L15–17 improves response style.

title: Parameter Efficient Multimodal Transformers for Video Representation Learning
claim: Cross-layer weight sharing does not hurt audio-visual classification performance (same depth, same data), confirming ALBERT's finding in the multimodal setting.
quote: The results show that sharing weights across layers does not hurt the performance, confirming the observations by Lan et al. (2020) in the audio-visual setting.

title: Parameter Efficient Multimodal Transformers for Video Representation Learning
claim: The combined sharing scheme reduces Transformer parameters by 97%.
quote: Our parameter reduction scheme reduces the number of parameters from 128M to 4M (by 97%) (Table 1 (c)).

title: LoopVLA: Learning Sufficiency in Recurrent Refinement for Vision-Language-Action Models
claim: With the same backbone and training, LoopOFT* (1.2B, all 8 loops) reaches 96.0% average LIBERO success vs 94.9% for the 2.2B full-depth Qwen3OFT at the same 0.53T FLOPs.
quote: LoopOFT* attains an average success rate of 96.0%, outperforming strong baselines such as π0 and Qwen3OFT, despite using fewer parameters.

title: LoopVLA: Learning Sufficiency in Recurrent Refinement for Vision-Language-Action Models
claim: At a fixed L x N = 24 budget, balanced splits (4x6, 3x8) are best; neither more unique depth nor more iterations alone is sufficient.
quote: This suggests that neither increasing depth nor iteration alone is sufficient; instead, effective performance arises from a proper balance between the two.

title: LoopVLA: Learning Sufficiency in Recurrent Refinement for Vision-Language-Action Models
claim: Adaptive (sufficiency-based) exit selection beats any fixed exit iteration, and optimal depth varies by task suite.
quote: Notably, adaptive selection (∗) consistently outperforms fixed strategies, indicating that the optimal computation depth is input-dependent.

title: ELT: Elastic Looped Transformers for Visual Generation
claim: In DiT, looped 16N x 2L (1.1B) and 8N x 4L (539M) beat the 32-layer 2.1B DiT at the same inference compute; the 1.1B looped model also beats the same-size 16-layer DiT (2.83 vs 3.87).
quote: ELT outperforms the baseline model with 32 layers (FID 3.43) using iso-inference-compute 8 𝑁 × 4 𝐿 (FID 3.16) and 16 𝑁 × 2 𝐿 (FID 2.83) settings, achieving 4× and 2× reduction in parameter count respectively.

title: ELT: Elastic Looped Transformers for Visual Generation
claim: A single unique layer looped 32 times fails (FID 10.30): a minimum block size N is needed.
quote: The 1 𝑁 × 32 𝐿 configuration (FID 10.30) reveals that a single unique transformer layer, despite 32 effective passes, lacks the representational capacity for high-fidelity generation

title: ELT: Elastic Looped Transformers for Visual Generation
claim: Vanilla looping only gives coherent images at the training loop count; ILSD enables any-time inference across loop counts.
quote: standard looping only produces a coherent image when the inference loop count exactly matches its training setup ( 𝐿 = 8), with quality severely degrading at all other values.

title: ELT: Elastic Looped Transformers for Visual Generation
claim: Increasing loops at fixed N keeps improving FID with diminishing returns; beyond a point, moving to a larger model beats over-looping a small one.
quote: the gains eventually diminish, where transitioning to the next architecture scale becomes more performant than over-looping smaller models.

title: ELT: Elastic Looped Transformers for Visual Generation
claim: In data-constrained video generation, a 76M looped model beats MAGVIT at iso-inference-compute, which the authors read as robustness to overfitting.
quote: Our compact 76M ELT model outperforms MAGVIT baseline (FVD 72.8 vs 76) on data-constrained settings of UCF-101 (∼13.7M training tokens) in iso-inference-compute settings.

title: MoR–Swin: Efficient Vision Transformer Using Mixture of Recursions
claim: MoR-Swin halves parameters and speeds inference up to 2x at a modest accuracy cost relative to Swin-B.
quote: MoR–Swin reduces parameters by about 50% and accelerates inference up to twofold at a modest accuracy cost (within about 0.5 points of Swin-B on ImageNet-1K).

title: LoopViT: Scaling Visual ARC with Looped Transformers
claim: At equal parameters (18M), the looped ViT beats the feed-forward VARC ViT on ARC-AGI-1 (65.8 vs 54.5) and the 73M VARC ensemble (60.4); compute is higher due to unrolling.
quote: By recycling weights across iterations, Loop-ViT (Large) achieves 65.8% on ARC-1, surpassing the 73M VARC ensemble.

title: LoopViT: Scaling Visual ARC with Looped Transformers
claim: A 3.8M Loop-ViT beats the 18M VARC baseline with about one fifth of the parameters.
quote: a 3.8M parameter Loop-ViT (Small) reaches 60.1% score on ARC-1, surpassing the 18M VARC baseline (54.5%) with roughly one-fifth of the parameters

title: LoopViT: Scaling Visual ARC with Looped Transformers
claim: Entropy-based dynamic exit (T in [4,8]) gives higher accuracy at lower average compute than a fixed 6-step model.
quote: the Dynamic Exit mechanism achieves higher accuracy while using lower average inference compute on ARC-AGI-1.

title: LoopViT: Scaling Visual ARC with Looped Transformers
claim: Low-capacity cores benefit most from added iterations; high-capacity cores keep scaling with T up to the limit.
quote: For low-capacity cores (B = 2), increasing T yields the most significant gains as weight-tied recurrence emulates the expressive depth of larger models

title: On the Role of Computation in Reinforcement Learning
claim: More recurrent steps substantially improve RL performance, up to about 10x on hard boxpick and OGBench manipulation tasks.
quote: In the challenging boxpick tasks, or the manipulation tasks in ogbench, performance increases up to 10 times after increasing the recurrent steps from one to ten.

title: On the Role of Computation in Reinforcement Learning
claim: IRU-(10) beats a ResNet baseline that uses about 2x more compute and 5x more parameters, and beats the parameter-matched MLP on all tasks.
quote: This is despite the ResNet using ≈ 2× more compute and ≈ 5× more parameters than IRU-(10).

title: On the Role of Computation in Reinforcement Learning
claim: Recurrent policies trained on nearby goals generalize better to unseen longer-horizon tasks (beat MLP on all, ResNet on 4/6), with more stable training.
quote: Figure 4 shows that IRU outperforms MLP on all tasks and ResNet on 4/6 tasks, and the IRU is more sample efficient on all tasks.

title: On the Role of Computation in Reinforcement Learning
claim: Gating is needed: recurrent ResNet blocks do not get the compute benefit, and TRM-style deep recursion works worse.
quote: We see that the recurrent ResNet blocks do not achieve the same benefits of added compute.

title: LoopVAE: Recurrent Depth Across Scales for Visual Tokenization
claim: At a fixed execution graph, global sharing (one seventh the stored core blocks) beats fully unshared processing on PSNR and SSIM, while unshared wins on LPIPS.
quote: Global sharing has the highest PSNR and SSIM, exceeding fully unshared processing by 0.120 dB and 0.0023, respectively, while using one seventh as many stored core blocks.

title: LoopVAE: Recurrent Depth Across Scales for Visual Tokenization
claim: The 29M looped CNN tokenizer is competitive with 84M VAEs but baselines use unmatched recipes, so no causal advantage of recurrence is claimed.
quote: Training recipes are not controlled, so quality differences cannot be attributed solely to recurrence or operator choice.

title: LoopVAE: Recurrent Depth Across Scales for Visual Tokenization
claim: Weight reuse does not reduce execution cost: the looped CNN uses more MACs and higher latency than a Flux-style reference.
quote: Runtime profiling shows that the 8x looped CNN stores 65.3% fewer parameters than a local Flux-style reference, but uses 1.57× its estimated MACs and 2.85× its batch latency.

title: LoopVAE: Recurrent Depth Across Scales for Visual Tokenization
claim: Small feature updates in a trained pass still matter a lot (bypass loses ~7.8 dB), and truncation produces output-range errors, so the recurrence is not an any-time decoder.
quote: feature by only 7.47–9.36% across images, yet bypassing it loses 4.00–11.94 dB PSNR (mean 7.78 dB).

title: Investigating Single-Block Recurrence in Vision Transformers for Image Recognition
claim: At sufficient width, a single block reused 12 times nearly matches ViT-B and ViT-L at the same training recipe and compute with ~10-20x fewer parameters.
quote: The correspondence is even closer for the large model, with bViT-L reaching 0.805 compared with 0.808 for ViT-L, while reducing the parameter count from 304.3M to 14.6M.

title: Investigating Single-Block Recurrence in Vision Transformers for Image Recognition
claim: At narrow width (384), full sharing loses ~10 points and more recurrent steps or heads do not close the gap.
quote: At an embedding dimension of 384, bViT-S reaches only 0.681 accuracy compared with 0.782 for ViT-S.

title: Investigating Single-Block Recurrence in Vision Transformers for Image Recognition
claim: At fixed 12 block evaluations and width, accuracy rises monotonically as more computation is assigned to unique blocks.
quote: Accuracy improves progressively as more of the computation is assigned to distinct blocks, from 0.681 with one block repeated 12 times to 0.782 with 12 independently parameterized blocks.

title: Investigating Single-Block Recurrence in Vision Transformers for Image Recognition
claim: At a fixed ~8.7M parameter budget, a wide single-block model beats narrower multi-block ViTs (not FLOP matched).
quote: As capacity is shifted from representation width toward independently parameterized blocks, accuracy decreases monotonically from 0.779 for bViTB to 0.747 for a 12-block ViT with embedding dimension 240

title: RecycleNet: Latent Feature Recycling Leads to Iterative Decision Refinement
claim: Recycling improves over nnU-Net and DRU on all datasets except liver tumor (CV), with no added parameters but more compute.
quote: We show clear performance improvements compared to both baselines across all evaluation datasets but the liver tumor segmentation dataset, where the DRU [18] shows the best cross validation score.

title: RecycleNet: Latent Feature Recycling Leads to Iterative Decision Refinement
claim: Test-time cycles beyond training (up to 7 vs 3) monotonically increase Dice and saturate ('prediction convergence').
quote: We observe a monotonous performance increase when increasing the number of recycling cycles during inference, asymptotically converging towards a saturation DSC value.

title: Universal Speech Transformer
claim: Removing depth embeddings and adding positional embedding only once improves the UT for acoustic inputs.
quote: we modify its processing framework by removing the depth embedding and only adding the positional embedding once at transformer encoder frontend.

title: Universal Speech Transformer
claim: The model outperforms the baseline by 3.88-13.7% on three ASR datasets.
quote: Experiments on LibriSpeech, Switchboard and AISHELL-1 datasets show that our model outperforms a baseline by 3.88%-13.7%, and surpasses other model with less computation cost.

title: LAST: Looped Audio Spectrogram Transformer
claim: At R=10, LAST beats a deeper 12-layer sequential AST on AudioSet with fewer parameters, MACs and higher throughput.
quote: at 𝑅 = 10, LAST reaches 0.3450 mAP against 0.3379 for sequential 𝐷 = 12 — a 2.1% relative improvement — with 49.4% fewer parameters, 42% fewer MACs, and 9.8% higher measured throughput.

title: LAST: Looped Audio Spectrogram Transformer
claim: Against the parameter-matched 6-layer sequential AST, LAST wins once R >= 6, and the 8 extra passes add only 1.2% compute.
quote: Against the parameter-matched sequential 𝐷 = 6 baseline, LAST wins once 𝑅 ≥ 6, and its mAP rises at every tested pass count, from 0.3275 at 𝑅 = 2 to 0.3450 at 𝑅 = 10.

title: LAST: Looped Audio Spectrogram Transformer
claim: Naive full-token recurrence with the same blocks gets worse with more passes despite 5x compute.
quote: With the same six shared blocks, full-token recurrence falls from 0.3247 mAP at 𝑅 = 2 to 0.3099 at 𝑅 = 10, despite a fivefold increase in computation.

title: Looping Back to Move Forward: Recursive Transformers for Efficient and Flexible Large Multimodal Models
claim: Naive recursion (feeding final hidden states back) is worse than the non-recursive baseline at both steps; RMSNorm alone does not fix it.
quote: As shown in Table 1, our non-recursive baseline consistently outperforms the vanilla recursive methods at both recursion steps with r = 1 and r = 2.

title: Looping Back to Move Forward: Recursive Transformers for Efficient and Flexible Large Multimodal Models
claim: With the connector and monotonic loss, recursion-trained models beat the non-recursive baseline by 1-2% at r=1 and about +3% at r=2.
quote: At the second recursion step, performance improves by +3% compared with the non-recursive baseline, confirming monotonic gains and validating our design for deploymentadaptive inference.

title: Looping Back to Move Forward: Recursive Transformers for Efficient and Flexible Large Multimodal Models
claim: R=3 gives diminishing or negative returns on general benchmarks but keeps improving HallusionBench.
quote: However, a striking trend emerges on the HallusionBench: performance consistently improves with deeper recursion (37.56 → 38.69 → 45.12).

title: ReLoop-UME: Recurrent Depth with Learnable Retrieval Registers for Universal Multimodal Embedding
claim: Under the same recipe, looping layers 17-26 with registers improves MMEB-V2 All over the single-forward model by 2.2-2.6 points across three 2B backbones.
quote: Single forward uses T = 1 and M = 0. The gains support the recipe beyond Qwen2-VL.

title: ReLoop-UME: Recurrent Depth with Learnable Retrieval Registers for Universal Multimodal Embedding
claim: Loop placement matters more than compute: full-decoder recurrence uses nearly twice the decoder applications yet performs worse than looping layers 17-26.
quote: More computation alone is insufficient: full-decoder recurrence requires 112 decoder applications, nearly twice the 58 of layers 17–26, yet performs worse

title: ReLoop-UME: Recurrent Depth with Learnable Retrieval Registers for Universal Multimodal Embedding
claim: Gains saturate at moderate depth: T=4 is best, T=8 slightly worse.
quote: Increasing T from 1 to 2 improves All from 60.6 to 62.1, and T = 4 reaches 63.2; extending to T = 8 slightly drops to 62.8 despite substantially more decoder applications.

title: ReLoop-UME: Recurrent Depth with Learnable Retrieval Registers for Universal Multimodal Embedding
claim: Recurrent depth gives large latency advantages over token-expanded reasoning embedders.
quote: It reduces per-sample latency from 9023 ms for UME-R1 to 201 ms, corresponding to a 44.9× speedup, and is 1.5× faster than PLUME.

title: Tab-TRM: Tiny Recursive Model for Insurance Pricing on Tabular Data
claim: Tab-TRM's out-of-sample Poisson deviance is competitive with the best neural architectures on French MTPL; baselines are taken from prior publications (unmatched).
quote: Tab-TRM achieves an out-of-sample Poisson deviance loss of 23.630 × 10−2 (single run) and 23.589 × 10−2 (nagging ensemble), which is competitive with the best network architectures in

title: Tab-TRM: Tiny Recursive Model for Insurance Pricing on Tabular Data
claim: Recursion gives large effective depth from few parameters: m=6, T=3 is comparable to a 40-50 layer FNN.
quote: For a typical configuration with m = 6 and T = 3, the effective depth is comparable to a 40 to 50 layer FNN, but with far fewer parameters and a much stronger inductive bias

title: CoReLoop: Parameter-Efficient Controlled Recurrent Refinement for Audio Deepfake Detection
claim: Naive recurrence of a frozen single-pass encoder degrades detection sharply, so recurrence must be converted with input adaptation and state control.
quote: simply feeding this output back without adaptation raises pooled EER from 4.85% at the first pass to 10.52% and 64.68% at the next two.

title: CoReLoop: Parameter-Efficient Controlled Recurrent Refinement for Audio Deepfake Detection
claim: Two controlled passes reduce pooled EER 4.85% -> 3.74% and beat single-pass LoRA with the same adapters and schedule (4.24%), so adapters alone do not explain the gain.
quote: It also outperforms single-pass LoRA (4.24% pooled EER), indicating that LoRA adaptation alone does not account for the full gain.

title: CoReLoop: Parameter-Efficient Controlled Recurrent Refinement for Audio Deepfake Detection
claim: A third pass gives only marginal pooled gains and slightly worse macro EER; adaptive halting matches two passes at 1.18 average passes.
quote: Adaptive inference achieves 3.73% pooled EER at an average of 1.18 passes, using 41% fewer encoder-core evaluations than fixed two-pass inference.

title: RecRec: Latent Interests Recursive Reasoning for Sequential Recommendation
claim: At training depth N=9, RecRec beats the best reasoning-enhanced baseline in NDCG@10 by 4.3-14.8% across four datasets.
quote: RecRec (S) improves NDCG@10 over the best reasoning-enhanced baseline by 14.8% on Steam, 9.3% on MicroLens, 8.2% on V-Shop, and 4.3% on S-Shop.

title: RecRec: Latent Interests Recursive Reasoning for Sequential Recommendation
claim: Deep supervision with detached rounds lets inference depth extend past the training depth with small gains on 3 of 4 datasets (MicroLens saturates near 4 and declines).
quote: on three of four datasets, performance is sustained past the training-time depth 𝑁 = 9 with small additional gains.

title: One-Step Diffusion Distillation via Deep Equilibrium Models
claim: With the same offline distillation data, GET matches the FID of a 5x larger ViT.
quote: Moreover, GET is able to match the FID score of a 5× large ViT, suggesting substantial parameter efficiency.

title: One-Step Diffusion Distillation via Deep Equilibrium Models
claim: At a fixed training budget (231 GFLOPs), the best implicit model (GET-Small, 31.2M) is preferable to the best explicit ViT-L (302M), and test-time iterations trade speed for FID.
quote: at 231 training GFLOPs, Figure 3(b) suggests that we should choose GET-Small (31.2M) among implicit models for the best performance, which is much more parameter efficient and faster in sampling than the best-performing explicit model, ViT-L (302M), at this training budget.

title: One-Step Diffusion Distillation via Deep Equilibrium Models
claim: Weight-tying acts as a regularizer that makes GET data efficient: with 1M offline samples it reaches parity with online distilled EDM at half the iterations, whereas PD, TRACT and CM use far more samples.
quote: even with a fixed and limited offline data budget of 1M samples, GET achieves parity with online distilled EDM [48, 88, 97] while using only half the number of training iterations.

title: Deeply-Recursive Convolutional Network for Image Super-Resolution
claim: At fixed parameters (four models with 1, 6, 11, 16 recursions), PSNR increases with recursion depth.
quote: We trained four models with different numbers of recursions: 1, 6, 11, and 16. Four models use the same number of parameters except the weights used for ensemble.

title: Deeply-Recursive Convolutional Network for Image Super-Resolution
claim: No single recursion depth is best across scales; ensembling intermediate recursions significantly helps.
quote: There is no single recursion depth that works the best across all scale factors. Ensemble of intermediate predictions significantly improves performance.

title: Learning When to Recur: Token-Adaptive Recursion for Imbalanced Ophthalmic Domain Incremental Learning
claim: Uniform recursion (no gate) from 1 to 3 steps does not improve; learned token selection at 3 steps improves Avg. F1 by 5.29 points.
quote: The two no-gate settings show that uniformly increasing recursion from one to three steps does not improve Avg. F1 or Avg. BAcc.

claim: Kmax=3 is best among 1, 3, 5, 10.

title: Solve the Loop: Attractor Models for Language and Reasoning

claim: At scale, the first runs (parameter-free norms, no embedding scale, additive adapter) collapsed: the model learned to ignore the recurrence, so perplexity was the same at 1 or 32 iterations.

title: Scaling up Test-Time Compute with Latent Reasoning: A Recurrent Depth Approach
claim: Against a non-recurrent twin trained on the same 180B tokens, the recurrent model is much better on harder tasks (ARC-C, GSM8K), with similar recall tasks; parameter/FLOP matching of the twin is not stated.
quote: In direct comparison of both models at 180B tokens, we see that the recurrent model outperforms its baseline with an especially pronounced advantage on harder tasks, such as the ARC challenge set.

title: Scaling up Test-Time Compute with Latent Reasoning: A Recurrent Depth Approach
claim: Test-time recurrence improves reasoning benchmarks up to compute equivalent to a 50B-parameter model; comparisons are to public models trained on other data.
quote: We show that the resulting model can improve its performance on reasoning benchmarks, sometimes dramatically, up to a computation load equivalent to 50 billion parameters.

title: MoEUT: Mixture-of-Experts Universal Transformers
claim: MoEUT slightly outperforms dense Transformers with the same parameter count on C4 perplexity, and the gap grows with scale (up to about 1B).
quote: The plot shows that our MoEUT model slightly outperforms dense models with the same number of parameters (Fig. 4a), and the gap tends to grow with scale.

title: MoEUT: Mixture-of-Experts Universal Transformers

title: MoEUT: Mixture-of-Experts Universal Transformers
claim: A small group size (G=2) is optimal at 244M; G=1 (single shared layer) and G=18 (no sharing) are worse; AABB stacking is almost as bad as no grouping.

title: MoEUT: Mixture-of-Experts Universal Transformers
claim: Peri-layernorm beats pre- and post-layernorm for shared-layer models; the gap shrinks with model size but grows with training steps.

title: MoEUT: Mixture-of-Experts Universal Transformers

quote: Upon careful investigation, we found that most of this poor performance comes from the ACT mechanism that the authors advertise as one of the main components of their model.

title: Lessons on Parameter Sharing across Layers in Transformers

quote: the proposed strategies (SEQUENCE, CYCLE, and CYCLE ( REV )) were faster and achieved slightly better scores than Universal when we set M = 6 and N = 12.

title: Lessons on Parameter Sharing across Layers in Transformers
claim: Stacking more layers barely helps when a single layer is shared across all layers.
quote: Universal (deep) didn’t improve the performance from Universal, and thus stacking many layers have small effect on BLEU scores when the model shares parameters of one layer with all layers.

title: Lessons on Parameter Sharing across Layers in Transformers
claim: In language modeling, full one-layer sharing is worse than no sharing, while partial sharing (N=12, M=6) beats the 6-layer Vanilla at equal parameters; SEQUENCE is best.
quote: This table indicates that Vanilla achieved better performance than Universal. Thus, the sharing parameters of one layer with all layers might not be suitable for a large-scaled language modeling task.

title: Lessons on Parameter Sharing across Layers in Transformers
claim: Which reuse pattern is best is setting dependent: SEQUENCE beats CYCLE and CYCLE(REV) in Pre-LN ASR (and LM), contrary to Post-LN MT where CYCLE(REV) is best.

title: Deep Equilibrium Models
claim: Training and inference need only constant memory regardless of effective depth, because gradients are computed by implicit differentiation at the equilibrium.
quote: Using this approach, training and prediction in these networks require only constant memory, regardless of the effective “depth” of the network.

title: Deep Equilibrium Models
claim: At similar parameter counts DEQs match or slightly beat Transformer-XL and TrellisNet on WikiText-103 while using 80-88% less memory.
quote: On both instantiations, the DEQ approach leads to an over 80% (up to 88%) reduction in memory consumption by the model (excluding word embeddings, which are orthogonal to the comparison here).

title: Deep Equilibrium Models
claim: Stacking several DEQs gives no extra representational power over a single DEQ.
quote: The theorem essentially shows that stacking multiple DEQs does not create extra representational power over a single DEQ.

title: Deep Equilibrium Models
claim: Weight-tied deep sequence models tend to converge to a fixed point as depth grows, motivating solving for the equilibrium directly.
quote: we hypothesize and observe that such weight-tied models tend to converge to a fixed point as depth increases towards infinity (see Appendix D for empirical evidence).

title: Deep Equilibrium Models
claim: DEQs are slower than the corresponding explicit deep networks (runtime ratios above 1x in Table 4), though computation can be traded via tolerance or Broyden iteration limits.
quote: Table 4: Runtime ratios between DEQs and corresponding deep networks at training and inference (> 1× implies DEQ is slower). The ratios are benchmarked on WikiText-103.

title: Adaptive Computation Time for Recurrent Neural Networks
claim: ACT lets a recurrent network learn how many computation steps to take per input, deterministically and differentiably.
quote: ACT requires minimal changes to the network architecture, is deterministic and differentiable, and does not add any noise to the parameter gradients.

title: Adaptive Computation Time for Recurrent Neural Networks
claim: Same parameters are used for all intermediate steps, explicitly to separate more steps from more parameters.
quote: It would also be possible to use different state and output parameters for each intermediate step; however doing so would cloud the distinction between increasing the number of parameters and increasing the number of computational steps.

title: Adaptive Computation Time for Recurrent Neural Networks
claim: On parity, the network without ACT fails (about 40% error) while ACT with low time penalty gets below 5% error.
quote: the network was unable to reliably solve the problem without ACT, with a mean of almost 40% error compared to 50% for random guessing. For penalties of 0.03 and below the mean error was below 5%.

title: Adaptive Computation Time for Recurrent Neural Networks
claim: For character-level language modeling ACT gives little gain; ponder is concentrated at spaces and sentence ends.
quote: the error rates are fairly similar with and without ACT, and across values of τ (although the learning curves suggest that the ACT networks are somewhat more data efficient).

title: Adaptive Computation Time for Recurrent Neural Networks
claim: Behaviour is sensitive to the hand-chosen time penalty tau.
quote: As we will see in the experiments section the behaviour of the network is quite sensitive to the value of τ , and it is not obvious how to choose a good value.

title: Allocating Recurrent Compute in Looped Language Models

title: Allocating Recurrent Compute in Looped Language Models

title: Allocating Recurrent Compute in Looped Language Models

title: The Topological Trouble With Transformers
claim: Feedforward transformers exhaust their depth on state tracking because state representations move deeper with each input step.
quote: feedforward models push evolving state representations deeper into their layer stack with each new input step, rendering information inaccessible in shallow layers and ultimately exhausting the model’s depth.

title: The Topological Trouble With Transformers
claim: Depth recurrence (looped transformers) does not by itself remove the upward drift of state across input steps.

title: The Topological Trouble With Transformers

title: Gated Recurrent Transformers: Expressive Depth through Recurrent Modulation

title: Zero Token-Driven Deep Thinking in LLMs: Unlocking the Full Potential of Existing Parameters via Cyclic Refinement

title: DeltaLLM: Compress LLMs with Low-Rank Deltas between Shared Weights

title: DeltaLLM: Compress LLMs with Low-Rank Deltas between Shared Weights
claim: 12% parameter reduction retains about 90% of base performance and beats pruning baselines at equal parameters removed.

title: Improving Recursive Transformers with Mixture of LoRAs

title: Improving Recursive Transformers with Mixture of LoRAs
claim: ModernALBERT (50M-120M) achieves state of the art among compact encoders and surpasses larger fully parameterised baselines.

title: AlgoFormer: An Efficient Transformer Framework with Algorithmic Structures
claim: A pre-transformer, looped transformer and post-transformer structure, mirroring preprocessing, iterative optimization and postprocessing, gives algorithmic inductive bias.
quote: our transformer framework consists of a pre-transformer that is responsible for task preprocessing, a looped transformer for iterative optimization algorithms, and a post-transformer for producing the desired results after post-processing.

title: AlgoFormer: An Efficient Transformer Framework with Algorithmic Structures
claim: AlgoFormer outperforms the standard transformer and the vanilla looped transformer on some algorithm-learning tasks and on NMT/text classification.
quote: Experimental results demonstrate the empirical superiority of the proposed transformer in that it outperforms the standard transformer and vanilla looped transformer in some specific tasks.

title: Loop Neural Networks for Parameter Sharing
claim: A 6-layer looped network matches the 12-layer GPT-2 validation loss on OpenWebText; 4 layers x 12 loops is within 1% of GPT2-124M.

title: MobileLLM: Optimizing Sub-billion Parameter Language Models for On-Device Use Cases
claim: Immediate block-wise weight sharing improves accuracy with no increase in model size and marginal latency overhead.
quote: Additionally, we propose an immediate block-wise weightsharing approach with no increase in model size and only marginal latency overhead. The resultant models, denoted as MobileLLM-LS, demonstrate a further accuracy enhancement of 0.7%/0.8% than MobileLLM 125M/350M.

title: MobileLLM: Optimizing Sub-billion Parameter Language Models for On-Device Use Cases
claim: Among sharing patterns, repeat-all-over (whole-stack cycle) performs best, but immediate block-wise repeat is chosen because the shared block fits in SRAM.
quote: Results in Table 2 indicate that the repeatover layer-sharing strategy produces the best performance among immediate block-wise repeat, repeat all-over, and reverse sharing strategies.

title: MobileLLM: Optimizing Sub-billion Parameter Language Models for On-Device Use Cases
claim: The SRAM constraint motivates immediate repetition.
quote: the SRAM for computing is typically limited to around 20MB. This capacity is usually only sufficient to hold a single transformer block.

title: Sparse Universal Transformer
claim: SUT matches strong baselines on WMT'14 with about half the computation and parameters.
quote: Experiments show that SUT achieves the same performance as strong baseline models while only using half computation and parameters on WMT’14

title: Sparse Universal Transformer
claim: Stick-breaking halting cuts inference computation by about 50% on formal language tasks with little performance loss.
quote: The new halting mechanism also enables around 50% reduction in computation during inference with very little performance decrease on formal language tasks.

title: Understanding Parameter Sharing in Transformers
claim: The success of sharing parameters to stack more layers is largely due to better convergence, with only a small part from increased FLOPs.
quote: we show that the success of this approach can be largely attributed to better convergence, with only a small part due to the increased model complexity.

title: Understanding Parameter Sharing in Transformers
claim: With convergence-related hyperparameters tuned, an unshared Transformer matches sharing models at half the model complexity (FLOPs).
quote: Our experiments on 8 WMT tasks show that the original model can achieve competitive performance against the sharing model, but with only half the model complexity.

title: Path Independent Equilibrium Models Can Better Exploit Test-Time Computation
claim: Path independent models improve monotonically with more test-time iterations; path dependent models degrade beyond training depth.
quote: path independent models increase their performance monotonically with the number of test-time iterations, whereas path dependent models degrade when the number of test time iterations exceeds those at training time.

title: Path Independent Equilibrium Models Can Better Exploit Test-Time Computation
claim: Input injection and implicit (fixed-point) updates improve both path independence and accuracy.
quote: We find that input injection and implicit updates improve both the path independence and the accuracy.

title: Path Independent Equilibrium Models Can Better Exploit Test-Time Computation
claim: Without input injection a path-independent network would forget the input, so any model that fits the data must be path dependent.
quote: Without input injection, a PI network would necessarily forget the input; hence, any model which successfully fits the training distribution must be path dependent.

title: Path Independent Equilibrium Models Can Better Exploit Test-Time Computation
claim: Interventions that promote path independence improve generalization to harder instances; those that penalize it degrade it.
quote: Experimental interventions made to promote path independence result in improved generalization on harder problem instances, while those that penalize it degrade this ability.

title: Recurrent multiple shared layers in Depth for Neural Machine Translation
claim: Looped shared blocks match a deep Transformer in BLEU and inference speed with about half the parameters, and beat shallow Transformer-Base/Big with far fewer parameters.
quote: Compared to the deep Transformer(20-layer encoder, 6-layer decoder), our model has similar model performance and infer speed, but our model parameters are 54.72% of the former.

title: Staircase Attention for Recurrent Processing of Sequences
claim: Staircase models give significantly lower perplexity than Transformers with the same number of parameters on language and dialogue modeling (not necessarily the same compute).
quote: repeated application of the recurrent network over the sequence also makes the model considerably deeper for the same number of parameters (but not necessarily the same amount of compute).

title: Staircase Attention for Recurrent Processing of Sequences
claim: Ladder (depth-only weight-shared repetition) is effective on standard LM tasks but fails some state-tracking tasks that time recurrence solves.
quote: Notably, Ladder models are surprisingly effective and simple to implement on standard modeling tasks which do not appear to require much recurrence in time, but fail on some state-tracking tasks.

title: Neural Parameter Allocation Search
claim: Existing sharing methods rely on hand-crafted strategies and many identical layers; SSNs learn where and how to share for any parameter budget, including a high-budget regime adding capacity without more inference FLOPs.
quote: NPAS covers both low-budget regimes, which produce compact networks, as well as a novel high-budget regime, where additional capacity can be added to boost performance without increasing inference FLOPs.

title: TextNCA: Neural Cellular Automata for Language Modeling via Hierarchical Local Attention
claim: At about 30M parameters the hierarchical iterated model is worse than parameter-matched Transformers.

title: TextNCA: Neural Cellular Automata for Language Modeling via Hierarchical Local Attention
claim: Iteration adds a bounded benefit with an optimum at T_s=4 and U-shaped degradation beyond; the GRU gate and per-step embeddings are required, and random T_s training gives an inference knob at higher PPL.
quote: Iteration adds a smaller bounded benefit on top of the schedule, with a clear optimum at $T_s{=}4$ and a U-shaped degradation beyond it.

title: UniPool: Learning Expert-to-Layer Ownership from Brief Global Access
claim: Same expert budget and routed FLOPs: learned allocation lowers loss by 0.024-0.037 vs vanilla MoE across scales up to 1.5B.
quote: With the same expert-FFN budget and routed expert FLOPs, this recipe lowers held-out loss relative to vanilla MoE by 0.024-0.037 across five dense-equivalent scales from 182M to 1.5B

title: UniPool: Learning Expert-to-Layer Ownership from Brief Global Access
claim: A globally shared expert pool across layers (UniPool-Full) beats vanilla MoE with only 50-66.7% of its expert parameters.
quote: Keeping full-pool access throughout training (UniPool-Full) also improves over vanilla MoE at four scales and outperforms it with only 66.7% (182M) to 50% (469M and 650M) of its expert parameters.

title: Write Back the $Δ$: Revisiting the Same Tokens with Fresh Representations
claim: Feeding back the depth increment (not the full state) is a better recurrence signal; synchronous ReFlux reduces perplexity and improves accuracy, up to 4.7 points on multi-hop reasoning.
quote: synchronous ReFlux consistently reduces perplexity across ten language-modeling corpora, and improves accuracy by 2.1–2.3 points, with gains reaching 4.7 points on multi-hop reasoning.

title: Write Back the $Δ$: Revisiting the Same Tokens with Fresh Representations
claim: Streaming feedback to subsequent tokens keeps most gains at the base model's theoretical backbone FLOPs.
quote: Streaming ReFlux further retains most of these gains while preserving the base model's 1x theoretical backbone FLOPs.

title: Reproducing Recurrent Transformers: The CoTFormer
claim: Base CoTFormer perplexity results reproduce exactly within confidence intervals.
quote: Ours represents a single-seed evaluation showing per-batch 95% confidence intervals. ∆ values fall within these boundaries, confirming exact reproducibility.

title: Reproducing Recurrent Transformers: The CoTFormer
claim: More loop depth did not improve OOD extrapolation on shifted-start counting for BUT, CoTFormer or Transformers.
quote: Increasing loop depth did not improve extrapolation under teacher-forced sequence prediction, suggesting that models may rely on positional shortcuts rather than an iterative counting procedure.

title: Rethinking Parameter Sharing as Graph Coloring for Structured Compression
claim: A second-order geometric criterion selects sharing groups that beat heuristic sharing strategies at higher compression ratios.
quote: Across diverse architectures and tasks, Geo-Sharing consistently outperforms state-of-the-art heuristic sharing strategies, achieving higher compression ratios with smaller accuracy degradation.

title: Principled Approximation Methods for Efficient and Scalable Deep Learning
claim: Proposes a NAS algorithm that uses parameter sharing across layers to explore implicitly recurrent architectures.
quote: In the context of architecture design, we design an algorithm for neural architecture search that leverages parameter sharing across layers to efficiently explore implicitly recurrent architectures.

title: Learning Fine-grained Parameter Sharing via Sparse Tensor Decomposition
claim: Cross-block shared basis with sparse layer-specific projections compresses ViTs and LLMs better than SVD baselines at matched compression.
quote: FiPS compresses Vision Transformers (ViTs) by up to 33% with less than 1% top-1 accuracy loss on ImageNet-1k, and by up to 57% when combined with fine-tuning.

title: Towards Autoformalization of Mathematics and Code Correctness: Experiments with Elementary Proofs

title: Do Generative Large Language Models need billions of parameters?
claim: Parameter sharing between model parts can reduce unique parameters without sacrificing language-modeling ability.
quote: The research explores novel methods that allow different parts of the model to share parameters, reducing the total number of unique parameters required.

title: Latent Universal Task-Specific BERT
claim: Combines the BERT objective with a generalized Universal Transformer and releases a model pretrained on 100M tweets.
quote: Finally, we release a pre-trained language representation model for social texts that was trained on 100 million tweets.

title: The Uncanny Similarity of Recurrence and Depth
claim: Recurrent models show the same hierarchical behaviors and depth benefits as feed-forward networks despite reusing filters.
quote: we observe that recurrent models exhibit the same hierarchical behaviors and the same performance benefits with depth as feed-forward networks despite reusing the same filters at every recurrence.

title: The Uncanny Similarity of Recurrence and Depth
claim: Recurrent networks can closely emulate non-recurrent deep models, often with far fewer parameters.
quote: we show that recurrent networks have the ability to closely emulate the behavior of non-recurrent deep models, often doing so with far fewer parameters.

title: Universal Transformers

title: Universal Transformers

title: Universal Transformers

title: Universal Transformers

quote: such a conditional computation mechanism can in fact improve accuracy on several smaller, structured algorithmic and linguistic inference tasks (although it marginally degraded results on MT).

title: Universal Transformers

title: Relaxed Recursive Transformers: Effective Parameter Sharing with Layer-wise LoRA

title: PonderLM: Pretraining Language Models to Ponder in Continuous Space

title: PonderLM: Pretraining Language Models to Ponder in Continuous Space

title: Intern-S2-Mobius: Foundation Model with Decoupled Knowledge and Reasoning

title: Recursive Inference Scaling: A Winning Path to Scalable Inference in Language and Multimodal Systems
claim: Stochastic RINS with linear adapters improves the LM even when recursion is disabled at test time (same training compute, parameters and inference cost).

title: Recursive Inference Scaling: A Winning Path to Scalable Inference in Language and Multimodal Systems

quote: We observe that recursive architectures, including RINS, do not confer any advantage in the supervised image classification domain

title: Recursive Inference Scaling: A Winning Path to Scalable Inference in Language and Multimodal Systems
claim: Sharing KV caches across recursion rounds (queries attend to first-call keys/values) reduces the gain but RINS keeps an advantage.

title: PonderNet: Learning to Ponder
claim: On parity extrapolation (more ones than in training), PonderNet reaches near-perfect accuracy while ACT stays at chance, and it increases thinking steps to about 5 (roughly twice interpolation).
quote: Figure 1b shows that PonderNet was able to achieve almost perfect accuracy on this hard extrapolation task, whereas ACT remained at chance level.

title: PonderNet: Learning to Ponder
claim: With the same UT transformer architecture, PonderNet solves all 20 bAbI tasks with far fewer steps than UT with ACT (1658 vs 10161).

title: PonderNet: Learning to Ponder

title: Can You Learn an Algorithm? Generalizing from Easy to Hard Problems with Recurrent Networks

title: Can You Learn an Algorithm? Generalizing from Easy to Hard Problems with Recurrent Networks

title: MoRE: Mixture of Reused Experts

quote: Monitoring then requires alternative access to the model, such as probing its activations or verbalizing the latent states back into text, but how much monitorability these alternatives preserve is unclear.

title: Does Out-of-Sight Equal Out-of-Mind in CoT Monitorability?
claim: Monitorability depends more on task properties and access to internals than on whether reasoning is explicit or latent.
quote: monitorability depends more on properties of the task (such as whether the correct answer constrains the supporting reasoning) and the level of access to model internals than on the reasoning mode.

title: Assessing Adversarial Robustness of Latent Reasoning Models
claim: Latent reasoning models are generally less robust than explicit CoT baselines under adversarial perturbations, especially white-box attacks.
quote: We find that, across our evaluated settings, LRMs are generally less robust than explicit CoT baselines under adversarial perturbations, with particularly severe degradation under white-box attacks.

title: Assessing Adversarial Robustness of Latent Reasoning Models
claim: Textual latent states show brittle dynamics; multimodal latent states can be largely invariant to input perturbations with limited influence on predictions.
quote: textual latent states exhibit brittle dynamics and high sensitivity to specific input patterns, while latent states in multimodal models can remain largely invariant to input perturbations and have limited influence on final predictions.

title: Final Checkpoints Are Not Enough: Analyzing Latent Reasoning Faithfulness Along Training Trajectories
claim: High task accuracy can coexist with low counterfactual responsiveness of latent steps, and responsiveness can decline as accuracy improves.
quote: We find that high task accuracy can coexist with low counterfactual responsiveness: as accuracy improves, responsiveness can decline, and different latent reasoning approaches follow distinct trajectories.

title: Final Checkpoints Are Not Enough: Analyzing Latent Reasoning Faithfulness Along Training Trajectories
claim: Evaluating only the final checkpoint can hide when responsiveness changes and what latent states contribute.
quote: These results show that evaluating only a final checkpoint can obscure both when counterfactual responsiveness changes and what the latent states contribute.

title: Chain of Thought Monitorability: A New and Fragile Opportunity for AI Safety
claim: Systems that think in human language offer an opportunity to monitor CoTs for intent to misbehave.
quote: AI systems that "think" in human language offer a unique opportunity for AI safety: we can monitor their chains of thought (CoT) for the intent to misbehave.

title: Chain of Thought Monitorability: A New and Fragile Opportunity for AI Safety
claim: CoT monitorability may be fragile, so developers should consider how development decisions affect it.
quote: Because CoT monitorability may be fragile, we recommend that frontier model developers consider the impact of development decisions on CoT monitorability.

title: Dissecting Hierarchical Reasoning Models: A Mechanistic Study
claim: Recurrent models beat one-pass baselines, but a single-state recurrent Transformer matches or slightly beats HRM, so hierarchy is not the source of the gain at this scale.
quote: outperforms HRM on puzzle accuracy, indicating that hierarchy does not itself clearly improve Sudoku at this scale.

title: Dissecting Hierarchical Reasoning Models: A Mechanistic Study
claim: The causally relevant solution state is task-dependent: zH is a progressively refined solution state for Sudoku, while zL carries the intermediate path for Maze.
quote: However, the functional contributions vary across tasks, with zH carrying the solution state for Sudoku and zL for Maze.

title: Dissecting Hierarchical Reasoning Models: A Mechanistic Study
claim: Task variables are linearly decodable (about 90% at the final step) but ablating the probe directions has effects comparable to random-direction controls.
quote: probe-direction ablations on Sudoku and Maze produce small behavioral changes relative to full-state interventions and are comparable to random controls.

title: Dissecting Hierarchical Reasoning Models: A Mechanistic Study
claim: SAE feature ablations have larger effects than probe ablations, but top SAE features are no more impactful than size-matched random features, indicating distributed computation.
quote: ablation of SAE features trained on HRM activations produces significantly larger effects than linear probe directions, but the top 50 SAE features are no more impactful than 50 random features.

title: Beyond Depth Truncation: Controlled Evaluation of Depth Utilization in Recursive Language Models

title: Beyond Depth Truncation: Controlled Evaluation of Depth Utilization in Recursive Language Models

title: Beyond Depth Truncation: Controlled Evaluation of Depth Utilization in Recursive Language Models

title: Hierarchical Reasoning Model

When compared with a larger Transformer under a matched training-FLOPs budget, however, their advantage is less consistent.

title: Form Follows Function: Recursive Stem Model

claim: At matched block-pass compute, untied depth and a flat two-stream recurrent baseline generalize best; the autoregressive TRM gives no consistent benefit and often degrades sharply.
quote: Across compute-matched experiments on character-level algorithmic tasks (addition, copying, reversing), untied depth and a flat two-stream recurrent baseline yield the strongest generalization per block evaluation.

title: Tiny Autoregressive Recursive Models
claim: Character accuracy (length 10): Dense and UT solve Copy and Reverse; on Addition Dense 80% vs UT 66%; autoregressive TRM ~10-12% on all three.
quote: Addition remains more difficult and separates these two models (80% vs. 66%). The autoregressive TRM performs poorly on all three tasks, reaching only 12%, 11%, and 10% accuracy, respectively.

title: Tiny Autoregressive Recursive Models
claim: Single-stream recurrent variants collapse at late output positions on addition, while Dual UT stays stable; only Dense and Dual UT overcome the last-character bottleneck.
quote: Only Dense and Dual UT reliably break through the final-character bottleneck, with lastcharacter accuracy rising sharply and reaching high values by the end of training.

title: BDH-CQ: In-Context Learning with Recurrent Latent Reasoning
claim: BDH-CQ reaches 29.5% pass@2 on ARC-AGI-1 public evaluation at a computed $0.00070 per task, beyond the leaderboard's previous cost-accuracy Pareto frontier.
quote: At the default point, the 150M-parameter system reaches 29.5% pass@2 in approximately 0.85 H200 GPU-seconds per task. At $3 per H200-hour this gives a computed cost of $0.00070 per task

title: BDH-CQ: In-Context Learning with Recurrent Latent Reasoning
claim: Unlike HRM/TRM ARC pipelines, neither task identifiers nor evaluation-task demonstrations are used in training.
quote: Neither task identifiers nor evaluation-task demonstration pairs participate in training, and no parameters are updated at inference time.

title: Self-Supervised Transformers as Iterative Solution Improvers for Constraint Satisfaction
claim: Iterating a one-step-trained refiner at test time solves out-of-distribution hard Sudoku, improving with more iterations (65.88% at 2k, 77.74% at 10k).
quote: ConsFormer achieves instance solve rates of 65.88% and 77.74% with 2k and 10k iterations, respectively.

title: Self-Supervised Transformers as Iterative Solution Improvers for Constraint Satisfaction
claim: Authors attribute better test-time scaling than a 32-iteration-trained recurrent Transformer to training for a single iteration.
quote: This could be due to Yang et al. (2023)'s approach being trained for 32 iterations, while ConsFormer was trained for a single iteration, allowing it to generalize better when applied iteratively.

title: G-RRM: Guiding Symbolic Solvers with Recurrent Reasoning Models
claim: Neural guidance from SE-RRM yields large speedups for backtracking and Glucose on 9x9 Sudoku, but not for CaDiCaL whose runtime is overhead-dominated and which always respects hints.
quote: on 9 × 9 Sudoku, where the SE-RRM correctly solves 91.1% of instances, backtracking accelerates by 33.3× and Glucose 4.1 by 1.70× (median, p < 0.001)

title: CosmicFish-HRM: Adaptive Reasoning via Hierarchical Recurrent Mechanisms in Compact Language Models
claim: At compact scale the HRM core does not improve zero-shot accuracy over similar-size Transformers; authors hypothesize the overhead amortizes at larger scale (untested).
quote: At compact scale, CosmicFish-HRM does not outperform conventional transformers of similar size on these benchmarks.

title: Latent Recurrent Thoughts: Recurrent Refinement of Proposed Latents for Reasoning with Frozen LLMs
claim: Scaling only the recurrent refiner (7M to 28M) with the decoder frozen improves Countdown-4 from 56.7 to 69.1 and HumanEval from 37.8 to 46.1.
quote: Countdown-4 rises from 56.7 to 66.3 to 69.1, and HumanEval from 37.8 to 44.0 to 46.1.

title: Latent Recurrent Thoughts: Recurrent Refinement of Proposed Latents for Reasoning with Frozen LLMs
claim: On Sudoku, thinking-mode Qwen3-8B fails (0.5) while the 7M refiner reaches 49.2; from-scratch symbolic solvers (TRM, EqR) remain far higher.
quote: Sudoku, is exactly where it fails (0.5) while a 7M recurrent refiner reaches 49.2: token-space search is not a substitute for iterative computation on a constraint-satisfaction substrate.

title: Parameter-Efficient Quality Estimation via Frozen Recursive Models
claim: TRM's recursive mechanisms do not transfer to QE: single-step models are best on external iteration, and internal recursion gives only narrow benefits.
quote: Contrary to intuitions from reasoning tasks, single-step models achieve the highest correlation (0.333 Pearson, 0.324 Spearman),

title: Parameter-Efficient Quality Estimation via Frozen Recursive Models
claim: Frozen-embedding TRM-QE (0.370 Spearman) outperforms an equivalent-depth standard Transformer (0.336).
quote: TRM-QE with frozen XLM-R embeddings achieves a Spearman's correlation of 0.370, matching fine-tuned variants (0.369) and outperforming an equivalentdepth standard transformer (0.336).

title: Selection, Reflection and Self-Refinement: Revisit Reasoning Tasks via a Causal Lens
claim: SR2 beats HRM by 11.6 points on Sudoku-Extreme and 19.2 on Maze-Hard with one eighth of the parameters.
quote: Moreover, SR2 surpasses HRM by 11.6% on Sudoku-Extreme and 19.2% on Maze-Hard, while using only one eighth of HRM's parameters.

title: Selection, Reflection and Self-Refinement: Revisit Reasoning Tasks via a Causal Lens
claim: A non-hierarchical Reflective Model matches HRM at equal parameters, suggesting the hierarchy is not necessary; input injection is what lifts a flat shared block (Block UT) to Recurrent Depth.
quote: HRM achieves results comparable to the Reflective Model, suggesting that hierarchical recurrent structures are not strictly necessary for reasoning tasks of this type.

title: What Limits Recursive Reasoning Models: Optimization, Architecture and Test-Time Scaling
claim: Explicit hierarchy (separate H/L parameters) is not a universal source of improvement: at matched parameter count shared modules win on Maze and ARC-AGI-1, separate ones give small gains on Sudoku and Game of Life.
quote: Shared modules perform better on Maze and ARC-AGI-1, while separate modules provide small gains on Sudoku and Game of Life; the two configurations are nearly identical on Arithmetic.

title: What Limits Recursive Reasoning Models: Optimization, Architecture and Test-Time Scaling
claim: Gradient horizon through the nested recurrence has an interior optimum: (KL,KH)=(2,2) gives the best Arithmetic OOD accuracy while (1,3), with the same number of differentiated applications, overfits ID.
quote: The intermediate setting (KL , KH ) = (2, 2) achieves the highest OOD accuracy of 71.16%, whereas (1, 3) reaches the highest ID accuracy of 99.60% but generalizes poorly, obtaining only 17.88% OOD.

title: What Limits Recursive Reasoning Models: Optimization, Architecture and Test-Time Scaling
claim: Gradient accumulation does not reproduce a large physical batch for recursive models: at fixed effective batch 8192, Game of Life OOD drops sharply with accumulation.
quote: OOD accuracy decreases from 63.16% with a physical batch of 8192 to 37.71% with four accumulation steps, while the mean pre-clipping gradient norm increases from 0.38 to 65.46.

title: What Limits Recursive Reasoning Models: Optimization, Architecture and Test-Time Scaling
claim: Larger recurrent blocks and extra test-time ACT steps give only domain-dependent gains (largest on Arithmetic and Sudoku, limited on Game of Life, Maze, ARC).
quote: Increasing the recurrent block from four to eight layers, increasing hidden size, or adding attention heads does not yield consistent accuracy gains across the tested settings.

title: What Limits Recursive Reasoning Models: Optimization, Architecture and Test-Time Scaling
claim: On ARC-AGI-1 the non-recurrent dense control is already competitive with recursive models; recursion helps most on Sudoku and Maze.
quote: ARC behaves differently: on ARC-AGI-1 the dense control is already competitive, while all systems remain limited on ARC-AGI-2.

title: What Limits Recursive Reasoning Models: Optimization, Architecture and Test-Time Scaling
claim: Parameter sharing reduces parameter count but not sequential inference cost: TRM and the 13.6M model have similar recurrent compute per answer.
quote: Parameter sharing therefore primarily reduces parameter count rather than sequential computation: TRM and our configuration have substantially different parameter counts but similar recurrent inference cost.

title: Probabilistic Tiny Recursive Model
claim: On Sudoku-Extreme, noisy rollouts with Q-head selection lift the deterministic TRM checkpoint from 87.3% to 98.75% (best-Q@K), using K=100 rollouts and 64 supervision steps.
quote: On Sudoku-Extreme, PTRM at K=100, D=64, σ=0.3 raises the deterministic baseline of 87.3% to 99.06% pass@K and 98.75% best-Q@K, achieving state of the art.

title: Probabilistic Tiny Recursive Model
claim: On Maze-Hard noise unlocks many correct rollouts (pass@K 95.63%) but the Q head selects them poorly (best-Q@K 85.17%, mode@K 86.73%).
quote: On Maze-Hard, PTRM at K=100, D=16, σ=1.0 reaches 95.63% pass@K, an 11.83 point gain over the 83.8% deterministic baseline. mode@K gives the best PTRM accuracy here at 86.73%

title: Probabilistic Tiny Recursive Model
claim: On ARC-AGI-2, PTRM gives a small pass@1 gain and no pass@2 gain over deterministic TRM with augmentation voting.
quote: With K=25 and σ=0.2, PTRM lifts pass@1 from 7.36% to 8.47% and pass@100 from 14.31% to 15.97% over our deterministic TRM baseline, while matching it at pass@2.

title: Probabilistic Tiny Recursive Model
claim: Width scaling dominates depth scaling: tripling depth at K=1 adds 3.1pp on PPBench validation while K=100 adds about 13pp.
quote: On the deterministic baseline (K=1), tripling the depth from 16 to 48 steps raises PPBench validation accuracy from 76.4% to 79.5% (+3.1pp).

title: Probabilistic Tiny Recursive Model
claim: Against frontier LLMs on the PPBench golden set, PTRM (91.2%) beats the strongest direct-strategy LLM and an oracle ensemble of 7 LLMs; this is an unmatched comparison (task-trained 7M model vs general LLMs).
quote: PTRM exceeds the strongest single LLM (direct strategy) by 57 points aggregate (91.2% vs. 34.7%), and exceeds the LLM ensemble by 36 points (91.2% vs. 55.1%)

title: Less is More: Recursive Reasoning with Tiny Networks
claim: Backpropagating through a full recursion process instead of HRM's 1-step gradient is the single largest gain (56.5% to 87.4% on Sudoku-Extreme).
quote: Yet, we can still leverage multiple backpropagation-free recursion processes to improve (z L , z H ). With this approach, we obtain a massive boost in generalization on Sudoku-Extreme (improving TRM from 56.5% to 87.4%; see Table 1).

title: Less is More: Recursive Reasoning with Tiny Networks
claim: Fewer layers with proportionally more recursions generalizes better: 2 layers beat 4 layers at roughly matched emulated depth; adding layers overfits.
quote: In doing so, we obtain better generalization on Sudoku-Extreme (improving TRM from 79.5% to 87.4%; see Table 1) while reducing the number of parameters by half (again).

title: Less is More: Recursive Reasoning with Tiny Networks
claim: A single network can replace HRM's separate f_L and f_H; using separate networks is worse.
quote: In doing so, we obtain better generalization on Sudoku-Extreme (improving TRM from 82.4% to 87.4%; see Table 1) while reducing the number of parameters by half.

title: Less is More: Recursive Reasoning with Tiny Networks
claim: HRM's fixed-point assumption behind the 1-step gradient is not satisfied in practice; residuals stay well above zero.
quote: Thus, while the application of the IFT theorem and 1-step gradient approximation to HRM has some basis since the residuals do generally reduce over time, a fixed point is unlikely to be reached when the theorem is actually applied.

title: Less is More: Recursive Reasoning with Tiny Networks
claim: TRM-Att beats HRM on Maze-Hard, ARC-AGI-1 and ARC-AGI-2 with a quarter of the parameters (HRM numbers copied from the HRM paper, same data/augmentation protocol).
quote: TRM with selfattention obtains 85.3% accuracy on Maze-Hard, 44.6% accuracy on ARC-AGI-1, and 7.8% accuracy on ARCAGI-2 with 7M parameters.

title: Less is More: Recursive Reasoning with Tiny Networks
claim: Self-attention replaced by a sequence MLP helps only for small fixed context (Sudoku 9x9), and hurts on 30x30 tasks.
quote: This worked well on Sudoku 9x9 grids, given the small and fixed context length; however, we found this architecture to be suboptimal for tasks with large context length, such as Maze-Hard and ARC-AGI (both using 30x30 grids).

title: Less is More: Recursive Reasoning with Tiny Networks
claim: Fixed-point iteration (TorchDEQ) instead of plain recursion slowed training and hurt generalization.
quote: However, this slowed down training due to the fixed-point iteration and led to worse generalization. This highlights the fact that converging to a fixed-point is not essential.

title: Less is More: Recursive Reasoning with Tiny Networks
claim: Failed ideas: MoE MLPs in the loop and gradients through only the last k steps did not help; removing ACT entirely hurt.
quote: We tried replacing the SwiGLU MLPs by SwiGLU Mixture-of-Experts (MoEs) (Shazeer et al., 2017; Fedus et al., 2022), but we found generalization to decrease massively.

title: Less is More: Recursive Reasoning with Tiny Networks
claim: Removing ACT (stopping only when solved) dropped generalization, attributed to too much time per sample.
quote: We tried removing ACT with the option of stopping when the solution is reached, but we found that generalization dropped significantly.

title: Universal Reasoning Model
claim: URM reaches 53.8% pass@1 on ARC-AGI-1 and 16.0% on ARC-AGI-2, above re-run TRM (40.0) and HRM (34.4).
quote: On ARC-AGI 2, URM obtains 16.0% pass@1, nearly tripling HRM and more than doubling TRM.

title: Universal Reasoning Model
claim: At equal FLOPs (32x), a weight-shared UT (4 layers x 8 loops) beats a 32-layer vanilla Transformer on ARC-AGI-1 pass@1 (40.0 vs 23.75); vanilla depth/width scaling saturates or degrades.
quote: At 32× FLOPs, reallocating computation from deep, non-shared layers to recurrent refinement improves pass@1 from 23.75 for vanilla Transformers to 40.0 for UTs.

title: Universal Reasoning Model
claim: Gains come from recurrence and nonlinearity, not elaborate hierarchy; weakening MLP activation or removing attention softmax degrades ARC-AGI-1 monotonically.
quote: Among these components, the activation function in the MLP plays a particularly critical role: replacing SwiGLU with simpler nonlinearities such as SiLU or ReLU leads to substantial degradation, while completely removing the attention softmax results in a dramatic collapse in performance.

title: Universal Reasoning Model
claim: Truncating gradients through the first loops helps; text says 2 forward-only loops of 8 is best, though in Table 3 pass@1 is marginally higher at 3 forward-only loops (39.50 vs 39.13).
quote: As shown in Table 5, when the total number of inner loops is fixed to 8, truncating gradients for the first two loops—i.e., running the initial two inner-loop iterations in forward-only mode—achieves the best performance.

title: Universal Reasoning Model
claim: Muon speeds convergence about twofold but does not improve final accuracy.
quote: On ARC-AGI 2, the Muon-optimized model reaches a pass@1 accuracy of 11.5% in approximately 600,000 training steps, whereas the Adamatan2 baseline requires over 1,300,000 steps to achieve the same performance, corresponding to nearly a twofold speedup in optimization.

title: Hierarchical Reasoning Models: Perspectives and Misconceptions
claim: Removing HRM's H-module and using an 8-layer L-module only performs similarly or slightly better than original HRM and trains faster.
quote: The plain transformer/L-module-only setting performs similarly or slightly better than the original HRM while at the same time runs much faster (runtime 1h 48m vs. original HRM’s 4h 21m on a A100 GPU).

title: Hierarchical Reasoning Models: Perspectives and Misconceptions
claim: HRM's one-step gradient training is effectively the diffusion / latent consistency model training paradigm.
quote: Second, the one-step gradient approximation employed by HRM is effectively equivalent to the training paradigm used in diffusion models.

title: Hierarchical Reasoning Models: Perspectives and Misconceptions
claim: Using HRM's learned ACT halting at inference does not improve accuracy; maximum steps is best.
quote: Finally, our analysis indicates that ACT does not enhance inference performance; rather, running the model for the maximum number of reasoning steps yields the best results.

title: Hierarchical Reasoning Models: Perspectives and Misconceptions
claim: Released HRM code trains with ACT halting but evaluates at full maximum steps (train/test mismatch).
quote: There is a critical mismatch in the original HRM implementation: while its ACT module learns to decide when to halt during training, evaluation ignores this policy and always executes the maximum number of reasoning steps.

title: Latent Reasoning in TRMs is Secretly a Policy Improvement Operator
claim: Latent recursion can be formalized as a policy-improvement algorithm, and DIS avoids dead compute, reducing forward passes 18x while maintaining performance.
quote: Using the Tiny Recursive Model as our testbed, we show that with our modifications we can avoid dead compute steps and reduce the total number of forward passes by 18× while maintaining performance.

title: Latent Reasoning in TRMs is Secretly a Policy Improvement Operator
claim: At 0.8M parameters, DIS doubles ARC-AGI-1 pass@2 over a same-size TRM (24.0 vs 12.0).
quote: As a highlight of our method, our model achieves a 24% accuracy on ARC-AGI-1 with 0.8 million parameters, outperform most of the existing open source LLM models without any

title: Latent Reasoning in TRMs is Secretly a Policy Improvement Operator
claim: Re-running TRM with DIS's reduced budget (T=1, n=2) hurts TRM, showing latent steps matter for standard TRM; explicit per-step supervision removes the need for long latent reasoning.
quote: We reduced the total number of latent steps nine times and achieved a significant improvement in performance. However, explicit supervision of each step can overcome this drawback by simplifying the task for the TRM, meaning that longer latent reasoning is unnecessary.

title: Latent Reasoning in TRMs is Secretly a Policy Improvement Operator
claim: Replication of TRM gave slightly lower scores than the original paper.
