quote: Since the points fall below the y = x line, classification performance is better for the untied model than it is for the tied.

title: Understanding Deep Architectures using a Recursive Convolutional Network
claim: At matched parameters and depth, tied and untied models perform about the same despite different widths, so performance is set by parameters and layers.
quote: perform about the same in each case. Thus, performance is determined by the number of parameters and layers, and is insensitive to the number of feature maps.

title: The Remarkable Robustness of LLMs: Stages of Inference?
claim: Without fine-tuning, models keep 72-95% of their top-1 predictions after deleting or swapping adjacent layers.
quote: Surprisingly, models retain 72–95% of their original top-1 prediction accuracy without any fine-tuning.

title: The Remarkable Robustness of LLMs: Stages of Inference?
claim: Middle layers are robust to deletion and reordering, and swapping adjacent layers is less harmful than dropping them; first-layer interventions are catastrophic.
quote: In contrast to the first and last layer interventions, the middle layers are remarkably robust to both deletion and minor order changes.

title: When Do Early-Exit Networks Generalize? A PAC-Bayesian Theory of Adaptive Depth
claim: Generalization of adaptive-depth networks is governed by expected exit depth and exit-depth entropy, not maximum depth.
quote: We prove the first generalization bounds depending on exit-depth entropy H(D) and expected depth E[D] rather than maximum depth K

title: When Do Early-Exit Networks Generalize? A PAC-Bayesian Theory of Adaptive Depth
claim: Bounds are much tighter than classical bounds, and bound-guided exit thresholds nearly match validation-tuned ones.
quote: Experiments across 6 architectures on 7 benchmarks demonstrate tightness ratios of 1.52–3.87× (all p < 0.001) versus >100× for classical bounds.

title: Constant Bit-size Transformers Are Turing Complete
claim: A constant bit-size transformer with a sufficiently long context window simulates any Turing machine, so longer inputs require only a longer window, not more parameters or precision.
quote: We prove that any Turing machine running on inputs of arbitrary length can be simulated by a constant bit-size transformer, as long as the context window is sufficiently long.

title: Constant Bit-size Transformers Are Turing Complete
claim: The expressive power of a constant bit-size transformer with window s(n) is exactly SPACE[s(n)].
quote: Theorem 1. For any non-decreasing function 𝑠 (𝑛) ≥ 𝑛, we have WINDOW [𝑠 (𝑛)] = SPACE [𝑠 (𝑛)]. In particular, WINDOW [ poly (𝑛)] = PSPACE.

title: A Little Depth Goes a Long Way: The Expressive Power of Log-Depth Transformers
claim: Looped transformers whose middle layers repeat Theta(log n) times can recognize regular languages and solve graph connectivity, which fixed-depth transformers cannot under standard conjectures.
quote: We prove that even such highly uniform transformers, when allowed log-depth, can recognize regular languages2 and solve graph connectivity, two important reasoning problems known to be beyond fixed-depth transformers

title: A Little Depth Goes a Long Way: The Expressive Power of Log-Depth Transformers
claim: Scaling depth is more efficient than scaling width (superpolynomial) or CoT steps (superlogarithmic) for these problems.
quote: showed that scaling depth to solve these problems is more efficient than scaling width (which requires superpolynomial increase) or scaling chain-of-thought steps (which requires superlogarithmic increase).

title: A Little Depth Goes a Long Way: The Expressive Power of Log-Depth Transformers
claim: Empirically (with non-looped transformers), effective A5 context length grows exponentially in depth with about 4.8 layers per log token, between the theoretical coefficients for universal (8) and non-uniform (4) transformers.
quote: The empirical slope for the depth relationship is is 4.8 layers per log tokens. This is less than the slope of 8 derived for universal transformers in Theorem 1

title: A Little Depth Goes a Long Way: The Expressive Power of Log-Depth Transformers
claim: Log depth cannot solve P-complete problems unless NC = P.
quote: Unless NC = P, log-depth (or even polylog-depth) transformers cannot express P-complete problems including solving linear equalities

title: TIDE: Token-Informed Depth Execution for Per-Token Early Exit in LLM Inference
claim: On DeepSeek R1 Distill 8B, TIDE cuts prefill latency 7.2% and raises single-batch throughput 6.6%; on Qwen3 8B throughput rises 8.1% at batch size 8.
quote: reduces prefill latency by 7.2%, and increases single-batch throughput by 6.6%.

title: TIDE: Token-Informed Depth Execution for Per-Token Early Exit in LLM Inference
claim: In decoding, the post-hoc mode runs all layers and only selects which layer's output to use, so it gives no wall-clock layer skipping.
quote: T IDE's post-hoc mode runs all layers on every step, selecting only which layer's output to use. This produces correct results and preserves the KV cache, but does not achieve wall-clock layer skipping.

title: Dynamic Rebatching for Efficient Early-Exit Inference with DREX
claim: Existing EE methods give large speedups without batching but marginal or negative gains with batching.
quote: Early Exiting (EE) provides a significant throughput boost of up to 33% for non-batched inference on SOTA frameworks

title: Dynamic Rebatching for Efficient Early-Exit Inference with DREX
claim: DREX improves throughput 2-12% over baselines while eliminating involuntary exits and maintaining quality.
quote: Our evaluation shows that DREX improves throughput by 2-12% compared to baseline approaches while maintaining output quality.

title: Learning to Ponder: Adaptive Reasoning in Latent Space
claim: FR-Ponder variants improve GSM8K accuracy by 3-5 points over CoT and Direct while using fewer tokens.
quote: On GSM8K, FR-P ONDER variants improve accuracy by 3–5 points over standard CoT and Direct baselines, with FP-BoN and FP-Direct delivering the strongest gains.

title: Learning to Ponder: Adaptive Reasoning in Latent Space
claim: Token usage falls 30-40% relative to CoT and BoN.
quote: Across all model scales, FP-BoN and FP-Direct achieve the most pronounced reductions, often cutting token counts by 30–40% relative to standard CoT and BoN.

title: Not All LLM Reasoning is Visible in the Chain-of-Thought
claim: Many frontier models benefit from filler tokens, with accuracy gains up to 13 points depending on token type and model.
quote: We evaluate 13 frontier language models across three tasks and find that many models benefit significantly from filler tokens, with accuracy improvements of up to 13 percentage points.

title: Not All LLM Reasoning is Visible in the Chain-of-Thought
claim: Neither RL nor SFT produced a filler-token benefit that persists at test time.
quote: Reinforcement learning gives Qwen3-235B strong preferences over filler token content, but neither RL nor supervised fine-tuning produces a filler token benefit that persists at test time.

title: Not All LLM Reasoning is Visible in the Chain-of-Thought
claim: Patching early-layer activations recovers most of the filler-type performance gap, indicating the useful signal originates in early layers.
quote: Patching at layers 0–30 recovers over 90% of the performance gap between the two filler types; patching at layers 70 and above yields negative recovery

title: How Transparent is DiffusionGemma?
claim: With an uninterpretable inter-step bottleneck, opaque serial depth is 28.6x the autoregressive Gemma 4; treating the bottleneck as interpretable reduces it to 1.1x.
quote: if we assume that the bottleneck is interpretable, the empirical opaque serial depth upper bound drops to 23, 571 / 21, 235 = 1.1X that of Gemma 4 26B A4B

title: How Transparent is DiffusionGemma?
claim: DiffusionGemma is similarly monitorable to Gemma 4, possibly because reasoning between canvases is autoregressive.
quote: Our main result in Fig. 4 is that monitorability of DiffusionGemma is similar to the monitorability of Gemma.

title: PonderLM-3: Adaptive Token-Wise Pondering with Differentiable Masking
claim: At matched executed additional steps (inference FLOPs proxy) and matched pretraining, PonderLM-3 has lower perplexity than fixed-depth PonderLM-1/2 and LoopedLM.
quote: Figure 3 shows that PonderLM-3 consistently defines a superior Pareto frontier, achieving the lowest perplexity at matched executed compute compared with the fixed-depth and looped baselines.

title: PonderLM-3: Adaptive Token-Wise Pondering with Differentiable Masking
claim: Downstream, PonderLM-3 is competitive with PonderLM-2 (not universally better) at lower inference compute.
quote: Accordingly, Table 2 is not intended to claim universal wins; rather, it shows that our method maintains competitive accuracy under substantially reduced inference compute

title: PonderLM-3: Adaptive Token-Wise Pondering with Differentiable Masking
claim: Increasing the maximum number of pondering steps K from 2 to 5 consistently lowers pretraining loss, with diminishing returns.
quote: Figure 6 shows that increasing 𝐾 consistently lowers pretraining cross-entropy in our setting, suggesting that additional pondering steps provide extra capacity for refining token representations.

title: RRFC: Recursive Refinement via Feedback Conditioning for Iterative Image-to-Image Generation
claim: Feedback refinement gives mixed results: as many significant degradations as improvements, with gains on reconstruction-fidelity tasks and losses on the semantic-layout task.
quote: Across 18 architecture-task settings, RRFC yields seven Holm-corrected improvements, seven degradations, and four non-significant changes.

title: BRAID: Learning Equilibrium Maps in Interdependent Security Games via Weight-Tied Iterative Graph Neural Networks
claim: A single forward pass of the tied iterative GNN replaces iterative best-response computation, up to 43x faster per instance.
quote: replacing iterative best response computation with a single forward pass that is up to 43X faster per instance.

title: Persistent Gaussian Perturbations Prevent Oversmoothing in Recurrent Graph Neural Networks
claim: Persistent noise gives a positive lower bound on stationary Dirichlet energy, preventing asymptotic oversmoothing in deep recurrent message passing.
quote: Our main theoretical result establishes an explicit positive lower bound on the expected stationary Dirichlet energy, proportional to both the noise variance and the spectral gap of the underlying graph.

title: Growing a Neural Network in Breadth, Depth, and Time
claim: Breadth, depth and recurrent time can be traded off against each other to reach a given accuracy, and networks spontaneously take more recurrent steps on occluded inputs.
quote: We find that all three resources can be traded off against each other to achieve a given level of accuracy.

title: Recurrent Sinusoidal INRs for Efficient High-Fidelity Representation
claim: At a fixed parameter budget, increasing recurrent unrolling steps from feed-forward to R=5 improves PSNR.
quote: At optimization step 500, increasing the number of recurrent unrolling steps from a single feed-forward pass to R = 5 improves PSNR

title: Listen, Think, Transcribe: Continuous Latent Test-Time Scaling for ASR
claim: Under minimal data, LatentASR is the only tested adaptation method that reduces WER on both clean benchmarks; dynamic halting keeps most of the gain while skipping about half of utterances.
quote: LatentASR is the only tested method that reduces WER on both clean benchmarks (FLEURS -2.54% and VoxPopuli -0.47% relative).

title: Listen, Think, Transcribe: Continuous Latent Test-Time Scaling for ASR
claim: Forcing all loop steps overshoots: later updates can degrade the transcript, so early halting improves accuracy, not just cost; removing the bounded-delta update is catastrophic.
quote: it truncates the loop before the still-active later steps degrade the transcript.

title: Parallelized Hierarchical Connectome: A Spatiotemporal Recurrent Framework for Spiking State-Space Models
claim: Iterating shared layers within each timestep makes parameter complexity Theta(D^2) versus Theta(D^2 L) for stacked SSMs, and the model is competitive with far larger SSM baselines.
quote: achieving test accuracy competitive with state-of-the-art SSM baselines at 1,312 to 4,891 trainable parameters (1 to 4 orders of magnitude smaller than every baseline).

title: Deep Recurrence for Dynamical Segmentation Models
claim: The feedback model reaches above-random performance with two training examples while the feedforward model needs at least four.
quote: Notably, feedback achieves above random performance with just two training examples, while the feedforward model requires at least four.

title: MazeNet: An Accurate, Fast, and Scalable Deep Learning Solution for Steiner Minimum Trees
claim: Training on mazes with few terminals suffices; larger instances are solved by reusing the same pretrained recurrent blocks, reaching perfect accuracy and lower runtime than exact algorithms.
quote: we only need to train the RCNN blocks on mazes with a small number of terminals; larger mazes can be solved by replicating the same pre-trained blocks to create a larger network.

title: Exploring Learngene via Stage-wise Weight Sharing for Initializing Variable-sized Models
claim: SWS-initialized models beat from-scratch training while reducing total training cost about 6.6x.
quote: Extensive experiments on ImageNet-1K demonstrate that SWS achieves consistent better performance compared to many models trained from scratch, while reducing around 6.6x total training costs.

title: Computing a human-like reaction time metric from stable recurrent vision models
claim: An evidence-accumulation metric over recurrent iterations matches patterns of human reaction times across four tasks.
quote: We demonstrate that our metric aligns with patterns of human reaction times for stimulus manipulations across four disparate visual decision-making tasks

title: Iterative Forward Tuning Boosts In-Context Learning in Language Models
claim: Running multiple forward iterations over demonstrations and refining KV memories improves ICL over a single pass, without training.
quote: This mechanism operates by manipulating the Key-Value matrices without training, fostering enhanced understanding capabilities in LLMs by thinking demonstrations multiple times.

title: Recurrent networks improve neural response prediction and provide insights into underlying cortical circuits
claim: Recurrence acts as an ensemble over effective feedforward paths of varying lengths, which explains its gains.
quote: We propose the recurrent circuit can be conceptualized as a form of ensemble computing, with each iteration generating more effective feedforward paths of various path lengths

title: ReSet: Learning Recurrent Dynamic Routing in ResNet-like Neural Networks
claim: Dynamic per-input selection of units from a shared pool beats the original ResNet-38 on CIFAR-10.1.
quote: We compare our model to ResNet-38 architecture and achieve better results than the original ResNet on CIFAR-10.1 test set.

title: State-Denoised Recurrent Neural Networks
claim: Multiple internal attractor steps per sequence step with a denoising loss improve generalization over a generic RNN and over the same model without the auxiliary loss.
quote: On a range of tasks, we show that the SDRNN outperforms a generic RNN as well as a variant of the SDRNN with attractor dynamics on the hidden state but without the auxillary loss.

title: Recurrent Residual Convolutional Neural Network based on U-Net (R2U-Net) for Medical Image Segmentation
claim: Recurrent residual conv layers give better segmentation than U-Net at the same number of parameters.
quote: it allows us to design better U-Net architecture with same number of network parameters with better performance for medical image segmentation.

title: Implicit Feature Refinement for Instance Segmentation
claim: An implicit weight-tied refinement block improves Mask R-CNN mask AP by about 1% with 30% of the mask-head parameters.
quote: Experiments on the COCO and YouTube-VIS benchmarks show that our IFR achieves improved performance on state-of-the-art image/video instance segmentation frameworks, while reducing the parameter burden

title: Implicit Feature Refinement for Instance Segmentation
claim: The usual four consecutive (untied) convolutions are unnecessary; weight-sharing blocks are competitive.
quote: which reveals that the widely-used four consecutive convolutions are not necessary. As an alternative, weight-sharing convolution blocks provides competitive performance.

title: Energy-Aware Deep Learning on GPUs through Parameter Sharing and Mixed Precision Training
claim: Parameter sharing (ALBERT) is slower and more memory-hungry in training than a conventional smaller model, because unrolled depth creates many activations.
quote: ALBERT is empirically up to 2.2× slower and triggers up to ~ 3× higher GPU memory footprint than DistilBERT

title: Deep Residual Weight-Sharing Attention Network With Low-Rank Attention for Visual Question Answering
claim: A fully weight-tied stack of attention layers is competitive with much fewer parameters than state-of-the-art VQA models.
quote: Experiments on VQA-v2, GQA, and CLEVR datasets show that the RWSAN achieves competitive performance with much fewer parameters over the state-of-the-art methods.

title: Memory-efficient Model Growth for Finetuning Automatic Speech Recognition Models
claim: Duplicating weight-shared layers with LoRA yields 10% relative improvement over the baseline at the same parameter budget.
quote: Our experiments on Dutch ASR demonstrate a 10% relative improvement over the baseline with the same parameter budget.

title: TranIU-Net: Indicative Electrical Tomography Imaging Based on Implicit Unrolling Transformer
claim: An implicit mapping guarantees convergence through a fixed point at unlimited depth with constant memory.
quote: Using only constant memory cost, the implicit mapping is analytically built to guarantee the convergence through the fixed-point at unlimited depth.

title: Recurrent Neural Networks With Intra-Frame Iterations for Video Deblurring
claim: Training with randomly chosen iteration counts makes fewer-iteration models partial computational paths of more-iteration ones, enabling compute-accuracy trade-offs.
quote: At training time, we randomly choose the iteration number on the fly and apply a regularization loss that favors less computation unless there are considerable reconstruction gains.

title: HyperPolypDEQ: A Lightning Transformer-Based Deep Equilibrium Model for Colon Polyp Segmentation
claim: A learned solver gives about 9x faster DEQ inference with similar accuracy.
quote: Experimental results show that our new models using Hyper-Solver can achieve similar results to existing DEQ models on several benchmark medical image datasets while having a significant speedup in inference time (about 9 times).

title: IDiffPose: Equilibrium Substitution for Lightweight Diffusion-Graph-Based Pose Estimation
claim: Substituting only the middle block with a weight-tied equilibrium operator improves accuracy with far fewer trainable parameters.
quote: On Human3.6M, substituting only the middle block improves MPJPE from 31.55 to 31.10 mm and P-MPJPE from 24.72 to 24.47 mm with 167,521 trainable parameters (vs. 1,025,674 explicit)

title: Stable and expressive recurrent vision models
claim: BPTT-trained recurrent CNNs diverge after the trained number of steps, while LCP-trained (contractive) models stay at a task-informative steady state.
quote: BPTT-trained model dynamics diverge when t > N , but models trained with LCP did not.

title: Stable and expressive recurrent vision models
claim: A 20-step C-RBP hGRU nearly matches BPTT on Pathfinder-14 using about half the memory.
quote: This model performs nearly as well as both BPTT and C-BPTT trained hGRUs (0.95 IoU), despite using approximately half the memory of either.

title: Stable and expressive recurrent vision models
claim: Recurrent panoptic heads trained with C-RBP improve with more steps and beat the feedforward FPN-ResNet-50 with fewer parameters.
quote: Importantly, each of these R-FPN-ResNet-50 models was more accurate than the feedforward FPN-ResNet-50 despite using 783,552 fewer parameters.

title: Is One Layer Enough? Understanding Inference Dynamics in Tabular Foundation Models
claim: A single block looped six times matches the compute of the 6-layer model with the parameter count of the 1-layer model, and performs almost identically to the 6-layer model, while the unlooped 1-layer model is clearly worse.
quote: We highlight that nanoTabPFN looped matches the computational complexity of nanoTabPFN 6l while retaining only the number of parameters of nanoTabPFN 1l .

title: Is One Layer Enough? Understanding Inference Dynamics in Tabular Foundation Models
claim: Depth in tabular foundation models mainly implements iterative computation, so recurrent reuse of one block gives comparable performance.
quote: This supports the view that depth in TFMs primarily facilitates iterative computation rather than learning fundamentally distinct transformations at each layer

title: Is One Layer Enough? Understanding Inference Dynamics in Tabular Foundation Models
claim: In pretrained TFMs, skipping early layers is catastrophic while middle and late layers can be skipped with little loss; repeating some layers gives slight gains in LimiX-16M and TabPFN(v1).
quote: Repeating certain layers results in slight performance improvements for models such as LimiX-16M and TabPFN(v1), supporting the idea of iterative refinement.

title: Is One Layer Enough? Understanding Inference Dynamics in Tabular Foundation Models
claim: The authors flag the looped result as small-scale with a gap to state-of-the-art TFMs.
quote: However, we note that our experiments were conducted at a small scale, and there remains a performance gap compared to state-of-the-art models such as TabPFN(2.5).

title: Parallel Loop Transformer for Efficient Test-Time Computation Scaling
claim: Sequential looping roughly doubles decode latency and KV memory at L=2; CLP keeps accuracy and cuts latency 37% vs naive loop at bs=4.
quote: Adding CLP at the same loop count (row (3)) keeps the accuracy nearly unchanged (39.7→39.6, −0.1), while it cuts latency from 9.4 ms to 5.9 ms (−37%) by parallelizing loop computation.

title: Parallel Loop Transformer for Efficient Test-Time Computation Scaling
claim: Sharing the first loop's KV cache halves KV memory but costs 3.4 average points; gated SWA recovers it with 1.4% extra KV.
quote: Adding G-SWA (row (5)) restores per-loop specificity using a local window, raising accuracy from 36.2 to 39.7 (+3.5) while adding only 1.4% KV-cache overhead (280M→284M) and nearly no latency penalty (4.8→4.9 ms).

title: Parallel Loop Transformer for Efficient Test-Time Computation Scaling
claim: PLT-2 latency advantage over naive looping holds across batch sizes; overhead vs vanilla grows modestly at large batch as decoding becomes less memory-bound.
quote: Overall, PLT -2 reduces latency by 47% compared to naive looping across batch sizes and remains within 4–6% of vanilla for practical serving (bs ≥ 32).

title: Parallel Loop Transformer for Efficient Test-Time Computation Scaling
claim: At matched accuracy, a shallower PLT-2 (1.7B/40B) beats a deeper vanilla MoE (2.5B/60B) by 0.5 avg points with about 30% lower latency and two-thirds the KV cache.
quote: The 1.7B/40B MoE model with P LT and two loops delivers about 30% lower latency than the vanilla 2.5B/60B MoE model.

title: Parallel Loop Transformer for Efficient Test-Time Computation Scaling
claim: The latency advantage relies on decoding being memory-bound; extra loop FLOPs are hidden, not removed.
quote: Compared with a standard non-loop decoder, it adds FLOPs that improve accuracy, yet the latency increase is negligible because decoding is memory-bound [44].

title: Efficient Parallel Samplers for Recurrent-Depth Models and Their Connection to Diffusion Language Models
claim: Diffusion-forcing sampler gives about 4.4-4.8x tokens/s over static AR r=32 at batch size 1 with small accuracy changes (GSM8K +0.31, HumanEval -2.44).
quote: We find that on all benchmarks, executing the parallelized sampler leads to significant speedups of around 5x, with only minor trade-offs in generation quality of around 1%, depending on the task

title: Efficient Parallel Samplers for Recurrent-Depth Models and Their Connection to Diffusion Language Models
claim: The sampler does not reduce FLOPs; speedup comes from exploiting GPU parallelism in memory-bound decoding (FLOPs are actually higher than AR per token).
quote: While this approach does not reduce FLOPs, it effectively exploits modern GPU architectures by unlocking additional opportunities for parallelization.

title: Efficient Parallel Samplers for Recurrent-Depth Models and Their Connection to Diffusion Language Models
claim: Huginn-0125 supports cross-recurrence KV sharing (cache of latest recurrence only) matching baseline GSM8K accuracy with r-times less KV memory.
quote: As shown in Figure 3, the trained Huginn-0125 model inherently supports KV cache sharing, allowing us to store only the KV state of the most recent recurrence for each token position

title: Efficient Parallel Samplers for Recurrent-Depth Models and Their Connection to Diffusion Language Models
claim: Diffusion sampler beats tuned self-speculative decoding (which itself is about 1.9x over static AR on GSM8K).
quote: Show that diffusion forcing sampling outperforms even well-tuned speculative decoding baselines for the same model with speed gains that can be smoothly traded off against accuracy.

title: Efficient Parallel Samplers for Recurrent-Depth Models and Their Connection to Diffusion Language Models
claim: Requirements for the sampler: input injection and intermediate states decodable to approximately correct outputs; models trained with a fixed recurrence count may fail.
quote: While this property is generally satisfied, it may fail in models trained exclusively with a fixed number of recurrences r, where decoding from earlier steps can yield nonsensical outputs

title: The Surprising Effectiveness of Shared Memory in Looped Transformers
claim: Memory sharing improves quality over a matched-depth looped baseline while reducing KV memory 2.0-4.7x with under 1% more FLOPs.
quote: At matched size and recursion count, LPT lowers validation perplexity by 0.38–1.09 and raises accuracy by 0.4–4.8 percentage points over LT, with 2.0–4.7× less KV memory and under 1% more FLOPs (Table 1).

title: The Surprising Effectiveness of Shared Memory in Looped Transformers
claim: Hybrid H-LPT beats a same-size standard Transformer while using 76-79% less context memory at five recursions.
quote: H - LPT lowers perplexity by 1.12–1.82 and raises accuracy by 3.1–5.6 points with 76–79% less memory.

title: The Surprising Effectiveness of Shared Memory in Looped Transformers
claim: Shared cache saves memory not time: at equal batch LPT is 3-8% slower than LT, and looped decoding at batch 1 is 2.3-5.7x slower than STD.
quote: At equal batch, LPT is 3–8% slower than LT, since each later recursion still reads the whole shared cache, and its own window too.

title: The Surprising Effectiveness of Shared Memory in Looped Transformers
claim: Throughput gains come only through larger batches: LPT peak throughput 7-91% above LT.
quote: The larger batches raise LPT’s peak throughput above LT’s by 7–91%, most at L with five recursions, where LT fits only 21 sequences.

title: The Surprising Effectiveness of Shared Memory in Looped Transformers
claim: Untrained first-recursion-only KV reuse hurts Ouro, so the benefit of sharing requires training it in; the paper argues sharing is an inductive bias, not just a cost.
quote: Keeping only the first recursion’s cache sharply reduces Ouro’s quality, which suggests that shared memory has to be trained.

title: The Surprising Effectiveness of Shared Memory in Looped Transformers
claim: Shared memory acts as a gradient highway; detaching shared-KV gradients raises perplexity and makes deeper models fail to train.
quote: To test whether this highway helps learning, we train LPT from scratch with shared KV detached at later reads.

title: FlashLoop: Fast and Memory-Efficient Looped Transformers via Lazy Updates
claim: Training-free FlashLoop gives up to 1.64x end-to-end speedup and up to 6x KV memory reduction while largely preserving accuracy.
quote: FlashLoop retains the parameter efficiency of looped Transformers and largely preserves their accuracy, while delivering up to 1.64× end-to-end speedup and reducing KV-cache memory by up to 6×.

title: FlashLoop: Fast and Memory-Efficient Looped Transformers via Lazy Updates
claim: Looped models have large practical overhead vs dense: Ouro-2.6B (4 loops) prefill of 32K is 27 s vs 3 s for LLaMA-3.1-8B and KV 48 GiB vs 4 GiB.
quote: On a single A100 machine, the prefill time for a 32K-token prompt is 27 seconds for Ouro-2.6B (Zhu et al., 2025) with four loops, compared with only 3 seconds for LLaMA-3.1-8B

title: FlashLoop: Fast and Memory-Efficient Looped Transformers via Lazy Updates
claim: Quantizing cross-loop KV residuals is more accurate than quantizing full KV per loop (KIVI4 per-loop gives larger drop).
quote: This alternative leads to a noticeably larger accuracy degradation, consistent with our observation in Section 3.3 that cross-loop KV residuals are more quantization-friendly than full KV states.

title: FlashLoop: Fast and Memory-Efficient Looped Transformers via Lazy Updates
claim: Savings grow with context length and loop count; at 32K, KV storage cut by 20 GiB (82.8%).
quote: At 32K context length, FlashLoop reduces KV-cache storage by 20 GiB, corresponding to an 82.8% reduction, while achieving a significant speedup in prefill and decode.

title: FlashLoop: Fast and Memory-Efficient Looped Transformers via Lazy Updates
claim: Thinking variants are more sensitive to cross-loop compression than base models.
quote: base models tend to be more robust to FlashLoop than their thinking counterparts, suggesting that thinking models may be more sensitive to cross-loop compression.

title: Shallow Queries, Mature Values: Depth-Asynchronous Self-Speculation
claim: DAS-Wave reaches 4.00-6.96x mean throughput speedup over paired full-depth AR across four checkpoints and four tasks, the best in all 16 settings.
quote: DAS-Wave achieves 4.00–6.96× throughput speedup over paired fulldepth AR and obtains the largest measured speedup in all sixteen settings.

title: Shallow Queries, Mature Values: Depth-Asynchronous Self-Speculation
claim: Values mature later than queries and keys across recurrent depth, so full-depth prefix V most improves shallow drafts.
quote: At draft depth r = 1, replacing prefix V with its full-depth counterpart raises Huginn’s draft–target agreement from 47.22% to 66.93%, whereas replacing K alone gives 46.83%.

title: Shallow Queries, Mature Values: Depth-Asynchronous Self-Speculation

title: Shallow Queries, Mature Values: Depth-Asynchronous Self-Speculation
claim: More refinement compute per round increases accepted length but lowers speed; acceptance length is not a sufficient proxy for speedup.
quote: For Huginn, increasing recurrent updates per refinement round from 2 to 8 raises A from 16.49 to 19.56, but reduces speedup from 4.33× to 2.37×.

title: Shallow Queries, Mature Values: Depth-Asynchronous Self-Speculation
claim: Lossless under greedy decoding: verification rule unchanged so outputs equal target AR in exact arithmetic.
quote: Because DAS modifies only proposal construction and prefix reads while leaving the target computation and verification rule unchanged, greedy target preservation follows the standard speculative-decoding argument in exact arithmetic

title: LoopCD: Loop-wise Contrastive Decoding for Improving Reasoning in Looped Language Models
claim: Contrasting early-loop and final-loop logits improves LoopLM reasoning without training and with negligible overhead.
quote: We find that this strategy is highly efficient, introducing only negligible inference overhead and requiring no additional training, while effectively improving reasoning performance by naturally refining reasoning-critical hard tokens.

title: LoopCD: Loop-wise Contrastive Decoding for Improving Reasoning in Looped Language Models
claim: Hard tokens with early overconfidence then revision make up 10-15% of reasoning traces and drive errors.
quote: these hard tokens usually result in high-entropy distributions, and they account for about 10%–15% of the reasoning trace

title: LoopCD: Loop-wise Contrastive Decoding for Improving Reasoning in Looped Language Models
claim: An amateur loop at roughly 15-30% of recurrence depth works best.
quote: choosing an early loop, roughly 15–30% of the recurrence depth, often works well across tasks and models.

quote: DT networks with recall on average solve 90.27% of 512-bit test samples when trained with the n = 0 loss, and with randomly sampled values of n, as described in Algorithm 1, they achieve 97.12% accuracy

title: Chain-of-Thought and Compressed Looped Transformers: A Memory-Budget Separation
claim: Theorem 4.2: a compressed latent loop with s slots, width d, precision p, T iterations (log precision, logspace-uniform) is simulable in deterministic space O(sdp + log n + log T); with polylog state and quasi-polynomial T it is a polylog-space machine.
quote: In particular, if s d p = polylog(n) and log T = polylog(n) (e.g. for polynomially many iterations), then CLL ⊆ DSPACE(polylogn).

title: Chain-of-Thought and Compressed Looped Transformers: A Memory-Budget Separation
claim: Theorem 4.4: assuming P is not contained in DSPACE(polylog n), no logspace-uniform compressed loop with polylog persistent state and log T = polylog(n) decides a P-complete language, whereas polynomial-length CoT can.
quote: Under a standard complexity assumption, such loops cannot decide problems that are P-complete under logspace reductions, whereas polynomiallength chain-of-thought can.

title: Chain-of-Thought and Compressed Looped Transformers: A Memory-Budget Separation
claim: The separation does not apply to standard looped transformers that carry a hidden vector at every position (sequence-state loops) or that append padding/scratch positions; these are memory-rich, consistent with prior universality and CoT-simulation results.
quote: The separation is specific to compressed loops, as full sequence-state loops carry state at every input position and live in a memory-rich regime closer to explicit scratchpads.

title: Chain-of-Thought and Compressed Looped Transformers: A Memory-Budget Separation
claim: Finite-size probe: in k-concurrent pointer chasing, compressed loops with fewer slots than chains (s < k) collapse while the sequence-state control is essentially saturated; above threshold, success is seed-dependent.
quote: In the subdiagonal regime s < k the collapse is robust, with mean cell accuracy 0.041 and maximum cell-mean 0.129.

title: Exploration of Fast-Slow Latent Recurrence for Train-Short, Test-Long Generalization
claim: Trained on Dyck sequences up to length 40, FSRM keeps about 80% token accuracy up to length 10^5, three orders of magnitude beyond training.
quote: our model of this family, trained on sequences of length ≤ 40, maintains ≈ 80% token accuracy up to length 105 , three orders of magnitude beyond training

title: Exploration of Fast-Slow Latent Recurrence for Train-Short, Test-Long Generalization
claim: Weight sharing in the inner loop matters: at the same inner budget T=5 the shared loop beats an unshared 5-layer stack with about twice the parameters, and a 10-layer stack is worse still.
quote: With the same inner-loop budget (T = 5), the shared recurrent loop reaches roughly 61% OOD accuracy, whereas the unshared 5-layer stack drops to about 51%, despite using roughly twice as many parameters.

title: Exploration of Fast-Slow Latent Recurrence for Train-Short, Test-Long Generalization
claim: Static-input looped models without the persistent fast-slow mechanism, including looped Transformers, do not show the OOD generalization.
quote: models without this persistent fast–slow mechanism, including looped Transformers, do not exhibit OOD generalization

title: DART: Distributional Adversarial Recurrent Training for Algorithm Learning
claim: On 31x31 mazes (trained on 9x9), CE training is unstable across seeds while DART reaches near-perfect peak and final accuracy.
quote: DART removes most of this sensitivity, reaching 99.91 ± 0.13% peak and final accuracy at 31 × 31.

title: DART: Distributional Adversarial Recurrent Training for Algorithm Learning
claim: On chess, CE peaks then collapses with more iterations (overthinking); progressive training removes the collapse and progressive DART gives the best final accuracy, so the two address complementary failure modes.
quote: Progressive DART inherits the same long-horizon stability while retaining a distributional objective, achieving the best final accuracy, 83.52 ± 0.16%.

title: DART: Distributional Adversarial Recurrent Training for Algorithm Learning
claim: For TRM on Sudoku trained with 20% masking, DART's gain over CE grows with the distribution shift.
quote: at depth 56, the gain is 0.5% at 30% masking, 3.3% at 40%, and 5.6% at 50%

title: Loom: A Scalable Analytical Neural Computer Architecture
claim: A fixed-weight 8-layer transformer, iterated, executes any program compiled from a C subset to a 22-opcode ISA, with fixed per-step cost independent of program length or history.
quote: The full machine state resides in a single tensor X ∈ Rd×n of fixed size, and every step has fixed cost for fixed d and n, independent of program length or execution history.

title: Loom: A Scalable Analytical Neural Computer Architecture
claim: Extends Giannou et al. from one opcode to 22 opcodes while reducing depth.
quote: Their construction uses 10 transformer layers for this single instruction. We extend this result from 1 opcode in 10 layers to 22 opcodes in 8 layers.

title: Loom: A Scalable Analytical Neural Computer Architecture
claim: All compiled-program correctness tests pass and match an independent ISA interpreter.
quote: We ran 50 end-to-end compiled-program tests including Fibonacci, GCD by subtraction, array minimum, nested conditionals, variable-index LOAD/STORE round-trips, and multi-iteration loops (up to 1000 ISA steps). All 50 tests pass.

title: Statistical Gains from Looped Estimation under Parameter Budgets
claim: At a sufficiently large fixed budget, the looped estimator's worst-case risk vanishes as n grows, whereas every estimator in the untied family under the same budget has risk bounded away from zero.
quote: At sufficiently large fixed budgets, looped worst-case risk vanishes while optimal worst-case untied risk remains bounded away from zero.

title: Statistical Gains from Looped Estimation under Parameter Budgets
claim: Looped residual FFNs and post-LN Transformers attain the minimax polynomial rate for Hölder targets up to log factors with a fixed number of bounded real parameters.
quote: looped residual feedforward networks and postlayer-normalized Transformers attain the minimax polynomial rate up to logarithmic factors with a fixed number of bounded real parameters

title: Statistical Gains from Looped Estimation under Parameter Budgets
claim: More loops trade approximation error for estimation complexity: iterations improve the approximation bound without adding parameters but increase computation and fitted-class complexity; the separation regime needs T_n/B_n to infinity, i.e. much more compute than the untied stack.
quote: In the separation regime, Tn /Bn → ∞, whereas untied depth is at most O(Bn ); a dense residual FFN loop uses order Bn Tn parameter-associated operations per forward pass

title: Statistical Gains from Looped Estimation under Parameter Budgets
claim: Empirically at cap B = 128, the looped residual FFN has the smallest mean regression MSE on all three synthetic families.
quote: At the prespecified cap B = 128, Loop has the smallest mean MSE for all three families (Table S1).

title: Universal Transformers for Circuit Computations: Perfect Length Generalization in Tiny Transformers
claim: Theorems 1-2: the constructed single-layer looped transformer evaluates any valid fully-parenthesized Boolean expression of depth d exactly in d iterations and halts autonomously.
quote: Combined with an autonomous halting criterion, the model terminates after d iterations for problems of depth d, yielding O(n · d) total complexity.

title: Universal Transformers for Circuit Computations: Perfect Length Generalization in Tiny Transformers
claim: Trained from random initialization on depth 1-2 only, the architecture reaches 100% accuracy at every test depth from 3 to 30.
quote: We achieved 100% generalization accuracy on all 3 tasks by training models from random initialization on depth 1 and 2 problems, and evaluating 100 problems at each depth from 3-30.

title: Universal Transformers for Circuit Computations: Perfect Length Generalization in Tiny Transformers
claim: A standard weight-shared looped transformer with learned, RoPE or FIRE positional encodings, given the ground-truth depth, fits training depths but collapses toward chance out of distribution.
quote: Every trained model still collapses toward chance out of distribution, whereas our construction remains exact.

title: Stabilizing Extrapolation in Looped Transformers via Learned Stochastic Stopping
claim: Looped transformers show extrapolation potential on binary addition but it is unreliable: runs with similar ID accuracy diverge OOD, with much larger variance than fixed-depth transformers.
quote: the OOD standard deviation is only 0.009 and 0.005 for the 3-layer and 60-layer Transformer baselines, but rises to 0.087 for Looped Transformers with fixed K = 20 and 0.122 for Looped Transformers with K = n

title: Stabilizing Extrapolation in Looped Transformers via Learned Stochastic Stopping
claim: The variance is traced to the spurious correlation between sequence length and number of loops; randomizing loop count during training reduces OOD variance and stabilizes predictions across inference-time loop counts.
quote: We trace this variance to the spurious correlation in simple algorithmic tasks between sequence length and number of loops.

title: Stabilizing Extrapolation in Looped Transformers via Learned Stochastic Stopping
claim: Stochastic schedules stabilize rather than monotonically improve accuracy: OOD accuracy improves from deterministic to +-5 window but decreases at +-10.
quote: Central OOD performance improves from the deterministic schedule to the ±5 window, but decreases again for the ±10 window.

title: Stabilizing Extrapolation in Looped Transformers via Learned Stochastic Stopping
claim: RL-Halting gives best OOD accuracy and lowest std on three of four tasks, but on Copy it stabilizes a worse computation.
quote: Across binary addition, Dyck-1, Unique Set, and Copy, learned stochastic stopping often improves this trade-off but can also stabilize a suboptimal computation.

title: Transformers Efficiently Perform In-Context Logistic Regression via Normalized Gradient Descent
claim: An L-layer softmax transformer can exactly implement L steps of normalized gradient descent on the in-context logistic (exponential) loss.
quote: under appropriate parameterizations, the outputs of softmax attention layers exactly match the iterates of normalized gradient descent applied to the in-context loss

title: Transformers Efficiently Perform In-Context Logistic Regression via Normalized Gradient Descent
claim: The construction is reachable by training one layer with a one-step GD teacher and then looping it; the looped model gets an OOD generalization guarantee.
quote: we show that our constructed transformer can be obtained through (i) training a single self-attention layer supervised by one-step gradient descent, and (ii) recurrently applying the trained layer to obtain a looped model

title: Transformers Efficiently Perform In-Context Logistic Regression via Normalized Gradient Descent
claim: Error of the looped model decays as O(log n / (alpha L)) in depth plus a statistical term, so more loops reduce the implicit-bias error.
quote: Theorem 4.7 shows that its prediction error is controlled by the implicit-bias error from Corollary 4.3 and the finite-sample statistical error of the in-context maximum-margin solution.

title: Fixed-Point RNNs: Interpolating from Diagonal to Dense
claim: Fixed-point iteration of a diagonal RNN lets a model trade parallelism for expressivity at a fixed number of parameters and reach state-of-the-art state-tracking accuracy.
quote: The resulting models can naturally trade expressivity for efficiency at a fixed number of parameters and achieve state-of-the-art results on the state-tracking benchmarks A5 and S5 , while matching performance on copying and other tasks.

title: Fixed-Point RNNs: Interpolating from Diagonal to Dense
claim: FP-RNNs adapt computation time to task difficulty by varying the number of fixed-point iterations; on simpler tasks the model effectively falls back to O(T) cost.
quote: This suggests that the model adapts to O(T ) complexity on simpler tasks when the full state-tracking expressivity is not required.

title: Fixed-Point RNNs: Interpolating from Diagonal to Dense
claim: The effective number of iterations adapts to difficulty: far fewer than sequence length on copying, modular arithmetic and language pretraining.
quote: Fig. 7 shows that the model automatically adapts to using less fixed-point iterations on language pretraining at context length 2048.

title: On the Reasoning Abilities of Masked Diffusion Language Models
claim: In the finite-precision log-width setting, masked diffusion models and polynomially padded looped transformers are equivalent, and MDMs can solve everything CoT transformers can.
quote: We show that MDMs and polynomially-padded PLTs are, in fact, equivalent in this setting, and that MDMs can solve all problems that CoT-augmented transformers can.

title: On the Reasoning Abilities of Masked Diffusion Language Models
claim: Padded looped transformers (and MDMs) with constantly many steps and polynomial padding equal L-uniform AC0; more loops (log^d N) raise expressivity to L-uniform AC^d, approaching NC with polylog loops.
quote: we get that with polylogarithmic looping and polynomial padding, MDMs converge to NC, the class of all parallelizable problems

title: On the Reasoning Abilities of Masked Diffusion Language Models
claim: With logarithmically many steps, CoT transformers stay in TC0 while MDMs (hence PLTs with linear padding) recognize all regular languages including NC1-complete ones, a strict separation under TC0 != NC1.
quote: While CoT transformers remain in TC0 , MDMs can solve NC1 -complete problems.

title: Unlocking Out-of-Distribution Generalization in Transformers via Recursive Latent Space Reasoning
claim: CoT-trained transformers generalize only modestly beyond training size (to about 40 nodes from <= 32) and degrade rapidly.
quote: While the best-performing CoT models exhibit a limited degree of OOD generalization to moderately larger graphs (N ≤ 32 ; N ≈ 40), this capability rapidly deteriorates as graph sizes exceed the training regime.

title: Unlocking Out-of-Distribution Generalization in Transformers via Recursive Latent Space Reasoning
claim: With all four mechanisms, the recurrent model achieves near-perfect performance on all OOD splits, i.e. on graphs several times larger than training.
quote: When all proposed ingredients are incorporated, i.e., Discrete Latent Space Supervision ⟲1 , the model robustly achieves near-perfect performance across all OOD splits we examined.

title: Unlocking Out-of-Distribution Generalization in Transformers via Recursive Latent Space Reasoning
claim: Continuous latent recurrence degrades with more recurrent depth because noise accumulates and representations drift; discretizing and re-embedding between iterations anchors states and fixes this.
quote: We attribute this to accumulating noise in the continuous vector representations — a phenomenon exacerbated when scaling test-time compute for larger problem instances — which eventually causes representations to drift

title: Enhancing Auto-regressive Chain-of-Thought through Loop-Aligned Reasoning
claim: Within training lengths both models are perfect, but beyond them the autoregressive CoT model deteriorates while the looped transformer stays better at all lengths.
quote: While the auto-regressive CoT Transformer’s performance deteriorates significantly, the looped Transformer maintains superior performance across all length regimes.

title: Enhancing Auto-regressive Chain-of-Thought through Loop-Aligned Reasoning
claim: Supervising each loop iteration with the corresponding CoT step preserves and even improves the looped model's length generalization.
quote: This additional iteration-wise supervision not only preserves the Looped Transformer’s ability for length generalization but also enables it to predict CoT reasoning steps for unseen data.

title: Enhancing Auto-regressive Chain-of-Thought through Loop-Aligned Reasoning
claim: Fine-tuning the autoregressive model on looped-model-generated long CoT chains significantly improves it beyond the original training length, approaching the looped model.
quote: the auto-regressive CoT model fine-tuned with data generated by RELAY (i.e., by the looped model with explicit CoT alignment) exhibits significant improvements on problems exceeding the original training length

title: A Formal Comparison Between Chain of Thought and Latent Thought
claim: Latent thought with log^k n iterations exactly captures TC^k (log precision) / AC^k, while CoT with log^k n steps is upper-bounded by TC^{k-1}, so latent thought is strictly more efficient on parallelizable problems under standard assumptions.
quote: We show that latent thought with logk n iterations exactly captures the power of TCk (Thm. 3.12); in contrast, CoT with logk n steps cannot realize the full power of TCk (Thm. 3.13) due to its inherent sequentiality.

title: A Formal Comparison Between Chain of Thought and Latent Thought
claim: CoT with stochastic decoding admits approximate counting (FPRAS) and approximate uniform sampling that deterministic latent thought with polynomially many iterations cannot, the first formal separation in favor of CoT.
quote: there exist target distributions that CoT can approximately represent and sample from, but that remain inaccessible to latent thought (Theorem 4.4). To the best of our knowledge, this constitutes the first formal separation in favor of CoT.

title: A Formal Comparison Between Chain of Thought and Latent Thought
claim: Empirically, looped transformers solve parallelizable tasks with fewer iterations than CoT needs, and the loops needed grow only logarithmically with input size.
quote: as the input size n increases, the number of loops required to maintain high accuracy grows only logarithmically, supporting our theoretical claim in the (poly-)logarithmic regime

title: A Formal Comparison Between Chain of Thought and Latent Thought
claim: On graph-coloring sampling, CoT covers valid colorings more uniformly than the looped model, which concentrates mass on fewer solutions.
quote: uniform, whereas the looped model concentrates probability mass on a smaller subset of solutions. This indicates that CoT achieves more uniform coverage of the valid colorings.

title: On Expressive Power of Looped Transformers: Theoretical Analysis and Enhancement via Timestep Encoding
claim: Theorem 3.6 / Corollary 3.7: single-layer looped transformers with fixed width (two heads, head size 1, width O(d)) universally approximate continuous permutation-equivariant seq2seq functions, with error decreasing as loop count r grows (under infinite-precision weights).
quote: Theorem 3.6 shows that increasing the number of loops r reduces the approximation error. Under infinite-precision weights, this leads to a universal approximation theorem.

title: On Expressive Power of Looped Transformers: Theoretical Analysis and Enhancement via Timestep Encoding
claim: The rate contains two additional moduli of continuity beyond the ReLU-network case, an error amplification intrinsic to weight tying; timestep-dependent scaling per loop removes it.
quote: The approximation rate in Theorem 3.6 includes two additional moduli of continuity, which can lead to increased errors, reflecting a limitation inherent to Looped Transformers.

title: On Expressive Power of Looped Transformers: Theoretical Analysis and Enhancement via Timestep Encoding
claim: Empirically, more loops improve reasoning-task accuracy, higher loop counts significantly outperform standard transformers, and timestep encoding adds further gains.
quote: The results in Table 2 demonstrate that increasing the number of loops improves performance on reasoning tasks, with higher loop counts significantly outperforming standard Transformers.

title: Looped ReLU MLPs May Be All You Need as Practical Programmable Computers
claim: A looped 23-layer ReLU-MLP with width n can emulate a programmable computer (SUBLEQ OISC), so attention is not necessary for looped universality.
quote: we provide an aﬃrmative answer that a looped 23-layer ReLU-MLP is capable of performing the basic necessary operations, more eﬃciently and eﬀectively functioning as a programmable computer than a looped Transformer

title: Looped ReLU MLPs May Be All You Need as Practical Programmable Computers
claim: With low-rank decomposition each forward pass costs O(n log n) versus O(n^2) for the looped transformer construction.
quote: each forward pass of our 23-layer ReLU-MLP only takes O(n log n) time complexity, while looped Transformer in [GRS+ 23] takes O(n2 ) time complexity for each forward pass

title: Can Looped Transformers Learn to Implement Multi-step Gradient Descent for In-context Learning?
claim: The global minimizer of the population loss for a linear looped transformer with L loops implements L steps of preconditioned gradient descent with a data-adapted preconditioner.
quote: we show that the global minimizer of the population training loss implements multi-step preconditioned gradient descent, with a preconditioner that adapts to the data distribution

title: Can Looped Transformers Learn to Implement Multi-step Gradient Descent for In-context Learning?
claim: Gradient flow converges fast despite non-convexity, the first such convergence result beyond one-layer transformers in this setting.
quote: we show a fast convergence for gradient flow on the regression loss, despite the non-convexity of the landscape, by proving a novel gradient dominance condition

title: Can Looped Transformers Learn to Implement Multi-step Gradient Descent for In-context Learning?
claim: Empirically, a 1-layer model looped L times performs similarly to an L-layer model, and models trained with few loops keep improving when looped more at test time, ID and OOD.
quote: For looped models trained with just few loops (2, or 5), evaluating with more loops keeps improving the loss in both cases, suggesting that it learned the correct iterative algorithm.

title: On Logical Extrapolation for Mazes with Recurrent and Implicit Networks
claim: Models that extrapolate in maze size fail in various ways under other difficulty shifts; whether they learned an algorithm remains uncertain.
quote: By varying test data along multiple axes — not just maze size — we show that models introduced in prior work fail in a variety of ways, some expected and others less so.

title: On Logical Extrapolation for Mazes with Recurrent and Implicit Networks
claim: Training on more diverse data (mazes with cycles) improves accuracy on cycles but paradoxically does not improve logical extrapolation.
quote: We show that training these models on more diverse data addresses some failure modes but, paradoxically, does not improve logical extrapolation.

title: On Logical Extrapolation for Mazes with Recurrent and Implicit Networks
claim: Logical extrapolators can succeed without fixed-point convergence: the DT-Net RNN sometimes enters limit cycles yet is as performant, complicating the fixed-point view of 2202.05826.
quote: we show that logical extrapolators can succeed even when their iterative part does not converge to a fixed point, and identify and quantify two exotic limiting behaviors

title: Unveiling Transformers with LEGO: a synthetic reasoning task
claim: Weight-tied ALBERT extrapolates to longer reasoning chains than untied BERT of the same depth: near-perfect on two unsupervised variables and nontrivial on a third, vs barely above random for BERT on one.
quote: the iterative ALBERT reaches near-perfect accuracy on two additional variables (#6 and #7), and nontrivial accuracy on the third (#8). These results clearly support that iterative architectures do generalize better in the iterative LEGO reasoning task.

title: Unveiling Transformers with LEGO: a synthetic reasoning task
claim: Training ALBERT with stochastic depth (randomized loop count) further improves length extrapolation.
quote: We uniformly sample depth between 6 and 12 per batch during training while fixing it at 12 during test. Figure 5 shows a clear improvement in generalization to longer lengths using stochastic depth.

title: The Devil is in the Detail: Simple Tricks Improve Systematic Generalization of Transformers
claim: Universal (weight-shared) Transformer variants outperform standard Transformers on most systematic generalization datasets, except COGS and CFQ MCD 1.
quote: Except for COGS and CFQ MCD 1, the universal variants outperform the standard ones.

title: The Devil is in the Detail: Simple Tricks Improve Systematic Generalization of Transformers
claim: On the CFQ output-length split, the Universal Transformer without timestep embedding beats the previously reported UT (77% vs about 66%), and with relative PE reaches 81%.
quote: The only architectural difference between the models is that ours does not make use of any timestep (i.e. layer ID) embedding.

title: On the Mirage of Long-Range Dependency, with an Application to Integer Multiplication
claim: A 321-parameter NCA iterated on a 2D grid achieves 100% accuracy from 16 to 4,096 bits after training on 2-6 bits, with steps scaling linearly in n.
quote: The model achieves 100% accuracy within the training range (2–6 bits) and maintains 100% on all tested out-of-distribution lengths — from 16 bits up to 4,096 bits (2,467 decimal digits), achieving 683 × length generalization.

title: On the Mirage of Long-Range Dependency, with an Application to Integer Multiplication
claim: Iterated transformers fail not because they cannot fit one step but because softmax attention distributions are size-dependent and the update cannot be iterated stably on larger grids.
quote: The problem is not that these architectures cannot fit the single-step target, but that they cannot stably iterate the learned update.

title: Bifurcation Models: Learning Set-Valued Solution Maps with Weight-Tied Dynamics
claim: Broad set-valued maps with locally Lipschitz branches can be represented by regular weight-tied equilibrium dynamics whose induced selectors are almost everywhere regular, while manually chosen single-branch selectors can be arbitrarily irregular.
quote: We prove that broad set-valued maps with locally Lipschitz branches can be represented by regular equilibrium dynamics and that the induced selectors are almost everywhere regular, while manual selectors can be arbitrarily irregular.

title: Advancing the Understanding of Fixed Point Iterations in Deep Neural Networks: A Detailed Analytical Study
claim: Looped neural networks can have exponentially many (2^d) robust fixed points under exponential or polynomial activations, via a sufficient condition based on input regions.
quote: we provide case studies that looped neural networks may exist 2d number of robust fixed points under exponentiation or polynomial activation functions, where d is the feature dimension

title: AlgoFormer: An Efficient Transformer Framework with Algorithmic Structures
claim: A designed AlgoFormer with one-layer pre and loop transformers and a two-layer post transformer can implement Newton's method for regression, with per-step error made arbitrarily small without increasing network size.
quote: However, the error can be made arbitrarily close to zero by increasing the temperature of the softmax and adjusting another free parameter, neither of which affects the size of the network.

title: AlgoFormer: An Efficient Transformer Framework with Algorithmic Structures
claim: On IWSLT De-En, AlgoFormer (single-layer modules, T=10) beats a 12-layer standard transformer and a vanilla looped transformer in cross-entropy and BLEU; on text classification results are mixed (AlgoFormer is worse than standard on DBPedia and Yelp).
quote: As shown in the results, AlgoFormer outperforms and performs comparably with the standard Transformer and the vanilla looped Transformer in the Neural Machine Translation and Text Classification tasks

title: Learning to Solve Constraint Satisfaction Problems with Recurrent Transformer
claim: A Transformer extended with recurrence learns to solve CSPs end to end with advantages over GNNs, SATNet and some neuro-symbolic models.
quote: We show that Transformer extended with recurrence is a viable approach to learning to solve CSPs in an end-to-end manner, having clear advantages over state-of-the-art methods such as Graph Neural Networks, SATNet, and some neuro-symbolic models.

title: Reasoning with Latent Thoughts: On the Power of Looped Transformers
claim: On synthetic reasoning tasks, a k-layer block looped L times nearly matches a kL-layer non-looped model and far outperforms the k-layer model.
quote: a k-layer transformer looped L times nearly matches the performance of a kL-layer non-looped model, and is significantly better than a k-layer model

title: Reasoning with Latent Thoughts: On the Power of Looped Transformers
claim: At LM scale, looped models have worse perplexity than the iso-depth baseline but recover far more of the gap on reasoning-heavy downstream groups (open-book QA, math word problems, reasoning primitives) than on memorization (closed-book QA).
quote: Overall the looped models are worse on perplexity and closed book QA (memorization benchmarks), but the % Gap is much higher for task groups that require reasoning (open book QA, math word problems).

title: Reasoning with Latent Thoughts: On the Power of Looped Transformers
claim: Theorem 5.1: for any finite group, a constant-precision 1-layer transformer looped ceil(log2 n) times computes composition of n elements, matching the best known non-looped depth.
quote: there exists a constant-precision looped transformer TFθ,T computing the composition of n elements from G with a 1-layer transformer block, T = ⌈log2 n⌉ loops

title: Reasoning with Latent Thoughts: On the Power of Looped Transformers
claim: Theorem 5.2: any L-layer transformer with at most R distinct layers is simulated exactly by a 1-layer block looped L times with embedding size d+R+2 and R*H heads; Corollary 5.3: p-hop solved by looping 1 layer floor(log2 p)+2 times with O(log n) precision, matching the non-looped depth lower bound of Sanford et al.
quote: p-hop problem (Definition A.1) can be solved by looping a 1-layer transformer ⌊log2 p⌋ + 2 times, which has O(log n) bits of precision

title: Reasoning with Latent Thoughts: On the Power of Looped Transformers
claim: Theorem 5.4: a looped transformer with L+O(1) layers and Omega(log(n+m)) extra embedding dimension simulates m CoT steps of an L-layer transformer using m loops over m appended dummy tokens.
quote: the output of non-looped transformer after m steps of CoT, TFm θ (v), is the same as that of the looped transformer on input x concatenated by m dummy tokens with m loops

title: Reasoning with Latent Thoughts: On the Power of Looped Transformers
claim: Downstream accuracy of both looped and deep models fits Acc = alpha log(D) + beta in effective depth D; loops help relatively more on reasoning tasks, and for reasoning primitives looping has larger slope than adding layers.
scale: 4-layer block looped up to 12 times (48 effective layers)
quote: Remarkably, the impact of loops is even higher (1.19x) than impact of depth for reasoning primitives, which further consolidates the benefit of looped models for reasoning.

title: Think Shallow, Solve Deep: Controlling Recurrent Dynamics for Reliable Test-Time Depth
claim: Settling operators do not degrade with added depth and on some tasks convert depth into accuracy on harder unseen instances; marginal and drifting ones stay flat, collapse or decay.
quote: settling operators do not degrade with added depth, and on some tasks convert it into higher accuracy on harder unseen instances (Sudoku, 0.19 to 0.34 past the training horizon)

title: Think Shallow, Solve Deep: Controlling Recurrent Dynamics for Reliable Test-Time Depth
claim: Proposition 1 (depth-safety): if the remaining latent path length R_t is smaller than the decoder margin, the decoded answer is frozen for all later iterations.
quote: once an operator’s per-step displacement is small relative to the decoder margin, the decoded answer cannot change under further iterations

title: Think Shallow, Solve Deep: Controlling Recurrent Dynamics for Reliable Test-Time Depth
claim: Removing the terminal fixed-point objective destroys conversion on Sudoku (0.34 to 0.03) or safety on reachability; adding it alone to a generic recurrence makes carry propagation a depth-safe extrapolator.
quote: On Sudoku it destroys conversion (the drifting ablation never rises, 0.34 → 0.03); on reachability it leaves the peak (0.97) but destroys safety

title: Think Shallow, Solve Deep: Controlling Recurrent Dynamics for Reliable Test-Time Depth
claim: Huginn-3.5B latent trajectories never settle (normalized-marginal), and its depth is unsafe on procedural probes; a label-free rank-16 LoRA anchoring objective restores depth-safety but not conversion.
quote: across per-token latent trajectories on 7 task categories (2,585 tokens), not one settles

title: Thinking Deeper, Not Longer: Memory-Efficient Test-Time Reasoning with Depth-Recurrent Transformers for Compositional Generalization
claim: Depth recurrence extrapolates on graph reachability where fixed-depth models barely extrapolate, and on sequence tasks comes within two points of fixed-depth transformers using 4-6.4x more parameters.
quote: it succeeds on the graph task where fixed-depth models barely extrapolate, and on the two sequence tasks comes within two points of fixed-depth Transformers that use 4–6.4× more parameters

title: Thinking Deeper, Not Longer: Memory-Efficient Test-Time Reasoning with Depth-Recurrent Transformers for Compositional Generalization
claim: Supervising the answer at every recurrence step (even with weight 0.1) makes the model learn shallow statistical shortcuts and destroys deep extrapolation; only final-step supervision solves 10-hop paths.
quote: This property disappears even when α = 0.1: 10-hop accuracy falls to chance for every seed.

title: Thinking Deeper, Not Longer: Memory-Efficient Test-Time Reasoning with Depth-Recurrent Transformers for Compositional Generalization
claim: A Universal Transformer with ACT halting is the weakest recurrent variant: its learned halting saturates at about 4 ponder steps where 8-12 are needed, returning to chance beyond the training range.
quote: its learned halting saturates at ≈4 ponder steps where 8–12 are structurally required and the ponder penalty rewards early stopping

title: Thinking Deeper, Not Longer: Memory-Efficient Test-Time Reasoning with Depth-Recurrent Transformers for Compositional Generalization
claim: The stability recipe does not change mean accuracy but removes seed sensitivity: the ablated model's graph OOD swings from 62 to 76 across seeds versus 0.2 variation.

title: Exact Expressive Power of Transformers with Padding
claim: Simulation (exact characterization, d=0): masked-pre-norm AHATs with polynomial padding recognize exactly FO-uniform TC0; n^k padding tokens give storage to resolve majority-logic formulas over k variables.
quote: We show that averaging-hard-attention, masked-pre-norm transformers with polynomial padding recognize precisely the class FO-uniform TC0 of extremely parallelizable problems.

title: Exact Expressive Power of Transformers with Padding
claim: Simulation (exact characterization, looping): with O(log^d n) repetitions of a looped block and polynomial padding, transformers recognize exactly FO-uniform TC^d; looping adds depth with no extra parameters.
quote: we prove that padded transformers with O(logd n) looping on inputs of length n recognize exactly the class FO-uniform TCd of moderately parallelizable problems.

title: Exact Expressive Power of Transformers with Padding
claim: Polylog looping + poly padding = FO-uniform NC, the parallel ceiling; consequently log/polylog-looped padded transformers solve problems believed outside TC0 (boolean formula evaluation, iterated matrix multiplication, graph connectivity, CFL recognition).
quote: Thus log or polylog-looped transformers can solve many problems outside TC0 under standard complexity conjectures, including boolean formula evaluation, iterated matrix multiplication, graph connectivity, and context-free language recognition.

title: Exact Expressive Power of Transformers with Padding
claim: Positioning vs CoT: looping and padding are strictly weaker than CoT under standard conjectures (CoT reaches beyond NC) but preserve parallelism.
quote: Thus, while looping and padding are not as powerful as CoT, our results suggest they are quite effective ways to expand transformers' expressive power while preserving parallelism.

title: Exact Expressive Power of Transformers with Padding
claim: Log-precision and poly-precision looped padded transformer classes are identical.
quote: This shows that these two levels of precision lead to identical power for polylog-looped polynomially-padded transformers.

title: Looped Transformers are Better at Learning Learning Algorithms
claim: A looped transformer matches a standard transformer on in-context data-fitting tasks with under 10% of its parameters.
quote: Experimental results suggest that the looped transformer achieves performance comparable to the standard transformer in solving various data-fitting problems, while utilizing less than 10% of the parameter count.

title: Looped Transformers are Better at Learning Learning Algorithms
claim: At matched effective depth (b=12 loops of 1 layer vs 12 distinct layers), the looped model does not match the standard transformer; it needs more loops than layers (about 20 iterations of 1 layer to match 8 layers).
quote: To match the performance of a standard transformer with L layers, the looped transformer needs more than L loop iterations, i.e. the effective depth of the looped transformer exceeds that of the standard transformer.

title: Looped Transformers are Better at Learning Learning Algorithms
claim: Input injection is necessary for stable extrapolation in loop count: without it, the weight-tied model diverges beyond the trained number of loops; with it, the model reaches a fixed point that persists past training iterations.
quote: During inference, the weight-tying transformer will quickly diverge after the trained loop iterations.

title: Looped Transformers are Better at Learning Learning Algorithms
claim: Looped transformers show an inductive bias toward simpler (sparser) solutions: better on sparse linear regression and skewed covariance, worse under input-scale shift.
quote: the looped transformer exhibits an inductive bias favoring simpler solutions when compared to the unlooped transformer.

title: Looped Transformers are Better at Learning Learning Algorithms
claim: The learned looped solver only emulates fixed-point iteration within the training distribution, with an error floor and limited OOD generalization; it does not recover a true algorithm.
quote: As a result, our trained looped transformer fails to identify an actual algorithm that generalizes to any input distribution, but only emulates the algorithm with the particular input distribution it is trained on.

title: Universal interpolation for deep residual self-attention networks
claim: Universality (depth-only, two shared blocks): two frozen single-head residual softmax attention blocks with Gaussian projections achieve universal interpolation of sequence batches; only block order, signs and durations depend on the task.
quote: Our main result establishes it for residual softmax attention using only two frozen single-head blocks with Gaussian-initialized projection matrices. The result holds at both continuous and finite depth.

title: Universal interpolation for deep residual self-attention networks
claim: With arbitrary heads, a dictionary of 2D (D = Nnd) Gaussian blocks gives universal interpolation on the full noncollinear domain, with block count growing with batch size.
quote: to establish universal interpolation with frozen random noncausal attention blocks for any prescribed number of heads, using a number of blocks that grows linearly with the batch size (Theorem 3.3);

title: Universal interpolation for deep residual self-attention networks
claim: Negative result for causal attention: exact and universal interpolation on the full configuration space are impossible once batch size exceeds token dimension, because causal masking preserves linear relations among first tokens.
quote: As a result, exact interpolation fails for N > d, whatever the number of heads (Proposition 3.8).

title: On the Spatiotemporal Dynamics of Generalization in Neural Networks

quote: Addition—achieving scale-invariant inference from L=16 to L=1,000,000 with 100% accuracy, exhibiting input-adaptive computation

title: On the Spatiotemporal Dynamics of Generalization in Neural Networks
claim: Parity extrapolates from length 16 to 10^6 with inference steps exactly L+1, consistent with light-cone propagation at speed 1.
quote: The model achieved perfect length generalization (from 16 to 106 , a generalization factor of 62,500x), and the inference steps 𝑇 were strictly equal to 𝐿 + 1

title: On the Spatiotemporal Dynamics of Generalization in Neural Networks
claim: Supervision is on known single-step rules, not discovery from input-output data; this is the key caveat for comparison with end-to-end trained looped models.
quote: It is important to emphasize that the model learns under supervised signals of known rules, not discovering rules from chaotic data—the latter is the harder “rule discovery” problem, left for future work.

title: Beyond the Training Horizon: Mechanisms and Limits of Length Generalization in Looped Transformers
claim: Under final-answer supervision, the two looped recipes learn mechanistically distinct recurrent algorithms (fixed readout accumulator vs advancing frontier).
quote: MR-Loop updates an intermediate state at a fixed readout while advancing relation selection through adjacent-token interactions and a transferable progress cue. DR-Loop instead propagates intermediate states across relation positions, forming an advancing computational frontier.

title: Beyond the Training Horizon: Mechanisms and Limits of Length Generalization in Looped Transformers
claim: Extrapolation has a finite range: MR-Loop final-answer accuracy with loops equal to input length drops to 70.3% at n=20 and 1.6% at n=30 (trained to n=12).
quote: The observed extrapolation has a finite operating range: final-answer accuracy with R = n loops is 70.3% at n = 20 and 1.6% at n = 30, and the key-state cue weakens at larger hop indices.

title: Beyond the Training Horizon: Mechanisms and Limits of Length Generalization in Looped Transformers
claim: Failure at extreme lengths comes from degradation of computation-supporting states plus limited self-correction, so errors compound geometrically in trajectory survival.
quote: extreme-length generalization fails when repeated updates degrade the states needed for subsequent computation and the learned recurrence does not reliably repair them

title: Beyond the Training Horizon: Mechanisms and Limits of Length Generalization in Looped Transformers
claim: Length generalization need not reflect faithful iterative computation; with compressible tasks models reach correct answers without exposing intermediate states.
quote: Successful length generalization therefore demonstrates behavioral transfer to longer horizons, but does not, by itself, establish that the model executes the intended state-by-state procedure.
