quote: We prove that a looped linear transformer with LN, trained by gradient descent, converges to a solution that implements the power method, with each self-attention layer performing one power iteration.

title: Looped Transformers with Layer Normalization Provably Learn the Power Method
claim: Separation in training outcome: even with layerwise power-iteration supervision, a transformer without LN cannot exactly learn the power method, whereas with LN it can, giving a provable performance gap.
quote: even with layerwise guidance from power iterations, a transformer without LN cannot exactly learn the power method, whereas the corresponding transformer with LN can, leading to a provable performance gap in principal component prediction.

title: Looped Transformers with Layer Normalization Provably Learn the Power Method
claim: Looping the LN-trained module yields exponential error decay whose contraction factor approaches the optimal power-method rate; without LN the factor is fixed and suboptimal.
quote: In contrast, for a transformer without LN, irrespective of the training target in (4.4), looping the learned module also results in exponential error decay, but with a fixed and suboptimal factor

title: Thinking Deeper, Not Longer: Memory-Efficient Test-Time Reasoning with Depth-Recurrent Transformers for Compositional Generalization
claim: Depth recurrence extrapolates beyond training depth on graph reachability where fixed-depth models barely extrapolate, and on sequence tasks comes within two points of fixed-depth transformers with 4-6.4x more parameters.
quote: Depth recurrence extrapolates beyond the training range: it succeeds on the graph task where fixed-depth models barely extrapolate, and on the two sequence tasks comes within two points of fixed-depth Transformers that use 4–6.4× more parameters.

title: Thinking Deeper, Not Longer: Memory-Efficient Test-Time Reasoning with Depth-Recurrent Transformers for Compositional Generalization
claim: Intermediate per-step supervision harms depth extrapolation: even alpha=0.1 per-step loss drops 10-hop accuracy to chance, while final-step-only training reaches 84%.
quote: On the graph task, whose adjacency mask makes propagation depth verifiable, intermediate per-step supervision—a standard recipe for deep iterative models—consistently harms this extrapolation.

title: Thinking Deeper, Not Longer: Memory-Efficient Test-Time Reasoning with Depth-Recurrent Transformers for Compositional Generalization
claim: Learned ACT halting does not extrapolate: the Universal Transformer's ponder budget saturates near 4 steps where 8-12 are needed, returning to chance OOD on graph reachability.
quote: because its learned halting saturates at ≈4 ponder steps where 8–12 are structurally required and the ponder penalty rewards early stopping.

title: Thinking Deeper, Not Longer: Memory-Efficient Test-Time Reasoning with Depth-Recurrent Transformers for Compositional Generalization

title: Loop, Think, & Generalize: Implicit Reasoning in Recurrent-Depth Transformers
claim: Looped models (R>=2) achieve systematic generalization on unseen fact compositions while a vanilla 4-layer model (R=1, same params) and an iso-FLOP 8-layer vanilla model at matched effective depth fail.
quote: We compare against an iso-FLOP 8-layer vanilla transformer with matched effective depth. The vanilla model exhibits only two training stages and fails to achieve non-zero systematic generalization regardless of training time

title: Loop, Think, & Generalize: Implicit Reasoning in Recurrent-Depth Transformers
claim: Scaling inference-time recurrence enables extrapolation to deeper compositions; the max training iterations determine the extrapolation range (R=6 reaches 14-hop, R=8 reaches 19-hop when trained up to 12-hop).
quote: increasing the number of training-time iterations substantially improves extrapolation when scaling inference-time iterations (e.g. R = 6 extrapolates up to 14-hop, while R = 8 reaches 19-hop).

title: Loop, Think, & Generalize: Implicit Reasoning in Recurrent-Depth Transformers
claim: Deeper vanilla transformers (8/16/24 layers) improve ID generalization but remain weaker than looped models of the same effective depth and show no OOD depth extrapolation.
quote: However, their ID generalization remains weaker than recurrent-depth models with the same effective depth. More importantly, the vanilla models still do not exhibit OOD generalization to more complex samples

title: Loop, Think, & Generalize: Implicit Reasoning in Recurrent-Depth Transformers
claim: Overthinking limits inference scaling: the correct-answer logit margin peaks then declines with more loops; dynamic training slows the decay, and input injection does not resolve it here.
quote: Note that although previous work mitigates overthinking by injecting inputs information in every iteration (Bansal et al., 2022; Geiping et al., 2025), we find that such methods do not resolve the issue in implicit reasoning.

title: Revisiting Padded Transformer Expressivity: Which Architectural Choices Matter and Which Don't

title: Revisiting Padded Transformer Expressivity: Which Architectural Choices Matter and Which Don't
claim: Robustness: once precision is logarithmic, attention type, width and further precision do not change padded expressivity; precision and depth are the main factors.
quote: Interestingly, growing width or precision beyond logarithmic does not increase expressivity, and all our results hold for both softmax and average hard attention transformers.

title: Revisiting Padded Transformer Expressivity: Which Architectural Choices Matter and Which Don't
claim: Resource-allocation implication: given a sequential budget, spend only log N on precision and the rest on looping, since expressivity scales with looping but not with extra precision (expressivity only, not learnability).
quote: Given a budget of, e.g., logd N sequential steps, our results suggest devoting only log N of those to numeric precision and the remaining logd−1 N ones to looping

title: Recurrent neural networks approximate continuous functions

quote: More precisely, each such function is uniformly approximated by the time evolution of a single ReLU recurrent neural network with fixed weights and fixed hidden dimension.

title: Recurrent neural networks approximate continuous functions

title: Recurrent neural networks approximate continuous functions

quote: We complement the construction with minimax lower bounds showing that runtime is not merely a proof artifact, but an unavoidable resource in this fixed-network approximation paradigm.

title: Beyond Memorization: Extending Reasoning Depth with Recurrence, Memory and Test-Time Compute Scaling

title: Beyond Memorization: Extending Reasoning Depth with Recurrence, Memory and Test-Time Compute Scaling

title: To CoT or To Loop? A Formal Comparison Between Chain-of-Thought and Looped Transformers

title: To CoT or To Loop? A Formal Comparison Between Chain-of-Thought and Looped Transformers
claim: Separation (loops > CoT): at the same polylogarithmic budget, CoT[log^k n] is strictly contained in LOOP[log^k n] under standard circuit conjectures; e.g., linear equations, bipartite perfect matching and fixed-CFL membership are in log^2 n loops but not log^2 n CoT steps.
quote: These results show that, under the same polylogarithmic number of steps or loops, Looped TF can simulate parallel computations more efficiently than CoT.

title: To CoT or To Loop? A Formal Comparison Between Chain-of-Thought and Looped Transformers
claim: Separation (CoT > loops): with stochastic decoding, CoT can approximately count solutions of some self-reducible relation, which no deterministic looped TF can do with polynomially many loops, assuming FPTAS != FPRAS.
quote: Assuming that FPTAS = ̸ FPRAS, there exists a relation R such that a probabilistic CoT can approximate the count |R(x)| within any desired relative error ε > 0 with high probability in polynomial time

title: To CoT or To Loop? A Formal Comparison Between Chain-of-Thought and Looped Transformers
claim: Looped TF with T(n) loops (poly width, log precision) is equivalent to nonuniform threshold circuits of polynomial size and depth T(n).
quote: a decision problem L belongs to the class LOOP[T (n), poly(n), log n] if and only if L is decidable by nonuniform families of threshold circuits of polynomial size and depth T (n).

title: Neural Algorithmic Reasoning for Hypergraphs with Looped Transformers

title: Neural Algorithmic Reasoning for Hypergraphs with Looped Transformers

title: On the Role of Depth and Looping for In-Context Learning with Task Diversity

title: On the Role of Depth and Looping for In-Context Learning with Task Diversity

title: On the Role of Depth and Looping for In-Context Learning with Task Diversity

title: ALTA: Compiler-Based Analysis of Transformers

quote: ALTA allows us to constructively show how Transformers can represent length-invariant algorithms for computing parity and addition, as well as a solution to the SCAN benchmark of compositional generalization tasks, without requiring intermediate scratchpad decoding steps.

title: ALTA: Compiler-Based Analysis of Transformers
claim: Resource bound: the compiled addition program needs N+2 layers (loop iterations) for N-digit inputs, and its minimal version trained on <=3-digit data generalizes to unbounded lengths.
quote: The number of layers required to compute the sum is N + 2, where N is the number of digits in the larger of the two inputs.

title: ALTA: Compiler-Based Analysis of Transformers

quote: However, in practice, all variants exhibit behavior similar to that of the minimal Sum + Modulo program, i.e., they exhibit some degree of length generalization but do not generalize to examples with more ones than were seen during training.

title: ALTA: Compiler-Based Analysis of Transformers
claim: More layers do not help end-to-end SCAN generalization even up to 256 encoder and 256 decoder layers.

quote: Our results demonstrate that as long as the input data has a constant condition number, e.g., n = O(d), the linear looped Transformers can achieve a small error by multi-step gradient descent during in-context learning.

title: Bypassing the Exponential Dependency: Looped Transformers Efficiently Learn In-context by Multi-step Gradient Descent
claim: Resource bound: after T loops the prediction error is at most |alpha| exp(-T/(2 kappa)) where kappa is the condition number of X^T X.
quote: the linear looped Transformer can predict a vector output with error ≤ |α| · exp(− 2κ ) by explicitly performing multi-step gradient descent in its hidden states.

title: Bypassing the Exponential Dependency: Looped Transformers Efficiently Learn In-context by Multi-step Gradient Descent
claim: Prior results needed an exponential number of in-context examples in the loop count; this work removes that dependency.

title: Transformers discover an elementary calculation system exploiting local attention and grid-like problem representation

title: Transformers discover an elementary calculation system exploiting local attention and grid-like problem representation

title: Graph Hierarchical Recurrence for Long-Range Generalization

quote: For floats, the formalism matching recurrent GNNs is a rule-based modal logic with counting, while for reals we use a suitable infinitary modal logic, also with counting.

title: Logical Characterizations of Recurrent Graph Neural Networks with Reals and Floats

title: Rethinking Deep Thinking: Stable Learning of Algorithms using Lipschitz Constraints

title: Recurrent Convolutional Neural Networks Learn Succinct Learning Algorithms
claim: The constants in the analysis are too large to be practically meaningful.

title: Context-free Recognition with Transformers

title: Context-free Recognition with Transformers

title: When Does Recurrence Become an Algorithm? Convergence Selection in Weight-Tied Looped Transformers
claim: At fixed effective depth 12 with parameters matched, the fully untied model is worst at length extrapolation and, on A5, untied/partially tied configurations with G>=3 fail to learn, while tied ones learn; with constant width (more params) untying looks mildly beneficial.
quote: with free parameters, untying appears mildly beneficial; with parameters matched, the fully untied model is worst at length extrapolation, and on A5 every configuration with G ≥ 3 fails to learn the task at all (9/9 seeds) while tied configurations learn it.

title: When Does Recurrence Become an Algorithm? Convergence Selection in Weight-Tied Looped Transformers
claim: Learning walls track operator size, not circuit class: NC1-complete A5 generalizes, S5 deadlocks under the standard curriculum, and an operator-first curriculum cracks S5 in 10/10 seeds.
quote: an operator-first curriculum—an extended n=2 stage that masters the composition table before any chaining—cracks S5 in every seed attempted (10/10 across two machines, exact match ≥ 0.92 at 2× training length).

title: When Does Recurrence Become an Algorithm? Convergence Selection in Weight-Tied Looped Transformers
claim: Standard instruments (skip tolerance, cross-step similarity, attribution) are provably blind once loops converge to a fixed point; only head-of-trajectory measurements identify the algorithm.
quote: any loop-mechanism claim based on skip tolerance, cross-step similarity, or shared-dictionary attribution is uninformative unless the measurement is localized to the head of the trajectory

title: When Does Recurrence Become an Algorithm? Convergence Selection in Weight-Tied Looped Transformers
claim: On the open prefix-sums benchmark, looped transformers extrapolate to 4x training length but break between 128 and 256 bits, short of convolutional Deep Thinking nets' 512-bit extrapolation.
quote: The frontier breaks between 128 and 256 bits (Table 9), well short of the 512-bit extrapolation that convolutional Deep Thinking networks achieve on this dataset (Bansal et al., 2022)

title: Neural Weight Norm = Kolmogorov Complexity
claim: Simulation/complexity: in fixed precision, the minimum weight norm of a looped network that halts and outputs a binary string equals the string's Kolmogorov complexity up to a logarithmic factor.
quote: We prove that, in any fixed-precision regime, the smallest weight norm of a looped neural network outputting a binary string equals the Kolmogorov complexity of that string, up to a logarithmic factor.

title: Neural Weight Norm = Kolmogorov Complexity
claim: Fixed precision is necessary: with infinite precision, networks encode non-computable functions and weight norm loses meaning.
quote: The fixed-precision assumption is essential: with infinite precision, neural networks can encode non-computable functions and the weight norm loses its relevance.

title: Neural Weight Norm = Kolmogorov Complexity
claim: The result concerns minimum-norm networks, not what gradient descent finds, and is not validated experimentally.
quote: Corollary 7 concerns the induced output prior Q(s), not what gradient descent finds; closing the gap between minimum-norm networks and trained networks is the natural next step. The theorem and its predictions are not validated experimentally.

title: Emergent Models: Intelligence from Tiny Substrates
claim: Universality: some Emergent Models are latent-universal, realizing any partial computable function with the rule and interface fixed and only the initial latent state varied.
quote: Theoretically, we prove that some EMs are latent-universal: with the update rule and interface held fixed, they can realize any partial computable function by varying only the initial condition of the latent state.

title: Emergent Models: Intelligence from Tiny Substrates
claim: Tiny iterated substrates extrapolate exactly on simple one-input arithmetic functions in all runs.
quote: Perfect extrapolation is observed, in all runs, for all oneinput tasks considered.

title: Simulation of Graph Algorithms with Looped Transformers
claim: Simulation: a looped transformer of constant width with adjacency-aware heads simulates Dijkstra's algorithm on rational-weighted graphs up to O(1/delta_hat) nodes.
quote: There exists a looped-transformer hT in the form of (2), with 17 layers, 3 attention heads, and layer width O(1) that simulates Dijkstra's shortest path algorithm for weighted graphs with rational edge-weights

title: Simulation of Graph Algorithms with Looped Transformers
claim: Parameter count does not grow with graph size, but finite precision limits the simulable graph size.
quote: The number of parameters in the networks does not increase with the input graph size, which implies that the networks can simulate the above algorithms for any graph. Despite this property, we show a limit to simulation in our solution due to finite precision.

title: Simulation of Graph Algorithms with Looped Transformers
claim: Universality: the architecture is Turing complete with O(1) width via an 11-layer, 3-head SUBLEQ simulation.
quote: with 11 layers, 3 attention heads, and layer width O(1) that simulates SUBLEQ.

title: Simulation of Graph Algorithms with Looped Transformers
claim: Learnability caveat: constructed parameters require approximating discontinuous functions, causing ill-conditioning that makes gradient-based recovery hard, worsening as tolerances shrink.
quote: Despite demonstrating the existence of parameters capable of simulation, discovering them through gradient-based training is challenging.

title: Transformers Can Do Arithmetic with the Right Embeddings
claim: Abacus Embeddings with looped transformers and input injection raise OOD addition accuracy from 92.9% to 99.1% (87% error reduction) relative to the embeddings with standard architectures.
quote: We show that when we combine Abacus Embeddings with input injection and looped transformers performance further improves, increasing from 92.9% to 99.1% in out of distribution accuracy, an 87% reduction in error

title: Transformers Can Do Arithmetic with the Right Embeddings
claim: At fixed effective depth 16, an 8-layer block looped twice (8x2) halves the OOD error of the non-recurrent 16x1 model with input injection.
quote: We see that a recurrent model with eight layers in the recurrent block and two recurrences is the most accurate of all effective depth 16 models, halving the error rate of a standard model with input injection in the OOD evaluation.

title: Transformers Can Do Arithmetic with the Right Embeddings
claim: With FIRE or NoPE on 40-digit training data, the looped transformer (input injection + progressive loss) has the best OOD addition despite ~10x fewer parameters.
quote: Despite having approximately 10× fewer parameters than the other models, we see that the looped transformer (recurrent, with input injection and progressive loss), achieves the best out of distribution performance using either position embedding.

title: Transformers Can Do Arithmetic with the Right Embeddings
claim: Looping does not uniformly help: on sorting, the standard transformer has the best exact-match accuracy, while the looped transformer is best only at identifying the minimum element.
quote: For sorting, different architectures appear to be better suited to different types of extrapolation, for example the looped transformer is best at extrapolating for finding the minimum element but not for sorting the whole array.

title: Transformers Can Do Arithmetic with the Right Embeddings
claim: Length generalization reaches 6x the training length (20 to 120 digits), versus 2.5x for prior state of the art.
quote: models trained with at most 20 digit operands can generalize to problems with 120 digit operands. This represents a state-of-the-art generalization factor of 6×, with the previous state of the art being only 2.5×.

title: Encode, Think, Decode: Scaling test-time reasoning with recursive latent thoughts
claim: Looping the selected middle layers during mid-training improves the identically mid-trained non-recursive OLMo-2 1B, most on math and reading comprehension; iteration count and FLOPs grow with k (not FLOP-matched to a deeper dense model).
quote: ETD models yield substantial gains on 17 reasoning benchmarks, including +28.4% relative accuracy improvement on GSM8K and +36% on MATH with the OLMo-2 1B Base model.

title: Encode, Think, Decode: Scaling test-time reasoning with recursive latent thoughts
claim: Which layers to loop matters: at equal FLOPs, looping the 4 knee-selected layers beats looping all layers or the middle 12 layers.
quote: Our approach consistently outperforms these alternatives under equal compute. For example, the 2–12*2–2 setup is FLOP-equivalent to our 7–4*4–5 configuration, yet yields lower accuracy.

title: Encode, Think, Decode: Scaling test-time reasoning with recursive latent thoughts
claim: The best block position depends on task category: 7-4*2-5 is best for math, while an earlier block (3-4*2-9) is best for reading comprehension.
quote: Interestingly, for reading comprehension, the 3-4*2-9 configuration performs best.

title: Encode, Think, Decode: Scaling test-time reasoning with recursive latent thoughts
claim: An ACT-style router trained end-to-end gives adaptive depth that tracks the fixed-depth accuracy-iteration trade-off and beats fixed k=5 on DROP and OpenBookQA with fewer average iterations.
quote: we see that adaptive-depth ETD outperforms the ETD with fixed k=5 iterations. Moreover, it also achieves this with fewer iterations on average.

title: Bridging the Gap Between Latent and Explicit Reasoning with Looped Transformers
claim: At 3B, the looped padded model with parallel gold-CoT supervision brings latent reasoning to within about 1 point of explicit CoT on GSM8K (same backbone, same data), unlike prior latent methods whose gap widens with scale.
quote: on L LAMA -3.2-3B-I NSTRUCT, it brings the GSM8K test accuracy to within 1 point of explicit CoT and surpasses explicit CoT on the out-ofdomain math average.

title: Bridging the Gap Between Latent and Explicit Reasoning with Looped Transformers
claim: For direct LM-head supervision, reading only the post-loop latents beats supervising every iteration; the auxiliary-decoder variant prefers per-iteration readout.
quote: LOTUS performs best with post-loop readout (70.0% vs. 68.2% per-iter), which lets the early latent blocks refine fully until the end of the loop.

title: Bridging the Gap Between Latent and Explicit Reasoning with Looped Transformers
claim: Trained loop depth matters strongly and extra test-time loops beyond the trained depth do not help.
quote: Accuracy climbs with R (22.7% at R“1 to 70.0% at R“6), peaks at the trained R“6, and dips slightly at R“7 (69.3%).

title: Bridging the Gap Between Latent and Explicit Reasoning with Looped Transformers
claim: The looped padded backbone helps even without latent supervision, and gold-CoT supervision adds further gains.
quote: Without any latent supervision, the looped backbone alone (63.3%) already exceeds CODI + SIM-CoT (62.3%, Table 1), which uses a single latent per step

title: Architectural Sampling: Test-Time Scaling via Computational Diversity in Frozen Vision Language Models
claim: At equal candidate count (9), candidates from repeated-layer paths cover more correct answers than temperature samples of the standard path; per-candidate compute is higher, so not FLOP-matched.
quote: Across five Qwen checkpoints and twelve multimodal benchmarks, architectural sampling improves pass@9 over standardpath temperature sampling by 6.58 percentage points on average at the same ninecandidate budget.

title: Architectural Sampling: Test-Time Scaling via Computational Diversity in Frozen Vision Language Models
claim: Which layers to repeat: early windows give the highest pass@9; gains fall as the window moves deeper.
quote: Every region improves over temperature sampling, but the gain falls as the window moves deeper. Reusing the early layers gives the highest pass@9 on all five benchmarks

title: Don't Commit Alone: Joint Token Commitment in Diffusion Language Models
claim: Extra layer reuse helps only with the marker signal: re-applying the last n layers without the marker lowers GSM8K accuracy, so the gain is not just added depth.
quote: Re-applying the last n layers without a marker reduces accuracy by 0.76 points, indicating that the marker announcement contributes beyond additional depth.

title: Don't Commit Alone: Joint Token Commitment in Diffusion Language Models
claim: Re-applying more layers does not help: n=3 beats n=6 and n=9 on average.
quote: Averaged over the seven benchmarks, n=3 scores 78.72, compared with 77.50 for n=6 and 77.65 for n=9.

title: Port-Hamiltonian Latent Deliberation: Mitigating the Deliberation Drift Cliff in Test-Time Compute Scaling
claim: Unconstrained recurrent latent updates diverge out of distribution when iterated well past the training horizon; dissipative constraints prevent this.
quote: an unconstrained baseline (B0-Naive) suffers a catastrophic drop from a peak of 96.60% at K = 4 down to 34.13% at K = 64 (∆ = −62.47%).

title: Layer Duplication in LLMs
claim: Duplicating the initial self-attention layers once or twice often improves performance.
quote: The re-sults demonstrate that duplicating the initial layers once or twice often yields a significant performance boost.

title: MACRO: Markov Chain Routing of Transformer Layers
claim: Task-level routing of a frozen LLM improves average accuracy over the unrouted model and over Dr.LLM while cutting route-search time.
quote: MACRO achieves a +5.0% average accuracy improvement over the unrouted baselines, with largest gains on small models. We outperform the best dynamic routing approach Dr. LLM by +7.2%, while reducing route-search time 9.4× (from 14.8 to 1.6 hours).

title: MACRO: Markov Chain Routing of Transformer Layers
claim: Gains shrink as the base model gets stronger: large on Qwen3-1.7B and the R1-distilled model, under 1 point on Qwen3-8B/14B.
quote: its margin over the unrouted baseline is widest exactly where that baseline is weakest, narrowing to a smaller but consistent gain once the model is already strong

title: MACRO: Markov Chain Routing of Transformer Layers
claim: The action space (including residual addition of earlier hidden states) matters more than the router: Dr.LLM's skip-and-repeat space often falls below baseline, while the same routers with MACRO's action space are much stronger.
quote: indicating that the action space itself is a decisive part of what makes layer routing help rather than hurt

title: MACRO: Markov Chain Routing of Transformer Layers
claim: Logit-lens analysis suggests routing exposes an answer already computed internally rather than adding new reasoning.
quote: this suggests that routing improves how an already-computed answer is exposed rather than changing the reasoning itself

title: Skip a Layer or Loop It? Learning Program-of-Layers in LLMs
claim: In an oracle MCTS search (validity judged by answer correctness), allowing layer recurrence beats skip-only, and joint skip+loop is best in every setting.
quote: Layer recurrence-only performs better than layer skipping-only, but combining the two complementary operators produces the best program-of-layers.

title: Skip a Layer or Loop It? Learning Program-of-Layers in LLMs
claim: Useful programs in pretrained models are local: mostly single-layer or two-layer contiguous segments, repeated at most once; deep iterative reuse is rare.
quote: Valid execution programs are predominantly composed of contiguous layer segments and typically require at most a single recurrence per segment.

title: Skip a Layer or Loop It? Learning Program-of-Layers in LLMs
claim: The learned predictor outperforms sampling-based inference of the same frozen model at pass@1 and pass@5, often with fewer unique layers.
quote: Base (sampling) improves from 32.8% at pass@1 to 43.8% at pass@5, while P O L AR improves from 35.1% to 51.2%.

title: Skip a Layer or Loop It? Learning Program-of-Layers in LLMs
claim: Pretrained models' training objective favors only short-range local reuse, limiting how much looping a frozen model can exploit.
quote: their training objectives favor short-range, local reuse over rich program composition

title: Programs-of-Layers in LLMs through the Lens of Cortical Areas
claim: Oracle search reproduces PoLar's ordering: repeat-only beats skip-only and combined skip&repeat beats both, on every model and difficulty.
quote: skip and repeat combined beat either alone, on every model and every DART-Math difficulty level, with repeat the stronger of the two mechanisms on its own.

title: Programs-of-Layers in LLMs through the Lens of Cortical Areas
claim: The learned single-shot router does not reproduce: its top-1 program is always the identity forward pass, even with PoLar's own code and many anti-collapse fixes.
quote: On every model, difficulty split, and training-data treatment tested, the router's top-1 decode is always the literal identity program, both for our own reimplementation and for Li et al.'s own unmodified training code run on our data

title: Programs-of-Layers in LLMs through the Lens of Cortical Areas
claim: A single well-chosen middle block repeated once, with no training, improves Qwen3-8B on MMLU-Pro; blocks straddling an early boundary (layer 6) collapse accuracy.
quote: Simply repeating a well-chosen middle block (layers 18–22), no retraining, no other intervention, already improves Qwen3-8B's accuracy on a 6-domain subset of MMLU-Pro

title: Programs-of-Layers in LLMs through the Lens of Cortical Areas
claim: Error-correcting programs are brittle and MMLU-Pro rescuing programs track answer position, not content, suggesting oracle program gains partly reflect overfitting.
quote: MCTS-discovered rescuing programs substantially overfit to the correct answer's position, not its content.

title: Skip a Layer or Loop it? Test-Time Depth Adaptation of Pretrained LLMs
claim: With per-sample oracle search, shorter paths exist for most correctly answered samples and correcting paths exist for most wrongly answered samples.
quote: For >75% of samples with correct predictions by the original LLM, we can find shorter CoLa, suggesting a large space for improving inference efficiency; (2) For >60% of samples with originally incorrect predictions, we can identify CoLa achieving correct predictions

title: Skip a Layer or Loop it? Test-Time Depth Adaptation of Pretrained LLMs
claim: Joint skip+recurrence search beats skip-only and recurrence-only on all datasets and models; skip-only is stronger on easy ARC tasks, recurrence-only on harder DART levels for instruct models.
quote: Our full method, which searches over both skipping and recurrence decisions, consistently achieves the highest accuracy on all datasets and models.

title: Skip a Layer or Loop it? Test-Time Depth Adaptation of Pretrained LLMs
claim: Recurrence-only gains come with increased depth; error-correcting paths are often shorter than the full model, suggesting 'overthinking' in depth.
quote: Recurrence-only strategies achieve moderate gains over the pretrained baseline, but do so by increasing the overall depth

title: Skip a Layer or Loop it? Test-Time Depth Adaptation of Pretrained LLMs
claim: Early layers are kept; skipping concentrates in middle layers, most sharply in small pretrained models.
quote: CoLa models consistently keep early layers but exhibit an elevated skip rate of middle layers.

title: Inner Loop Inference for Pretrained Transformers: Unlocking Latent Capabilities Without Training
claim: Naively repeating a block of a frozen pretrained model degrades accuracy for every tested start-end configuration, some collapsing toward chance, consistent with distribution shift of activations.
quote: All looped configurations perform worse than the baseline accuracy, with some settings collapsing to near-chance performance.

title: Inner Loop Inference for Pretrained Transformers: Unlocking Latent Capabilities Without Training
claim: Interpolating looped states (uniform averaging of cached loop states) yields modest gains on Gemma models; Llama-3-8B (pure pre-norm) responds inconsistently.
quote: this yields modest but consistent accuracy gains for Gemma models, while Llama 3–8B responds less reliably, due to architectural differences.

title: Inner Loop Inference for Pretrained Transformers: Unlocking Latent Capabilities Without Training
claim: The best loop region is in the middle of the network (about 40-60% depth).
quote: the selected intervals consistently fall within comparable relative depths, roughly 40–60% of the network, matching the stage-wise inference dynamics reported in [2].

title: Inner Loop Inference for Pretrained Transformers: Unlocking Latent Capabilities Without Training
claim: Normalization placement matters for stability of repeated application: pre-norm is described as less stable under repetition than Gemma 2's pre+post norm.
quote: most modern LLMs rely on pre-layer normalization, which improves optimization during training but is known to be less stable when blocks are repeatedly applied

title: Training-Free Looped Transformers
claim: Naive K-fold reapplication of a mid block in a frozen model degrades accuracy almost universally, because post-loop layers were trained on the one-pass endpoint.
quote: But the post-loop layers are not trained to receive the trajectory at t=K, and empirically, naive K-fold looping degrades performance almost universally (Section 3).

title: Training-Free Looped Transformers
claim: Damped sub-stepping (K Euler steps of size 1/K, or K-stage RK with anchor) keeps iterates in the trained regime and improves over the unlooped checkpoint on most cells.
quote: The principled goal of g (K) is therefore not to advance integration to t=K, but to better approximate the same endpoint x(t=1) that the unmodified network already targets.

title: Training-Free Looped Transformers
claim: Which layers to loop: the optimal window sits at a stable fractional depth across architectures; MoE models need layer-mode iteration.
quote: A universal depth-fraction rule places the optimal window at fractional depth ≈0.45–0.60 across dense and MoE architectures from 16 to 48 layers.

title: Training-Free Looped Transformers
claim: Higher-order solvers and fixed-point accelerators do not beat simple damped sub-stepping, suggesting the looped middle of a pretrained transformer is not contractive.
quote: find none robustly beats K-stage Runge–Kutta, suggesting the looped middle of a pretrained transformer [35, 77, 5] is not contractive in any useful sense

title: Entropy-Gated Latent Recursion
claim: Majority vote over the L-axis rollout pool improves over greedy decoding of the same frozen model on almost all cells, and beats FLOP-matched beam search.
quote: EGLR-SC improves over greedy on 44/48 (model, dataset) cells across 8 instruction-tuned models and 6 math reasoning benchmarks, and outperforms FLOP-matched beam search on 11/12 cells.

title: Entropy-Gated Latent Recursion
claim: Single-configuration recursion is not reliably beneficial; gains come from aggregation over configurations.
quote: A single L without aggregation sometimes degrades accuracy (e.g., Qwen2.5-3B / MATH-500 at L = 10: 61.6% vs. greedy 64.6%). The reliable gain comes from aggregating over the L-axis pool via EGLR-SC.

title: Entropy-Gated Latent Recursion
claim: Training-free recursion must stay close to the anchor state: a small fusion weight is stable, large weights collapse because drift compounds.
quote: drops sharply at α = 0.5 (56.6%, −8.4 pp), and collapses at α ≥ 0.7 (near-zero at 0.9). Large α erases the anchor signal; the recursion then compounds drift errors.

title: GramLoop: Training-Free Gram-Gated Replay for Robust Dense Prediction
claim: Gram-gated replay of a mid window of a frozen DINOv3 improves every shifted benchmark over the paired baseline, at about 2x inference time.
quote: GramLoop improves over the paired DINOv3 baseline on every shifted benchmark. Although the gains on the -C and -P suites are modest, they are obtained without training or parameter updates

title: GramLoop: Training-Free Gram-Gated Replay for Robust Dense Prediction
claim: Measuring drift at the final layer and applying the update at the loop endpoint is the best placement; naive replay can disrupt the relational structure the suffix expects.
quote: Table 4 shows that measuring Gram consistency at the final layer while applying the accepted update at the loop endpoint performs best.

title: Hopping Too Late: Exploring the Limitations of Large Language Models on Multi-Hop Queries
claim: Re-running layers by patching a later-layer state into an earlier layer corrects a large share of previously incorrect two-hop answers, but only with oracle choice of layers.
quote: correctly answering between 32%-66% of incorrect cases while keeping the correct cases at 100% across models and token positions.

title: Hopping Too Late: Exploring the Limitations of Large Language Models on Multi-Hop Queries
claim: Back-patching is not a practical inference method because the right source/target layers must be chosen a priori.
quote: our current proposed method is not a practical inference method, as only a subset of back-patches generate the correct answer.

title: ScaleNet: Scaling up Pretrained Neural Networks with Incremental Parameters
claim: A 2x depth-scaled DeiT-Base built by weight sharing plus adapters beats training the deeper model from scratch with a third of the epochs (excluding the cost of the source checkpoint).
quote: With a 2× depth-scaled DeiT-Base model, ScaleNet achieves a 7.42% accuracy improvement over training from scratch while requiring only one-third of the training epochs

title: ScaleNet: Scaling up Pretrained Neural Networks with Incremental Parameters
claim: Reusing layers twice helps but three reuses hurts, suggesting a limit on how often a shared pretrained layer can be reused.
quote: increasing the reuse time to three leads to a performance drop, with DeiT-Base dropping to 82.27% and Swin-Base to 83.58%. This suggests that reusing the same parameters too many times can constrain ability of the model

title: ScaleNet: Scaling up Pretrained Neural Networks with Incremental Parameters
claim: Per-instance adjustment parameters stabilize training of the weight-shared expanded model; without them gradient norms increase and fluctuate.
quote: when layer adjustment is not applied to the model, the gradient norms increase significantly, with fluctuations observed in the initial layers.

title: ScaleNet: Scaling up Pretrained Neural Networks with Incremental Parameters
claim: Which layers / ordering: interleaving reused layers is best for isotropic DeiT, stacking at the tail is best for hierarchical Swin.
quote: For DeiT-Base, interpolating layers yields the best performance, achieving a Top-1 accuracy of 82.53%, compared to 82.23% for stacking layers

title: Speeding up Deep Model Training by Sharing Weights and Then Unsharing
claim: Sharing weights for the first ~10% of steps then untying improves BERT over the standard untied baseline trained for the same number of iterations.
quote: Our experiments show that oftentimes under various settings, the best result is given by sharing weights for the first 10% of the total number of iterations.

title: Speeding up Deep Model Training by Sharing Weights and Then Unsharing
claim: Keeping weights tied throughout (ALBERT-style) is much worse; never sharing generalizes worse; untying around 10% is best.
quote: If weights are shared throughout the entire pre-training process, the final performance will be much worse than without any form of weight sharing

title: Speeding up Deep Model Training by Sharing Weights and Then Unsharing
claim: With multi-layer sharing units, half the iterations match the baseline trained for full iterations.
quote: SWE 4x6 and 2x12 trained for a half million iterations achieve similar fine-tuning results compared to the non-SWE baseline trained for one million iterations.

title: Retrofitting Recurrent Depth into a Pretrained Language Model: Installation, Extrapolation, Transfer, and Retention at Two Parameter Budgets
claim: Prelude re-injection is required; without it iterated pretrained layers drift off-manifold within a few loops.
quote: The re-injection is essential: without fresh access to the Prelude representation, iterated application drives states off the pretraining manifold within a few loops

title: Retrofitting Recurrent Depth into a Pretrained Language Model: Installation, Extrapolation, Transfer, and Retention at Two Parameter Budgets
claim: A 6.01M-parameter LoRA retrofit over frozen base weights matches the 180.6M full-block retrofit overall (identical protocol), better in-support, worse beyond depth 11.
quote: The adapter matched the full block overall (83.8% versus 84.0%), led through depth 11, and trailed beyond.

title: Retrofitting Recurrent Depth into a Pretrained Language Model: Installation, Extrapolation, Transfer, and Retention at Two Parameter Budgets
claim: The recurrent retrofit beats a same-size scratchpad CoT SFT model overall and especially beyond its horizon, and is faster at batch 1; but training lineage, tokens and inference compute are not matched (system comparison).
quote: The recurrent model won overall, 84% versus 72%, retained 53% versus 2.5% beyond depth 10, and answered 7.6 times faster in fewer output tokens.

title: Retrofitting Recurrent Depth into a Pretrained Language Model: Installation, Extrapolation, Transfer, and Retention at Two Parameter Budgets
claim: Differential learning rates for new retrofit parameters must be implemented as separate tensors in their own optimizer group; gradient-slice scaling silently fails under AdamW and Muon.
quote: when retrofitting a recurrent bridge into a pretrained transformer, any parameter that needs its own learning rate must be a separate tensor in its own optimizer group.

title: LoopUS: Recasting Pretrained LLMs into Looped Latent Refinement Models
claim: LoopUS-adapted checkpoints improve average zero-shot accuracy over the original backbones by +1.6 to +2.2 points (1.7B-14B), mostly on ARC-C/OBQA; MMLU/HellaSwag flat.
quote: yields consistent gains across models, reducing WikiText and LAMBADA perplexities and improving average downstream accuracy by +1.6 to +2.2 points, with the clearest gains on ARC-C and OBQA.

title: LoopUS: Recasting Pretrained LLMs into Looped Latent Refinement Models
claim: On TinyLlama, LoopUS reports a larger gain (+6.3) with 3B tokens than McLeish et al. (-2.9 at 52B) and Bae et al. (+3.5 at 60B), but numbers are copied from the respective papers and the authors call it non-controlled.
quote: Since prior results are drawn from the corresponding papers, we treat this comparison as an adaptation-efficiency reference rather than a fully controlled head-to-head benchmark.

title: LoopUS: Recasting Pretrained LLMs into Looped Latent Refinement Models
claim: Random deep supervision with per-step detachment beats truncated BPTT: TBPTT costs more and plateaus at higher LM loss; removing the selective gate also gives higher loss.
quote: TBPTT [59] incurs higher computational cost while plateauing at a substantially higher LLM than the standard LoopUS training recipe, indicating lower efficiency and worse performance in this setting.

title: LoopUS: Recasting Pretrained LLMs into Looped Latent Refinement Models
claim: The gated loop extrapolates stably to far more loops than trained (no divergence up to 100 iterations), with gains saturating after a few iterations.
quote: This stability extends well beyond the training regime: the checkpoint continues to behave robustly even at unseen recursion depths such as 40, 80, and 100.

title: Penelope: Localized Latent Recurrence for Efficient Structured Reasoning
claim: Under matched source checkpoint, data and optimizer-update count, Penelope is within about 0.5 point of Coconut on Deep ListOps while cutting latency; parameter counts and training FLOPs are not matched (75.35M vs 11.28M trainable).
quote: Under matched optimizer-update and data-exposure budgets, Penelope reaches 52.25 ± 0.72% EM, within 0.54 point of Coconut, while exceeding Visible CoT and CODI by 0.98 and 1.08 points, respectively.

title: Penelope: Localized Latent Recurrence for Efficient Structured Reasoning
claim: Which layers are looped barely matters: early, middle and output-side 5-layer intervals are within 0.19 point; full-decoder recurrence is only 0.27 point better at 2.51x the layer calls.
quote: Early, middle, and output-side recurrence lie within 0.19 point, while full-decoder recurrence is only 0.27 point above the outputside interval despite 2.51× more sequential decoder-layer applications.

title: Penelope: Localized Latent Recurrence for Efficient Structured Reasoning
claim: Recurrence contributes only a small gain over the same checkpoint run with K=0 (boundary only).
quote: K = 0 obtains 51.56 ± 0.81% pooled test EM, whereas independently validation-selected depths obtain 52.25 ± 0.72%.

title: SCOUT: Teaching Pre-trained Language Models to Enhance Reasoning via Flow Chain-of-Thought
claim: SCOUT gives monotonic per-iteration gains over SFT on the same data (+0.23, +1.05, +1.81 average), the best among recursive variants; gains are small and no variance is reported.
quote: SCOUT outperforms all baselines, with monotonic improvement across iterations (+0.23 → +1.05 → +1.81), and highest final performance (e.g., 35.5 on GSM8K, 52.4 on GLUE).

title: SCOUT: Teaching Pre-trained Language Models to Enhance Reasoning via Flow Chain-of-Thought
claim: Uniform per-loop supervision (same hard labels or same 7B teacher at every iteration) stagnates or regresses with more iterations; reversing teacher order collapses at iteration 3.
quote: R-SCOUT, which reverses teacher order (7B → 3B → 1.5B), initially achieves strong results (+1.47) but collapses in later steps (–0.42), confirming the necessity of aligning teacher strength with iteration depth.

title: SCOUT: Teaching Pre-trained Language Models to Enhance Reasoning via Flow Chain-of-Thought
claim: Naive state-integration choices (init injection, additive, concat-project, gate, AdaLN modulation) degrade with more iterations when retrofitting; only cross-attention stays flat.
quote: Naive fusion strategies such as Init, Add, and CatProj show diminishing returns with deeper iterations, suggesting limited support for long-horizon reasoning.

title: LayerNorm as Implicit Gain Control in Looped Transformers
claim: The relevant stability budget of a pre-LN looped block is the spectral margin of the recurrence Jacobian, not an operator-norm bound, because LayerNorm makes the Jacobian non-normal.
quote: it renders the recurrence Jacobian non-normal—asymptotically contractive at every verified fixed point even where its operator norm exceeds 1—so the true stability budget is the spectral margin, not an operator-norm bound.

title: LayerNorm as Implicit Gain Control in Looped Transformers
claim: A diagonal carry constraint rho < 1 (Parcae) is necessary but does not certify convergence of the full nonlinear recurrence; some initializations never reach a fixed point.
quote: so the diagonal carry constraint is necessary but not sufficient for convergence of the full recurrence.

title: LayerNorm as Implicit Gain Control in Looped Transformers
claim: Without the carry constraint, gradient descent drives the carry above 1 at higher learning rates and the hidden state explodes; the coda LayerNorm keeps loss finite so loss curves can hide the failure.
quote: the loss stays finite even while the state explodes, because the Coda’s LayerNorm normalizes hT before the unembed—loss curves alone can hide this failure mode.

title: LayerNorm as Implicit Gain Control in Looped Transformers
claim: Small activations are the dangerous regime: activation implosion raises the block Lipschitz constant and leads to divergence, a failure mode distinct from residual explosion.
quote: This predicts a failure mode distinct from residual explosion: activation implosion followed by divergence.

title: LayerNorm as Implicit Gain Control in Looped Transformers
claim: On cross-channel tasks gradient descent stores depth-memory in the nonlinear block and leaves the constrained carry at rest; the carry is recruited only on axis-aligned per-channel tasks.
quote: gradient descent routes memory through the block’s more expressive nonlinear recurrence and leaves the stability-constrained carry at rest—the carry’s role is stabilization, not memory.

title: Simply Stabilizing the Loop via Fully Looped Transformer
claim: Looped-LM training instability at high loop counts has two components: early gradient oscillation and residual-state explosion; per-layer RMSNorm alone does not prevent the explosion.
quote: Although all of our models already incorporate RMSNorm [Zhang and Sennrich, 2019] in each layer to regulate the output residual states, residual explosion still occurs.

title: Simply Stabilizing the Loop via Fully Looped Transformer
claim: FLT trains stably to 12 loops while other looped baselines collapse.
quote: enabling the Fully Looped Transformer to be trained stably up to 12 loop iterations, whereas other baseline looped models collapse in this regime.

title: Simply Stabilizing the Loop via Fully Looped Transformer
claim: At base size vanilla LT gets worse with more loops and collapses at 9, whereas FLT improves monotonically with loops; but at small size input-injection LT is best, so the gain is scale-dependent.
quote: The original LT drops from 40.52 to 36.56 between 3 and 6 loops and collapses at 9 loops, while LTi and LTai show only fluctuating or saturated gains.

title: Simply Stabilizing the Loop via Fully Looped Transformer
claim: Fully looped connectivity with plain residual fusion only attenuates residual explosion; attention-based injection is needed for stable training.
quote: This indicates that FLA attenuates residual amplification, but is not sufficient by itself to guarantee stable training.

title: Simply Stabilizing the Loop via Fully Looped Transformer
claim: Models trained with fixed loops benefit from more test-time loops only within the training range; beyond it performance fluctuates.
quote: When the loop count at inference exceeds the maximum used during pretraining, performance begins to fluctuate, indicating that the model struggles to adapt to excessive computational resources.

title: On the Residual Scaling of Looped Transformers: Stability and Transferability
claim: Standard 1/sqrt(depth) residual scaling fails for looped networks because shared weights make residual updates correlated; 1/N scaling is required to keep the residual stream bounded.
quote: We show that this is insufficient for looped architectures: weight sharing makes residual updates correlated across iterations, requiring the stronger scaling ε = 1/N .

title: On the Residual Scaling of Looped Transformers: Stability and Transferability
claim: With 1/N scaling the optimal learning rate depends only on unique depth L, not loop count N, so LR tuned at N = 1 transfers to larger N.
quote: A key consequence is that the optimal learning rate depends only on the number of unique layers L, not on the loop count N , enabling direct hyperparameter transfer from small to large N without retuning.

title: On the Residual Scaling of Looped Transformers: Stability and Transferability
claim: Linear residual scaling gives lower loss than sqrt scaling at 8 loops.
quote: at N = 8, linear scaling achieves a lower minimum loss than sqrt scaling (a reduction of 0.025 nats), indicating better trainability at larger loop counts.

title: On the Residual Scaling of Looped Transformers: Stability and Transferability
claim: Loop-step increments remain positively correlated after full training, so the mechanism persists beyond initialization.
quote: the pairwise cosine similarities between loop-step increments decrease after full training, but the correlation matrix remains positive for most loop-step pairs across all three depths

title: Stability and Generalization in Looped Transformers
claim: Looped networks without input recall have countable fixed points and cannot achieve strong input-dependence; recall plus outer normalization yields reachable, locally smooth fixed points with stable backpropagation.
quote: prove that looped networks without recall have countable fixed points and cannot achieve strong inputdependence at any spectral regime, while recall combined with outer normalization reliably produces a regime in which fixed points are simultaneously reachable

title: Stability and Generalization in Looped Transformers
claim: For autonomous networks no Jacobian spectral regime gives a useful training signal: contractive vanishes the input-gradient, expansive fails reachability, critical explodes parameter gradients.
quote: We find that no regime provides useful training signal: ρ(J) < 1 causes the input-gradient to vanish exponentially, ρ(J) > 1 fails reachability, and ρ(J) = 1 induces exploding parameter gradients.

title: Stability and Generalization in Looped Transformers
claim: Outer normalization on recall models improves hard (OOD) accuracy over the best unnormalized recall model.
quote: The best normalized model performs 12 and 2 percentage points better on hard data than the best un-normalized model on sudoku and chess, respectively

title: Stability and Generalization in Looped Transformers
claim: Recall looped models (about 1M params) beat fixed-depth 15-layer models with an order of magnitude more parameters on sudoku and prefix sums and match them on chess.
quote: If they were, fixed-depth models – which have an order of magnitude more parameters – would dominate across tasks, yet they are outperformed by recall variants on sudoku and prefix-sums, and only match them on chess

title: Stabilizing Recurrent Dynamics for Test-Time Scalable Latent Reasoning in Looped Language Models
claim: Normalization placement, not the normalizer type, determines looped dynamics; pre-norm lets the hidden-state norm grow without bound beyond the training horizon while post-norm stays bounded but ineffective.
quote: Without a constraint mechanism after the residual addition, the norm of the hidden state tends to grow without bound.

title: Stabilizing Recurrent Dynamics for Test-Time Scalable Latent Reasoning in Looped Language Models
claim: Prelude/coda layers (Huginn-style) do not change the stability tendencies of the recurrence.
quote: Finding 3: The inclusion of Prelude and Coda layers does not alter the system’s dynamical tendencies.

title: Stabilizing Recurrent Dynamics for Test-Time Scalable Latent Reasoning in Looped Language Models
claim: Random loop sampling improves performance retention beyond the training loop count but does not fix effective stability and is sensitive to the sampling range; L2 regularization between consecutive states adds almost nothing.
quote: Finding 4: Overall, sampling loop counts during training significantly enhances performance retention and generalization capabilities. However, it does not fundamentally transform the effective stability of the system and is sensitive to the size of the sampling range.

title: Stabilizing Recurrent Dynamics for Test-Time Scalable Latent Reasoning in Looped Language Models
claim: STARS fine-tuning of Ouro-1.4B reduces accuracy collapse when running more loops than trained and improves the peak over SFT on the same data.
quote: on GSM8K, while Ouro-1.4B experiences a 20.47% drop from its peak performance after 8 recurrent steps, our method degrades by only 8.26%.

title: LoopMTP: A looped transformer guided by latent multi-token prediction
claim: LoopMTP beats a parameter-matched non-looped model trained on the same 6.8B tokens on nearly every benchmark; it costs 2.49-7.05x the FLOPs, so the comparison is iso-param/iso-data, not iso-FLOP.
quote: Despite being slightly smaller, L OOP MTP outperforms the non-looped baseline on nearly every benchmark: not only on reasoning-based tasks, but also on perplexity, general tasks, and QA suites.

title: LoopMTP: A looped transformer guided by latent multi-token prediction
claim: Without the latent MTP auxiliary loss, math BPB degrades monotonically as loop count grows; with it, performance improves with loops.
quote: The effect is most pronounced on math, where step-by-step reasoning is required: without MTP, increasing the loop count causes performance to degrade monotonically.

title: LoopMTP: A looped transformer guided by latent multi-token prediction
claim: Residual scaling by running depth (1/((t-1)L+l)) shrinks later-iteration updates so much that their gradient contribution vanishes; a fixed 1/T factor is used instead.
quote: yields tiny factors for later iterations of deep unrollings, which we found empirically neutralizes their gradient contribution.

title: LoopMTP: A looped transformer guided by latent multi-token prediction
claim: LoopFormer training diverged from gradient explosion unless LR/WD/warmup were grid-searched per loop count, whereas LoopMTP trains stably with one fixed configuration.
quote: LoopFormer's grid search targets training stability: without the right combination training diverges due to gradient explosion.

title: DeepLoop: Depth Scaling for Looped Transformers
claim: At matched loop count, params, data and compute, DeepLoop's residual parameterization is neutral at R=1 and beats the pre-LN looped baseline in validation loss at every R>=3 at both scales (single seed).
quote: DeepLoop is effectively tied with the baseline at R=1 and improves over it in these single-seed runs at R=3, R=5, and R=7 at both scales.

title: DeepLoop: Depth Scaling for Looped Transformers
claim: Weight tying changes residual scaling: the conservative aligned regime needs exponent p=1/2 rather than DeepNorm's 1/4 as loop count grows at fixed physical depth.
quote: The bound recovers the DeepNorm exponent when visits decorrelate, but in the conservative aligned regime it requires the exponent to increase from 1/4 to 1/2 as loop count grows at fixed physical depth.

title: DeepLoop: Depth Scaling for Looped Transformers
claim: Empirical p-sweep at R=3: training escape from the unigram floor is unreliable through p=0.50 and universal only from p=0.55; smaller p gives lower loss when it trains.
quote: escape is the minority outcome in the clearly sub-threshold region p ≤ 0.40, remains unreliable through p = 0.50, and becomes universal from p = 0.55.

title: DeepLoop: Depth Scaling for Looped Transformers
claim: Truncating gradients to the last outer cycle (HRM) puts the truncated module in the untied-DeepNorm regime; analysis counts only gradient-visible visits.
quote: The truncation thus places H in the untied-DeepNorm regime even though H is

title: Scheduling Recursive Reasoning in Looped Transformers
claim: Adaptive step-size control improves terminal accuracy of frozen recurrent models without retraining, while fixed rescaling is inconsistent.
quote: Table 1 shows that all six variants improve terminal accuracy and reach the unit-step baseline's terminal performance in less wall-clock time on both tasks.

title: Scheduling Recursive Reasoning in Looped Transformers
claim: On recurrent LMs (Ouro-1.4B, Huginn-0125) all TAPS variants improve average accuracy over unit steps; fixed rescaling can substantially degrade performance.
quote: all six TAPS variants improve average accuracy over unit-step inference on both models, although the gains vary across tasks. In contrast, fixed rescaling is sensitive to the chosen scale and can substantially degrade performance

title: Scheduling Recursive Reasoning in Looped Transformers
claim: A training-time penalty on fluctuation exceeding progress (co-design SFT) reduces late-stage loss variability and improves held-out accuracy at matched training loss.
quote: Co-design leaves the final training loss largely unchanged, but reduces its late-stage variability by 10.3%. At matched training loss, it lowers held-out terminal loss by 5.9%

title: Loop Dropout: Regularizing Shared Updates in Looped Language Models
claim: With all four loops active, a standard shared LoRA update is much more effective at later loop positions than earlier ones.
quote: For Ouro-1.4B fine-tuned on GSM8K with standard LoRA, loss reduction falls from 32% when the update is applied at the fourth loop to 12% when applied at the first, relative to the same frozen model.

title: Loop Dropout: Regularizing Shared Updates in Looped Language Models
claim: Randomly omitting adapter applications alone does not help, because it shrinks the expected training update relative to inference; inverse-survival rescaling is required.
quote: Randomly omitting adapter applications alone, however, does not improve task performance; it reduces expected update strength during training while leaving inference unchanged.

title: Loop Dropout: Regularizing Shared Updates in Looped Language Models
claim: Loop Dropout improves math fine-tuning at both Ouro sizes versus LoRA under matched examples, steps and LR-search budget.
quote: On Ouro-1.4B, GSM8K accuracy increases by 1.19 percentage points over LoRA, while MATH-500 rises from 38.87% to 47.53%, an 8.67-point gain. On Ouro-2.6B, the corresponding gains are 1.11 and 4.33 points.

title: Loop Dropout: Regularizing Shared Updates in Looped Language Models
claim: Adapters trained at 4 loops transfer better to deeper recurrence with Loop Dropout; advantage grows with evaluation depth.
quote: For adapters trained at four loops, Loop Dropout exceeds LoRA by 2.98 and 4.75 percentage points on GSM8K when evaluated at six and eight loops, respectively.

title: Dense Supervision Is Not Enough: The Readout Blind Spot in Looped Language Models
claim: Per-loop CE through RMSNorm readouts still lets final hidden-state norms drift into the tens of thousands in loops without inter-loop normalization; scale-visible readouts and norm penalties keep norms in the tens.
quote: The key negative result is per-loop + RMSNorm: it receives a CE loss at every loop, yet reaches final-loop norms of 39,207 at 44M and 56,051 at 129M. Raw readouts keep norms in the tens under both terminal-only and per-loop CE.

title: Dense Supervision Is Not Enough: The Readout Blind Spot in Looped Language Models
claim: Dense supervision trains exits; scale control needs a scale-visible loss or removing scale from the loop (inter-loop normalization).
quote: The resulting design rule is simple: dense supervision trains exits; recurrent scale control requires either making scale visible to a loss or removing it from the loop.

title: Dense Supervision Is Not Enough: The Readout Blind Spot in Looped Language Models
claim: Norm drift costs depth use: RMSNorm per-loop models become nearly K-invariant (additional loops barely change the normalized state), whereas scale-controlled variants improve with more loops and achieve lower PPL at matched K/throughput.
quote: with final-loop norms in the tens of thousands, angular updates shrink like 1/sk , so additional loops barely change the normalized state the readout sees.

title: Dense Supervision Is Not Enough: The Readout Blind Spot in Looped Language Models
claim: At 1.4B Ouro-scale with inter-loop RMSNorm, both checkpoints are essentially K-invariant after ~1.3B tokens, consistent with inter-loop norm bounding scale.
quote: Both checkpoints are essentially K-invariant on this slice (CE varies by less than 0.01 nats across K=2,3,4), which is consistent with Ouro's inter-loop RMSNorm bounding in-loop scale

title: What Makes Looped Transformers Perform Better Than Non-Recursive Ones
claim: Looped attention follows a simple-to-complex two-phase curriculum while the single-pass model stalls after simple patterns, attributed to a V-shaped-valley landscape bias.
quote: we conjecture that the recursive architecture of Looped-Attn induces a landscape-level inductive bias towards River-V-Valley.

title: What Makes Looped Transformers Perform Better Than Non-Recursive Ones
claim: A non-recursive 3-layer model (Deep-Attn) shows the same static Hessian spectrum as single-pass, so the effect is attributed to recursion, not depth alone.
quote: We find that the spectral shape and evolution of Single-Attn (Figure 8) and Deep-Attn (Figure 10∼12) are nearly identical.

title: What Makes Looped Transformers Perform Better Than Non-Recursive Ones
claim: SHIFT (single-pass first, then looped) reaches comparable final performance to pure looped training with less training time; the switch point matters (too early suboptimal, too late fails to converge).
quote: SCP selects a shift point between 100 and 150 epochs. This achieves a training speedup of approximately 1.26× without compromising final performance

title: LoopRPT: Reinforcement Pre-Training for Looped Language Models
claim: Per-loop RL on the latent steps improves hard-token next-token-reasoning accuracy while cutting average loops versus the same Ouro checkpoint without LoopRPT.
quote: On Ouro-2.6B, LoopRPT boosts Hard Peak accuracy by +3.58 while reducing average steps from 3.51 to 2.28.

title: LoopRPT: Reinforcement Pre-Training for Looped Language Models
claim: Standard output-token RLVR is mismatched to looped models because Ouro's dynamic early exit causes instability and credit-assignment problems; LoopRPT moves reward to latent steps.
quote: the dynamic early-exit mechanism—which adaptively determines computation depth—introduces instability and credit assignment issues for standard RLVR alignment.

title: LoopRPT: Reinforcement Pre-Training for Looped Language Models
claim: Downstream gains over Ouro are small on general tasks and largest on math/code (e.g. GSM8K 81.76 to 85.36 at 2.6B); comparisons to Qwen/Gemma/Llama use numbers copied from the Ouro paper.
quote: At the 2.6B scale, GSM8K accuracy increases from 81.76 to 85.36, alongside improvements in HumanEval+

title: LoopRPT: Reinforcement Pre-Training for Looped Language Models
claim: Forcing more loops does not monotonically help: forced-depth accuracy can drop for medium and hard tokens, because later loops are not trained to refine monotonically.
quote: forced-depth accuracy is not guaranteed to improve monotonically as depth increases, and may even degrade for Medium and Hard buckets.

title: LoopRPT: Reinforcement Pre-Training for Looped Language Models
claim: Ablation: removing the representation loss plus exit-entropy bonus hurts most; removing Gaussian latent noise or PG+KL also raises average exit steps.
quote: Removing Lrep + Lent yields the largest degradation in both accuracy and efficiency, underscoring that representation regularization and entropy shaping are vital for learning effective latent transitions.

title: Prioritize the Process, Not Just the Outcome: Rewarding Latent Thought Trajectories Improves Reasoning in Looped Language Models
claim: Spreading reward over the latent trajectory beats terminal-loop GRPO on hard math, with matched base checkpoint, data, steps and rollouts.
quote: RLTT yields statistically significant improvements over GRPO on challenging mathematical reasoning benchmarks, improving mean accuracy over MATH500, AIME24/26, and BeyondAIME by +5.8% on the 1.4B scale, and +10.9% on the 2.6B scale.

title: Prioritize the Process, Not Just the Outcome: Rewarding Latent Thought Trajectories Improves Reasoning in Looped Language Models
claim: The authors attribute earlier failures of RLVR on LoopLMs to terminal-only credit assignment: GRPO rewards only the last latent state.
quote: standard policy-gradient objectives such as GRPO only reward the last latent state before token emission, implicitly assuming a single-step decision process.

title: Prioritize the Process, Not Just the Outcome: Rewarding Latent Thought Trajectories Improves Reasoning in Looped Language Models
claim: The gain is not sensitive to the per-loop weighting scheme (uniform, progressive, exit-probability), so exposing all loops to the reward matters more than the schedule.
quote: RLTT’s performance is largely insensitive to the precise loop-weighting strategy used to distribute credit

title: Prioritize the Process, Not Just the Outcome: Rewarding Latent Thought Trajectories Improves Reasoning in Looped Language Models
claim: RLTT's extra cost is memory, which grows linearly with loop count; tokens packed per GPU had to be halved compared with GRPO.
quote: The practical overhead is instead memory, which scales linearly with the number of loops because RLTT must retain per-loop log-probabilities to form the trajectoryweighted objective.

title: Prioritize the Process, Not Just the Outcome: Rewarding Latent Thought Trajectories Improves Reasoning in Looped Language Models
claim: RL-tuned Ouro beats Qwen3 + GRPO trained on the same MATH data, but the base models were pretrained differently, so this comparison is unmatched.
quote: Ouro1.4B+RLTT reaches 46.0% mean benchmark accuracy, outperforming both Qwen3-1.7B+GRPO (27.2%) and Qwen34B+GRPO (31.7%), while Ouro-2.6B+RLTT further improves to 51.2%

title: Latent Thinking Optimization: Your Latent Reasoning Language Model Secretly Encodes Reward Signals in Its Latent Thoughts
claim: A lightweight classifier on Huginn's recurrent latent trajectory predicts answer correctness well (near-perfect on SVAMP, about 0.8 ROC-AUC on MBPP).
quote: On SVAMP, it achieves an ROC-AUC score close to 1.0, while on MBPP it achieves an ROC-AUC score of around 0.8.

title: Latent Thinking Optimization: Your Latent Reasoning Language Model Secretly Encodes Reward Signals in Its Latent Thoughts
claim: At equal sampling budget (N=20), LRM-guided selection of latent trajectories beats majority voting and text-space self-correction on Huginn-3.5B on all five datasets.
quote: Across all datasets, LTO consistently outperforms both the base model and the best baseline for thinking correction.

title: Latent Thinking Optimization: Your Latent Reasoning Language Model Secretly Encodes Reward Signals in Its Latent Thoughts
claim: With more recurrence steps (16 to 32), LTO's gain shrinks because random-init trajectories become less diverse, leaving fewer problems with mixed correct and incorrect samples.
quote: This is attributed to the reduced diversity in the sampled latent thoughts and answers when longer thinking steps are used.

title: Latent Thinking Optimization: Your Latent Reasoning Language Model Secretly Encodes Reward Signals in Its Latent Thoughts
claim: LTO only resamples and does not change the policy, so it cannot help when every sampled latent trajectory is wrong; the authors suggest moving the LRM signal into RL or preference optimization.
quote: LTO cannot improve the latent thinking processes, since every generated latent thinking trajectory remains incorrect.

title: Energy-Entropy Regularization: The True Power of Minimal Looped Transformers
claim: The energy-entropy regularized d=8 looped model length-generalizes to L=1000 and beats a much larger looped baseline; the baseline differs in size, heads, steps, learning rate and loss, and there is no same-model cross-entropy-only ablation.
quote: The EER framework achieves successful length generalization up to L = 1000, significantly outperforming the baseline despite having less than 0.02% of its parameter count

title: Energy-Entropy Regularization: The True Power of Minimal Looped Transformers

title: Closing the Loop: Practical Training Recipes for Looped Language Models

quote: At equal parameter count, four-step LoopLM outperforms dense-ouro-1.4B on all 12 benchmarks.

title: Closing the Loop: Practical Training Recipes for Looped Language Models
claim: At matched inference compute (3 loops vs a 72-layer dense twin on the same data), the dense model is ahead or level on every benchmark; the looped model's advantage is parameter count.
quote: At equal inference compute the larger dense model is ahead or level on every benchmark, and the advantage of LoopLM at this point is its size.

title: Closing the Loop: Practical Training Recipes for Looped Language Models
claim: Without Ouro's staged schedule the exit gate collapses to exit-after-loop-1; LR warmup prevents the early collapse and a larger KL/entropy coefficient beta lets the gate recover; LM loss does not reveal the collapse.
quote: Thus, warmup prevents early collapse at our β, while larger β enables recovery if collapse occurs

title: Closing the Loop: Practical Training Recipes for Looped Language Models
claim: Normalization placement around the shared block matters: post-norm and sandwich-norm fail to train because gradients vanish through the block; a final norm before the LM head removes loss spikes.
quote: Post-norm and sandwich-norm fail because gradients vanish through almost the entire decoder block, and this failure persists across warmup lengths, batch sizes, and normalization parameterizations.

title: Closing the Loop: Practical Training Recipes for Looped Language Models
claim: Naively looping a pretrained decoder degrades later steps; one learned embedding-mixing scalar plus a smoothed exit loss yields refinement, and per-step LoRA adds little.
quote: We show that looping the pretrained decoder as it is degrades the representation, that one learned scalar stops this degradation and that adapters are optional.

title: Closing the Loop: Practical Training Recipes for Looped Language Models
claim: RL (RLTT) on the LoopLM helps only when rollout solve rate gives mixed-success groups and the LR is large enough to move the policy.
quote: What separates the two runs is the solve rate at rollout time.

title: Closing the Loop: Practical Training Recipes for Looped Language Models

quote: Thus, we could not reproduce the gains reported in the original work under our data and training setup.

title: Teaching Pretrained Language Models to Think Deeper with Retrofitted Recurrence
claim: Initializing the recurrent model from pretrained layers is far more efficient than random initialization (same architecture, same data).
quote: We show that initializing parameters of recurrent models from those of a pretrained fixed depth model is significantly more efficient than using a random initialization (Figure 2).

title: Teaching Pretrained Language Models to Think Deeper with Retrofitted Recurrence
claim: A curriculum that slowly raises the mean recurrence keeps loss while reducing training cost; scheduling the max backprop depth instead is FLOP-efficient but worse per step.
quote: We propose a curriculum over recurrent depths, slowly increasing the average number of recurrent iterations during training to maintain performance while improving training speed (Figure 3).

title: Teaching Pretrained Language Models to Think Deeper with Retrofitted Recurrence
claim: At equal training FLOPs on the same data order, retrofitted recurrent models with fewer unique parameters beat the non-recurrent parent on GSM8K/MATH, and keep improving where the parent plateaus.
quote: In all cases, under the same training FLOP budget, depth-recurrent models with fewer parameters can achieve higher accuracy on math problems than the non-recurrent parent model.

title: Teaching Pretrained Language Models to Think Deeper with Retrofitted Recurrence
claim: Muon is more stable than AdamW (including Huginn's AdamW variant) for recurrent training; AdamW loss spikes to NaN.
quote: Muon is the most stable and achieves the lowest loss for recurrent models. Note, the AdamW line ends early as the loss spikes and becomes NaN.

title: Teaching Pretrained Language Models to Think Deeper with Retrofitted Recurrence
claim: Which layers to keep: early layers as prelude and later layers as recurrent block and coda, dropping middle layers; this beats ShortGPT-selected layers.
quote: We find taking early layers for the prelude, and later layers for the recurrent block and coda to be best.

title: Teaching Pretrained Language Models to Think Deeper with Retrofitted Recurrence
claim: A healing phase on web text before high-quality data recovers general LM ability lost to surgery.

title: CHERRY: Compressed Hierarchical Experts with Recurrent Representational Yield
claim: A 6-layer block unrolled 8 times matches the loss of a 24-layer block unrolled twice at 2.5x fewer parameters; note both are compressed looped variants, and the uncompressed 48-layer original is much better.
quote: 6L×8 (227M, loss 2.934) ≈ 24L×2 (566M, loss 2.926). Parameter reduction: 2.5× at identical performance.

title: CHERRY: Compressed Hierarchical Experts with Recurrent Representational Yield

quote: Applying recurrent loop unrolling to an untrained, freshly-merged model increases loss by 212–346%

title: ConceptMoE: Adaptive Token-to-Concept Compression for Implicit Compute Allocation
claim: In CT conversion at matched FLOPs and total parameters, looping 8 intermediate layers (plus 11 experts) gives large gains while adding experts alone (15) gives little; looping partly drives the gain.
quote: ConceptMoE-top15 achieves a modest 0.4 point improvement over MoE, while ConceptMoE-top11-loop8 shows substantial gains of 5.5 points overall, with particularly strong improvements in reasoning (+8.3), math (+12.2), and code (+6.4).

title: The Tell-Tale Norm: $\ell_2$ Magnitude as a Signal for Reasoning Dynamics in Large Language Models
claim: A single norm-triggered refinement loop of a frozen layer improves reasoning, but excessive loops degrade below the base model.
quote: A single refinement loop (Loop-1) already achieves significant gains over the base model (e.g., AIME24: 60.00 → 66.67), indicating that lightweight, one-step refinement suffices to capture the benefit.

title: The Tell-Tale Norm: $\ell_2$ Magnitude as a Signal for Reasoning Dynamics in Large Language Models
claim: Repeating one layer of a pretrained model makes the activation norm grow rapidly, so only a few loops are safe.
